`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# Working on this project

Notes for contributors and coding agents: how the project is laid out, how to build and test it, and
the rules that keep a test run from disturbing the machine it runs on.

## Layout

- `src/`: the hand-written part: the app and its hooks (`main.cpp`, `ng2_app.h`), the native
  renderer (`src/gpu/video.cpp`, `d3d_hooks.cpp`, shaders in `src/gpu/shaders/`), the menus
  (`recomp_settings.cpp`: RECOMP SETTINGS on the title menu and in the in-game menu, the title
  menu's entries; `gpu/menu_label.cpp`: the pictures of their labels and the Options header), the
  frame-rate counter (`perf_overlay.cpp`), movies on the host (`src/movie/`), the scripted
  controller for tests (`script_input.h`), mods (`mods.cpp`: game files replaced through the
  game's own loose-file loading; how it works is in its header comment).
- `generated/default/`: the recompiled game code, generated at build time from the player's
  `default.xex`. **Never commit it**, nor the game's data (`game_files/`, `*.iso`, `*.xex`, saves,
  captures of the game's pictures).
- `ng2_manifest.toml`, `ng2_codegen.toml`, `ng2_pointer_funcs.toml`: the ReXGlue project: manifest,
  codegen overrides (function boundaries, fibers, setjmp/longjmp), and functions only reached through
  pointers (`tools/find_pointer_funcs.py` on an image dumped with `NG2_DUMP_IMAGE`).
- `patches/`: changes to the ReXGlue SDK, XenosRecomp and plume (`git am` onto the pinned
  versions in `thirdparty/`, which aren't committed).
- `packaging/`: the AppImage (`appimage/build.sh`: the portable one, built in a container;
  `appimage/build-local.sh`: the native build, for this machine only), the Windows build
  (`windows/build.sh`) and their resources. Both packages carry the game built twice, x86-64-v2
  (`ng2`) and x86-64-v3 (`ng2-avx2`); `src/cpu_handover.cpp` starts the second where the CPU has
  AVX2 (`NG2_NO_AVX2=1` keeps the first). `portable.txt` next to the package keeps everything in
  `userdata/` beside it (`packaging/appimage/AppRun`, `src/windows_setup.cpp`).
- `docs/`: `renderer-plan.md` (the renderer, with what was measured), `menus.md` (the game's menus,
  reverse-engineered), `shaders.md`, the D3D function maps (`d3d-map-*.md`), `xenia-notes.md`.
  The game is Title Update 3 since 2026-11-03 (Title Update 2 from 2026-11-02); older notes use
  TU2 or 1.0 addresses, which `title-update.md` maps (`tools/map_addresses.py` made the maps).

## Building

See the README. After the first build, `cmake --build out/build/linux-amd64-release --target ng2`
rebuilds the app alone.

## Test runs

A test run must not disturb the machine it runs on: no window on the desktop, no sound, no input
devices, and none of the player's settings or saves.

- `tools/run-headless-windows.sh` does the same for the Windows build under Proton (umu-run).
- `tools/run-headless.sh <seconds> <out dir> [game options]` runs the game in a headless gamescope
  with its own HOME, settings (`<out dir>/ng2.toml`), user data and log (`<out dir>/ng2.log`, which
  rotates at 5 MB: read `ng2.1.log` first). `NG2_SHOTS="30 60"` takes screenshots at those seconds.
- `NG2_PAD_SCRIPT=30000:start,34000:a,...` plays a controller (`<ms>:<button>[:<hold ms>]`;
  buttons and sticks in `src/script_input.h`). From boot, `30000:start,34000:a,37000:a,40000:a,
  58000:a,63000:a,80000:a,262000:a,280000:a` reaches Chapter 1's first fight at about 280 s (TU3:
  the chapter card takes the press at 80 s); Back about 300 s opens the in-game menu.
- `tools/collect_pipelines.sh <out dir>` remakes the packaged pipeline seed
  (`packaging/ng2-pipelines-seed.bin`): headless runs through Chapter 1 and Mission Mode (missions
  1-12, fighting), their pipeline lists merged by `tools/merge_pipelines.py`. The game makes the
  seed's pipelines in the background at start (src/gpu/video.cpp, `MakeListedPipelines`), moved to
  the player's antialiasing. Remake it when shaders or the pipeline key change.
- `NG2_ROOM_JUMP=<from>:<to>` swaps a room in the story script (src/room_jump.cpp lists the rooms
  with cutscenes): with the New Game path above, `3:5` plays the cutscene before Chapter 2 at about
  80-110 s.
- The native renderer draws by default; to compare with Xenia's set `NG2_RENDERER=xenos` and add
  `--gpu_plugin=xenos --headless` (Xenia's draws cutscenes black in this build).

## Environment

- `NG2_RENDERER=xenos`: the SDK's Xenia GPU emulation draws instead of the native renderer (dev
  builds only: the packages leave out the GPU plugin, `librexgpu-xenos`). The native renderer runs
  with no GPU emulation (src/gpu/native_gpu.cpp).
- `NG2_AUDIO=0`: no audio device; the game's audio still runs.
- `NG2_BARYCENTRIC=1` or `0`: cut-off parts' id interpolated in the shader, or by the hardware
  (default: in the shader on NVIDIA, where the GPU supports it).
- `NG2_CONFIG=<file>`: settings file instead of `<exe dir>/ng2.toml`.
- `NG2_PROFILE=1`: time per renderer stage, once a second, and every 5 s (Linux) the busiest threads' CPU
  time ("threads, ms of CPU each second"; "(renderer)" is the game's render thread, "Render
  Commands" ours). `NG2_HITCHES=1` (or `log_hitches`): slow frames with what they were spent on.
  `NG2_FPS_LOG=1`: the game's frame rate once a second.
- `NG2_PIPELINE_STATS=1`: what the driver compiled each shader pair to, logged once a pair (registers,
  scratch, instructions; VK_KHR_pipeline_executable_properties, plume patches 0011 and 0012: the driver feature is only enabled with it). On AMD the vertex
  stage is `ShaderProperties.gs`; `scratchMemUsageInBytes` above 0 there means spilled registers.
- `NG2_PRESENT_GAPS=1`: the time between real presents (on the thread that makes them) each second.
  Test switches for choppy play at a steady 60 (#36, #46): presents are held until 90% of a refresh
  after the last (V-Sync FIFO or Mailbox only; on by default since 0.5.58, `NG2_TEST_EVEN_PRESENT=0` turns it off); `NG2_TEST_GAMESCOPE_AUTO=1` lets
  Frame Pacing Auto work under gamescope, where it otherwise acts as Timer (experimental: if gamescope
  reports a frame shown when it arrives, the lock can follow its own presents). At 60 fps the game's own
  frame limiter (sub_822F0BF8) doesn't run (its interval word is 0): the presents pace the game.
- `NG2_LATENCY_LOG=1`: every 10 s, from the game reading the pad to that frame's present and to its
  reaching the screen (the display clock, VK_KHR_present_wait). `NG2_TEST_REFRESH=59` (run-headless.sh)
  sets the headless display's rate.
- `NG2_RENDER_THREAD=0`: Vulkan commands, submits and presents on the game's render thread again
  instead of the "Render Commands" thread (for comparisons).
- `--log_slow_reads=<ms>`: log game file reads that take at least that long (thread, size, file).
  `--async_file_reads=false`: reads the game asks to be asynchronous block its thread again.
  `--test_read_delay_us_per_mb=12000`: slow every read to about SD card speed, to measure loading
  hitches on a fast disk.
- `NG2_TRACE_FRAME=t<sec>+<count>`: log every draw of those frames.
- F7, or `NG2_TRACE_FILE=<file>` (starts when the file appears): every draw of the next
  `NG2_TRACE_FRAMES` (60) frames and a small picture every 10, in `~/ng2-trace-<n>` (`HOME` decides
  where).
- `NG2_DUMP_TEXTURES=<dir>`: write decoded textures (PGM/PAM/DDS).
- `NG2_DEBUG_HIGHLIGHT=<vs hash>|<hash>,<hash>...|cycle:<s>|all|rigid`: draw a vertex shader's
  draws in magenta (a list or all: a colour per shader, logged; rigid: the unskinned ones;
  `NG2_DEBUG_EXCLUDE=<hash>,...` leaves some out).
- `tools/xtr_draws.py <trace.xtr>`: draws, constants (`--consts`), registers (`--regs`) and
  buffers (`--dump`) of a Xenia Edge GPU trace, to compare a frame with ours.
- `NG2_DUMP_IMAGE=<file>`: write the loaded XEX image for analysis.
- `NG2_D3D_STATS=1`: D3D draw, clear, resolve and swap counts every second.
- `NG2_DRAW_STACKS=1`: each distinct chain of guest callers behind a draw, logged once (what draws
  a picture). `NG2_BUCKET_LOG=1`: each 2D render bucket's box per second and its draw methods
  (src/aspect.cpp).
- Mission Mode is a quick way to reach bosses headless (Mission 04, Ruler of Lightning). Quick
  menu: d-pad up, then up, left and A equips the bow.
- `NG2_MOVIES=xmedia`: the game's own movie player instead of FFmpeg; `NG2_MOVIE_TRACE=1` logs it.
- `NG2_PAD_LIVE=<file>`: presses each line appended to the file.

## Reverse engineering

Ghidra (headless) on the loaded image works well for this game: import the image raw at base
`0x82000000` as `PowerPC:BE:64:A2ALT-32addr`. The recompiled C++ in `generated/default/` carries each
instruction as a comment, which helps where Ghidra stops. What is known about the menus is in
`docs/menus.md`.

```

`CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
# ng2 - ReXGlue Recompiled Project
#
# SDK boilerplate lives in generated/rexglue.cmake.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(ng2 VERSION 0.5.58 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

include(generated/rexglue.cmake)

# Cross-compiled (Windows from Linux): the build-time tools are the host
# build's (NG2_HOST_BUILD_DIR, built first): the code generator, and the
# shader cache that build translated (the code and shaders don't depend on
# the target).
if(CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING)
    set(NG2_HOST_BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/out/build/linux-amd64-release" CACHE PATH
        "A native build of this tree, for its build-time tools and shader cache")
    set(NG2_HOST_REXGLUE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/install/linux-amd64/bin/rexglue"
        CACHE FILEPATH "The host's ReXGlue code generator")
    if(NOT EXISTS "${NG2_HOST_REXGLUE}")
        message(FATAL_ERROR "No ${NG2_HOST_REXGLUE}: build and install the native SDK first")
    endif()
    set_target_properties(rex::rexglue PROPERTIES
        IMPORTED_LOCATION "${NG2_HOST_REXGLUE}" IMPORTED_LOCATION_RELEASE "${NG2_HOST_REXGLUE}")
endif()

# Sources
set(NG2_SOURCES
    src/main.cpp
    src/gpu/video.cpp
    src/gpu/native_gpu.cpp
    src/gpu/menu_label.cpp
    src/gpu/prompts.cpp
    src/controls.cpp
    src/extras.cpp
    src/storage_prompt.cpp
    src/cpu_handover.cpp
    src/gpu/d3d_hooks.cpp
    src/perf_overlay.cpp
    src/recomp_settings.cpp
    src/movie/movie_hooks.cpp
    src/movie/host_movie.cpp
    src/debug_waits.cpp
    src/room_jump.cpp
    src/cheats.cpp
    src/frame_wait.cpp
    src/dlc.cpp
    src/mods.cpp
    src/stderr_log.cpp
    src/gameplay.cpp
    src/aspect.cpp
    src/windows_setup.cpp
)

if(WIN32)
    # The executable's icon.
    add_executable(ng2 WIN32 ${NG2_SOURCES} packaging/windows/ng2.rc packaging/windows/ng2.manifest)
else()
    add_executable(ng2 ${NG2_SOURCES})
endif()

# xenos (GPU emulation) is the reference renderer while the native one is built.
rexglue_setup_target(ng2 GPU_PLUGINS xenos)
target_compile_definitions(ng2 PRIVATE NG2_VERSION="${PROJECT_VERSION}")

# The SDK sets an $ORIGIN rpath on Linux but only stages its shared runtime
# libraries on Windows and macOS.
if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)
    foreach(_lib rex::runtime rex::TracyClient)
        if(TARGET ${_lib})
            add_custom_command(TARGET ng2 POST_BUILD
                COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different
                    $<TARGET_FILE:${_lib}> $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ng2>
                VERBATIM)
        endif()
    endforeach()
endif()

# Shaders, translated ahead of time like Unleashed Recompiled does: the
# shader containers sit in the XEX image, ng2_dump_image extracts that image
# from the user's default.xex and XenosRecomp (patched for NG2, see
# docs/shaders.md) turns every container into SPIR-V, embedded as a zstd
# compressed cache.
set(NG2_GAME_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/game_files" CACHE PATH
    "Extracted game files (default.xex is read at build time for its shaders)")
set(NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/thirdparty/XenosRecomp")

if(CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING)
    set(NG2_SHADER_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/shaders")
    set(NG2_SHADER_CACHE "${NG2_HOST_BUILD_DIR}/shaders/ng2_shader_cache.cpp")
    if(NOT EXISTS "${NG2_SHADER_CACHE}")
        message(FATAL_ERROR "No ${NG2_SHADER_CACHE}: build the native tree (NG2_HOST_BUILD_DIR) first")
    endif()
else()
    add_executable(ng2_dump_image tools/dump_image/main.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(ng2_dump_image PRIVATE rex::runtime)

    include(ExternalProject)
    ExternalProject_Add(xenos_recomp
        SOURCE_DIR "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}"
        BINARY_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/xenos_recomp"
        CMAKE_ARGS
            -G Ninja
            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
            -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}
            -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}
            -DXENOS_RECOMP_DXIL=OFF
        BUILD_BYPRODUCTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/xenos_recomp/XenosRecomp/XenosRecomp"
        INSTALL_COMMAND ""
        BUILD_ALWAYS ON)

    set(NG2_SHADER_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/shaders")
    set(NG2_SHADER_CACHE "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/ng2_shader_cache.cpp")
    add_custom_command(
        OUTPUT "${NG2_SHADER_CACHE}"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E make_directory "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/input"
        COMMAND ng2_dump_image "${NG2_GAME_DIR}" default.xex "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/input/default.img"
        COMMAND "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/xenos_recomp/XenosRecomp/XenosRecomp"
            "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/input" "${NG2_SHADER_CACHE}"
            "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}/XenosRecomp/shader_common.h"
        DEPENDS ng2_dump_image xenos_recomp "${NG2_GAME_DIR}/default.xex"
            "${NG2_GAME_DIR}/default.xexp"
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/xenos_recomp/XenosRecomp/XenosRecomp"
            "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}/XenosRecomp/shader_common.h"
        COMMENT "Translating NG2 shaders with XenosRecomp"
        VERBATIM)
endif()

add_library(ng2_shaders STATIC "${NG2_SHADER_CACHE}"
    "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}/thirdparty/smol-v/source/smolv.cpp")
target_include_directories(ng2_shaders PUBLIC src/gpu
    "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}/thirdparty/smol-v/source")
if(WIN32)
    # zstd from XenosRecomp's copy, built in; FFmpeg from a prebuilt shared
    # build (packaging/windows/build.sh fetches it into NG2_FFMPEG_DIR).
    set(ZSTD_BUILD_PROGRAMS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(ZSTD_BUILD_SHARED OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    set(ZSTD_BUILD_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    add_subdirectory(thirdparty/XenosRecomp/thirdparty/zstd/build/cmake zstd EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
    target_link_libraries(ng2_shaders PUBLIC libzstd_static)
    target_include_directories(ng2_shaders PUBLIC thirdparty/XenosRecomp/thirdparty/zstd/lib)
else()
    find_package(PkgConfig REQUIRED)
    pkg_check_modules(ZSTD REQUIRED IMPORTED_TARGET libzstd)
    target_link_libraries(ng2_shaders PUBLIC PkgConfig::ZSTD)
endif()
target_link_libraries(ng2 PRIVATE ng2_shaders)
if(WIN32)
    # The first-run setup (src/windows_setup.cpp): the title update's SHA-1.
    target_link_libraries(ng2 PRIVATE bcrypt)
endif()

# Movies decoded on the host (src/movie): the game's WMV3/VC-1 and WMA files.
if(WIN32)
    set(NG2_FFMPEG_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/out/windows-deps/ffmpeg" CACHE PATH
        "FFmpeg for Windows: include/, lib/*.lib, bin/*.dll")
    target_include_directories(ng2 PRIVATE "${NG2_FFMPEG_DIR}/include")
    foreach(_lib avformat avcodec avutil swresample swscale)
        target_link_libraries(ng2 PRIVATE "${NG2_FFMPEG_DIR}/lib/${_lib}.lib")
    endforeach()
else()
    pkg_check_modules(FFMPEG REQUIRED IMPORTED_TARGET
        libavformat libavcodec libavutil libswresample libswscale)
    target_link_libraries(ng2 PRIVATE PkgConfig::FFMPEG)
endif()

# Native renderer: plume (Unleashed Recompiled's RHI), Vulkan only, with the
# Wayland surface support from patches/plume.
add_subdirectory(thirdparty/plume EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
if(UNIX AND NOT APPLE)
    find_package(X11 REQUIRED)
    target_link_libraries(plume PUBLIC X11::X11)
endif()
target_link_libraries(ng2 PRIVATE plume)

# Internal shaders (present, copies), HLSL compiled to SPIR-V with the DXC
# that ships with XenosRecomp and embedded in the executable.
set(NG2_DXC_DIR "${NG2_XENOS_RECOMP_DIR}/thirdparty/dxc-bin")
set(NG2_INTERNAL_SHADERS
    "fullscreen_vs:vs_6_0"
    "present_ps:ps_6_0"
    "rect_list_gs:gs_6_0"
    "copy_ps:ps_6_0"
    "copy_7e3_ps:ps_6_0"
    "copy_7e3_ms_ps:ps_6_0"
    "scale_ps:ps_6_0"
    "depth_copy_ps:ps_6_0"
    "depth_copy_ms_ps:ps_6_0"
    "debug_ps:ps_6_0"
)
set(NG2_INTERNAL_SHADER_SOURCES "")
foreach(_entry ${NG2_INTERNAL_SHADERS})
    string(REPLACE ":" ";" _parts "${_entry}")
    list(GET _parts 0 _name)
    list(GET _parts 1 _profile)
    set(_hlsl "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/gpu/shaders/${_name}.hlsl")
    set(_spv "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/internal/${_name}.spv")
    set(_cpp "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/internal/${_name}.cpp")
    add_custom_command(
        OUTPUT "${_cpp}"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E make_directory "${NG2_SHADER_DIR}/internal"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env "LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${NG2_DXC_DIR}/lib/x64"
            "${NG2_DXC_DIR}/bin/x64/dxc-linux" -T ${_profile} -E main -spirv
            -fvk-use-dx-layout -HV 2021 -Qstrip_debug -Fo "${_spv}" "${_hlsl}"
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DINPUT=${_spv} -DOUTPUT=${_cpp} -DNAME=g_${_name}
            -P "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed_spirv.cmake"
        DEPENDS "${_hlsl}" "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/embed_spirv.cmake"
        COMMENT "Compiling ${_name}.hlsl"
        VERBATIM)
    list(APPEND NG2_INTERNAL_SHADER_SOURCES "${_cpp}")
endforeach()
target_sources(ng2_shaders PRIVATE ${NG2_INTERNAL_SHADER_SOURCES})

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing

Bug reports, test results, saves and code are all welcome. This page says what helps most.

Never attach or commit game files: disc images, `default.xex` or other files from the disc, the
generated code in `generated/default/`, or shaders and textures captured from the game.

## Reporting a bug

Check the [known issues](README.md#known-issues) first, then open an issue with the **Bug report**
template. Include:

- the version (or the commit, if you built it), your system (Linux distribution, Windows, or
  Proton), GPU and driver, and your RECOMP SETTINGS (render scale, anti-aliasing, V-Sync, Frame
  Pacing, Input Latency);
- where in the game it happens (chapter and place, or the menu) and what you did just before;
- a screenshot or a short video of a graphics glitch;
- for a **crash, freeze or a problem starting**: the log, `ng2.log` (where it is kept is in the
  [README](README.md#where-things-are-kept));
- for **stutter**: set `log_hitches = true` in the settings file, `ng2.toml` (same place), play the part that
  stutters, and attach the log;
- if it only happens in one place: a save from just before it.

To tell our bug from the game's own behaviour, compare with Xenia, or with footage of the Xbox 360 if
you can find it, and say what you saw there.

## Suggesting a feature

Open an issue and describe what you want and why. Changes that make the game look or play
differently from the Xbox 360 are added as options, off by default.

## Testing builds

Test builds are posted in issues. When you report back, include your GPU, driver, system and
settings, and what you tried: "fixed", "not fixed" and "different" are all useful. A screenshot of the
same spot before and after helps most.

## Code

Pull requests are welcome. A patch attached to an issue works too.

- Build from source as described in the [README](README.md#building-from-source).
  [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) has the project layout, the debugging tools, and the rules for test runs.
- Keep a pull request to one fix or feature, and say in it how you tested it (GPU, settings, where in
  the game).
- **Fixes** that make the port match the Xbox 360 can be on by default. Check them against Xenia.
- **Enhancements** that change the original look or behaviour go behind a setting, off by default.
- Changes to the SDK, XenosRecomp or plume go in `patches/` as `git format-patch` files; the
  checkouts in `thirdparty/` aren't committed. Don't edit `generated/`; it is regenerated from each
  person's disc.
- Commit messages start with the area when it helps (`Renderer:`, `Menus:`, `Audio:`, ...) and name
  the issue.

The project is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later, and contributions are accepted under the same license.
Contributors are credited in the release notes.

```

`README.md`:

```md
![Ninja Gaiden II Recompiled](docs/images/banner.jpg)

# Ninja Gaiden II Recompiled

**A PC port of Ninja Gaiden II by static recompilation.**

A native Linux and Windows version of *Ninja Gaiden II* (Xbox 360, 2008), made by statically
recompiling the game's own PowerPC code to run directly on a PC, not an emulator. It is built on the
[ReXGlue SDK](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) and draws with its own Vulkan renderer, which
takes over the game's Direct3D calls instead of emulating the Xbox 360 GPU. It plays at a steady
60 fps on modest hardware (the Steam Deck is the baseline) and adds PC options in the game's own
menus: higher render resolutions, widescreen and ultrawide, anti-aliasing, keyboard and mouse,
PlayStation and Nintendo button prompts, and more.

**You need your own copy of the game.** This project contains none of the game's data (graphics,
sound, movies, text): on first start it asks for your disc image, Games on Demand package or
extracted game, and installs it. It is made for the **World release** (title ID `544307D5`) with
**Title Update 3**, which it asks for too. The downloadable content (Mission Mode, the costume packs)
is supported and optional: it can be added on the first start or later.

## Features

- Native Linux (AppImage) and Windows (x64) builds; Steam Deck friendly
- Its own Vulkan renderer: render resolution up to 8x, anti-aliasing (MSAA up to 8x), anisotropic
  filtering, texture LOD bias, the game's bloom on, reduced or off
- 16:9, 16:10, 21:9, 32:9 and 4:3: the 3D fills the screen, the HUD goes to the screen's corners,
  the menus and movies keep their own frame
- Keyboard and mouse, with the keys' own pictures in the game's button prompts; Xbox,
  PlayStation and Nintendo prompts, following the controller in use
- Options from alicenotmech's Master Edition, in the port's own versions: skip the death screen,
  chapter cards that go on by themselves, a HUD that fades out when not fighting (or hidden),
  no post-effects, smoother HUD and menus, a sharper font
- Skip intro and skip any cutscene; cheats: infinite health and ninpo, unlock difficulties and
  costumes, all weapons and ninpo, all crystal skulls, max health and ninpo
- Low input latency and frame pacing on the display's own refreshes (options)
- Mods: game files replaced by files in a mods folder, nothing of the game's changed
- Render pipelines made in the background and remembered between sessions, so new areas don't
  stutter; the game's movies decoded on the PC (FFmpeg)
- **RECOMP SETTINGS** on the title menu and in the in-game menu; **EXIT GAME** on the title menu

## Performance

The Steam Deck is the baseline for optimization: changes are judged by whether it holds 60 fps in the
game's heaviest scenes.

Measured on a Steam Deck LCD in Game Mode, on battery, with sound, in Chapter 1's first fight
(29 seconds each, the Deck's own performance overlay's frame log), the port at the Deck's default
1x render scale and Xenia Edge at its defaults (November 2026 builds):

| | This port | Xenia Edge |
|---|---|---|
| Average fps | 60.0 | 55.4 |
| 1% low | 57.4 | 20.3 |
| 0.1% low | 55.5 | 17.9 |
| Slowest frame | 18 ms | 56 ms |
| Frames over 20 ms | 0 | 380 |
| CPU load | 26% | 50% |
| GPU load | 52% | 84% |
| Whole Deck's power draw | 10 W | 22 W |

The port holds 60 fps with no slow frame, while the emulator averages 55 fps and drops to 18. The
port draws less than half the power, so a charge lasts about twice as long.

## Shaders

The game's shaders are translated once, when the port is built, not while you play. All 663 of them
are in the game's executable: the build converts each into a Vulkan shader (SPIR-V) and packs them
into the program, so none is compiled at run time.

What a GPU still has to make is pipelines: a shader together with the draw settings it is used
with. This is the step that makes emulators stutter the first time an effect appears. Here:

- At start, the port makes the pipelines of a list recorded by playing through the game (333 of
  them), in the background as the game starts.
- A pipeline that wasn't on that list is made in the background when the game first needs it; the
  game doesn't wait, and the effect it belongs to can be missing for a frame or so
  (`async_pipelines = false` in `ng2.toml` waits instead). It is added to your own list
  (`ng2-pipelines.bin`) and made at every later start.
- The GPU driver keeps the finished pipelines in its own cache, so later starts are quicker than the
  first one after installing.

## Getting started

### What you need

These files, from your own console or discs. The first start asks for them in this order.

1. **The game**, World release (`544307D5`), in any one of these forms:
   - a disc image: `*.iso`
   - the Games on Demand package: the file in `544307D5/00007000` (named like
     `C1200E9B558D04454FA6`), with its `.data` folder next to it
   - an extracted copy: the folder with `default.xex` and the `.ng2` archives
2. **Title Update 3** (required): `TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4`, or the `default.xexp`
   taken from it. On a console it is in `Content/0000000000000000/544307D5/000B0000`. The port is
   built for this update and checks it; the Japanese release's Title Update 3 is refused.
3. **The DLC** (optional): the console's `544307D5/00000002` folder, with Mission Mode and the
   costume packs. It can also be added later, in the game folder's `dlc` folder.

And a 64-bit PC with SSE4.2 (any from about 2009 on) and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers.

The first start after installing takes longer to load: the render pipelines are made then and
kept, and later starts are quicker.

### Linux and Steam Deck

1. Download `NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage` from the releases page and make it executable
   (`chmod +x`, or Properties → Allow executing).
2. Run it. On the first start it asks whether to keep everything next to the AppImage (portable
   mode, below), then for your copy of the game, Title Update 3 and, if you have it, the DLC folder. A disc image or package is copied once into the data folder (below).
   More DLC can go in the game folder's `dlc` folder later; it is installed on the next start.
3. On a Steam Deck, add the AppImage to Steam (Add a Non-Steam Game) to play it in Game Mode, and
   choose 16:10 in RECOMP SETTINGS → Display.

Needs a 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (SteamOS, Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12, Fedora 36+),
and Python 3. The first-start windows use `kdialog` (SteamOS and KDE desktops), or `qarma` or
`zenity` where kdialog isn't installed (GNOME, Cinnamon, Xfce...). With none of them, start the
AppImage from a terminal and it asks there. An extracted copy of the game next to the AppImage
(`default.xex` beside it, or in a `game_files` or `game` folder there) is used without asking, as
is `NG2_GAME_DIR`; Title Update 3's `default.xexp` goes next to `default.xex` and DLC in its `dlc`
folder.

### Windows

1. Download `NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip` from the releases page and extract it anywhere.
2. Run `ng2.exe`. The first time it asks about portable mode (below), then for the game, Title Update 3 and the DLC as on Linux; a
   disc image or package is copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2\game`.

Needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit). The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are included.

Both packages carry the game twice, for any PC with SSE4.2 and for one with AVX2 (most PCs since
2013, the Steam Deck): the faster one is used where the CPU has it. `NG2_NO_AVX2=1` keeps the other.

### Where things are kept

| | Linux | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Copied game (from a disc image or package), saves, log (`ng2.log`) | `~/.local/share/ng2-recomp` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2` |
| Settings (`ng2.toml`), the chosen game folder, the pipeline list (`ng2-pipelines.bin`) | `~/.config/ng2-recomp` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2` |

**Portable mode:** with a file named `portable.txt` next to the AppImage (or `ng2.exe`), all of
these go into a `userdata` folder next to it instead. The first start offers it. The folder must
be writable (not inside Program Files). Delete `portable.txt` to go back.

`NG2_GAME_DIR=<folder>` starts with that game folder instead of the remembered one (Linux; on
Windows pass `--game_data_root=<folder>`).

## Settings

Everything is in the game's own menus: **RECOMP SETTINGS** on the title menu, and **Recomp
Settings** in the in-game menu (Back, under Save Method). Changes apply at once and are saved;
each defaults to the game's own behaviour.

- **Graphics**: Render Scale (1x–8x, with the resolution it draws at, as "2x 2240x1168");
  Anti-Aliasing (off, or 2x MSAA as on the console, 4x, 8x); Texture Filtering (the game's, or
  4x–16x anisotropic); Texture LOD Bias (the game's, 0 or -1: less shimmer at higher render
  scales); Bloom (on, reduced, off); Post-Effects (off: no blur, no white flashes)
- **Display**: Window Mode (windowed, borderless, fullscreen) and Window Size; Aspect Ratio (16:9,
  16:10, 21:9, 32:9, 4:3); V-Sync (Off, FIFO, Mailbox, Adaptive; a mode the driver lacks falls back
  to FIFO); Frame Pacing (Timer, the game's own 60 Hz clock, or Auto: the game's frames on the
  display's own refreshes, measured from the frames reaching the screen, so no frame is shown
  twice for the drift on a screen a little off 60 Hz, as 59.94; needs VK_KHR_present_wait, else it
  runs as Timer). Timer is the default: use it on a variable-refresh display, G-Sync or FreeSync.
  In the Steam Deck's Game Mode (and any game run through gamescope) Auto acts as Timer: there it
  gave me uneven frame pacing
- **Cheats**: Infinite Health; Infinite Ninpo (each cast's ninpo filled back); Unlock Costumes;
  All Weapons and Ninpo (Level 1 or 3: every melee and projectile weapon, ninpo and ammo, given at a
  new game, a load and a stage's start; what it gives stays in the save when it's turned off, as
  items found); All Crystal Skulls; Max HP and Ninpo (the life and ninpo upgrades full while it's
  on; the save keeps your own)
- **Interface**: HUD (shown, fading out when not fighting, hidden); Hi-Res Font (text drawn from
  glyphs twice the size, sharper above 720p; from the next start); Smooth HUD and Menus (the 2D
  always filtered); Show FPS; Button Prompts (Auto follows the device in use; Xbox, PlayStation,
  Nintendo, Keyboard); Mouse Sensitivity
- **Extras**: Skip Intro; Skip Cutscenes (any, watched or not); Skip Death Screen (straight to the
  game over menu); Auto Chapter Screen (chapter cards and mission briefings go on by themselves)
- **Gameplay**: Input Latency (Low: no finished frame waits for the screen; needs
  VK_KHR_present_wait; in the Steam Deck's Game Mode, and any game run through gamescope, it acts as
  Standard, as Low made frames come in pairs there); Unlock Difficulties (every path in New Game and Mission Mode, at once
  either way)

In the in-game menu, a page with six settings has no Restore Defaults row (the list has no room
for it); the title menu's has.

The game's own Options (camera, controller, sound, screen) are where they always were.

Some settings have no menu entry; they go in `ng2.toml`:

- `async_pipelines = false`: make render pipelines as they're needed instead of in the background
  (a new effect can stutter, but never appears a frame late)
- `log_hitches = true`: log every frame that takes over 25 ms with what the renderer spent it on
- `half_pixel_offset = false`: drop the console's half-pixel shift
- `frame_pacing_phase = 5`: where in a refresh Frame Pacing Auto starts a frame (% of it)

## Mods

Mods replace the game's files: models, motions, effects, stages, text, sounds. They go in a `mods`
folder in the data folder (`~/.local/share/ng2-recomp/mods`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2\mods`,
or `userdata/mods` in portable mode), one folder per mod:

    mods/
      Ryu's New Look/
        mod.toml
        files/
          char/ryu_b/ryu_b.gmd

A file in `files/` replaces the game's file with the same path (`files/char/ryu_b/ryu_b.gmd` is
Ryu's in-game model, `char\ryu_b\ryu_b.gmd`). The game loads it in place of the one in its
archives, so a mod never changes the game folder: delete the mod's folder and the game is as it
was. `mod.toml` is optional:

    name = "Ryu's New Look"
    version = "1.0"
    enabled = true          # false turns the mod off

    # One of the game's own files loaded in place of another (here his costume C model):
    [replace]
    'char/ryu_b/ryu_b.gmd' = 'char/ryu_c/ryu_c.gmd'

Mods are read at start, in their folders' name order: when two replace the same file, the first
one's is used. The log (`ng2.log`) lists each mod and the files it brings. To find which file to
replace, set `log_file_loads = true` in `ng2.toml`: the log then names every file the game loads.

## Controls

A controller works as on the Xbox 360; a PlayStation or Nintendo controller too, with its own
button prompts. The keyboard and mouse can be used at any time: the game follows whichever was
touched last, and its prompts change to match (or stay on one set: Button Prompts, in Interface).
The mouse moves the camera only while the keyboard and mouse are in use, and the pointer hides while
a controller is.

| Key | Action | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| W A S D | move | mouse | camera |
| left mouse, J | quick attack (X) | right mouse, K | strong attack (Y) |
| Space | jump (A) | E | projectile (B) |
| F | ninpo (Y + B) | C | water run (A + X) |
| Shift | block (LT) | Q, middle mouse | RT |
| R | LB | V | RB |
| Z / X | stick clicks | Tab / Escape | Back / Start |
| arrows | d-pad | Return / Backspace | A / B |
| Numpad 8 4 5 6 | camera (keys) | | |

The keys can be changed in `ng2.toml` (`keybind_a = "Space,C,Return"` and so on: a list of keys
for each button; a key in two lists presses both, as the game's two-button moves need).

## Known issues

- Some cutscenes may have slight audio delays.
- Tested on a Linux desktop, the Steam Deck, under Proton and in a Windows 11 virtual machine; reports
  from other systems, and from real Windows PCs especially, are welcome.

When reporting a graphics glitch, pressing **F7** while it is on screen records the next frames'
drawing to `~/ng2-trace-<n>` (Linux) or `C:\Users\<you>\ng2-trace-<n>` (Windows): attach that
folder, zipped. For a crash or a freeze, attach the log (`ng2.log`, above).

## Building from source

The build needs the game's code, so it starts from your own disc image. Requirements: clang 20+,
CMake 3.25+, Ninja, Python 3, the Vulkan headers and loader, FFmpeg (libavformat, libavcodec,
libswresample, libswscale).

1. The ReXGlue SDK, pinned at v0.10.0, with this port's patches:

       git clone --recursive https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk thirdparty/rexglue-sdk
       cd thirdparty/rexglue-sdk && git checkout v0.10.0 && git submodule update --init --recursive
       git am ../../patches/rexglue-sdk/*.patch
       cmake --preset linux-amd64
       cmake --build out/build/linux-amd64 --config Release --target install
       cd ../..

2. XenosRecomp (the shader translator) and plume (the Vulkan layer of Unleashed Recompiled), with
   this port's patches:

       git clone --recursive https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenosRecomp thirdparty/XenosRecomp
       cd thirdparty/XenosRecomp && git checkout 990d03b && git submodule update --init --recursive
       git am ../../patches/xenosrecomp/*.patch
       cd ../..

       git clone https://github.com/renderbag/plume thirdparty/plume
       cd thirdparty/plume && git checkout 1192686 && git submodule update --init contrib/volk contrib/VulkanMemoryAllocator contrib/Vulkan-Headers
       git am ../../patches/plume/*.patch
       cd ../..

   (`git am` makes commits: it needs a git name and email, `git config --global user.name` and
   `user.email`.)

3. Extract the disc (or the Games on Demand package) into `game_files/` and put Title Update 3's
   `default.xexp` next to `default.xex` (see [docs/title-update.md](docs/title-update.md)):

       python3 tools/xdvdfs_extract.py "Ninja Gaiden II (World).iso" game_files
       python3 tools/stfs_extract.py TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4 default.xexp game_files/default.xexp

4. Build. This generates about 560 MB of C++ from the game's code and translates its shaders
   (see [docs/shaders.md](docs/shaders.md)):

       cmake --preset linux-amd64-release
       cmake --build out/build/linux-amd64-release

5. Run it:

       out/build/linux-amd64-release/ng2 --game_data_root=game_files

The AppImage, `packaging/appimage/build.sh`, builds the SDK and the game in an Ubuntu 22.04
container (Docker; `packaging/appimage/Dockerfile`; it also needs rsync,
zsync (`zsyncmake`, for the `.zsync` updaters use) and
[appimagetool](https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool) on the PATH, or `APPIMAGETOOL=<path>`), so it needs only glibc 2.35 and runs on
SteamOS and other current distributions. It bundles a small FFmpeg with the movies' codecs and
writes `out/appimage/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage`. `packaging/appimage/build-local.sh` packs
the native build instead, quicker but only for the machine that built it.

The Windows build is cross-compiled from Linux after the native one: `packaging/windows/build.sh`
(clang and lld against Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK from
[xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin), `xwin --accept-license splat --output ~/.xwin`; plume
also needs its `contrib/D3D12MemoryAllocator` submodule there). It builds the SDK for Windows, fetches
FFmpeg's Windows build, and packs `out/windows/NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip`.

How it works: [docs/renderer-plan.md](docs/renderer-plan.md) (the renderer),
[docs/menus.md](docs/menus.md) (the menus), [docs/shaders.md](docs/shaders.md). How to contribute:
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); the layout, tools and test rules, also for coding agents:
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
```

`cmake/embed_spirv.cmake`:

```cmake
# Writes a SPIR-V binary as a C++ array.
# cmake -DINPUT=<file.spv> -DOUTPUT=<file.cpp> -DNAME=<symbol> -P embed_spirv.cmake
file(READ "${INPUT}" data HEX)
string(LENGTH "${data}" length)
math(EXPR size "${length} / 2")
string(REGEX REPLACE "([0-9a-f][0-9a-f])" "0x\\1," bytes "${data}")
file(WRITE "${OUTPUT}"
    "#include <cstddef>\n#include <cstdint>\n"
    "alignas(4) extern const uint8_t ${NAME}[] = {${bytes}};\n"
    "extern const size_t ${NAME}_size = ${size};\n")

```

`cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-clang-xwin.cmake`:

```cmake
# Cross-compile Ninja Gaiden II for Windows x86-64 from Linux: clang (its GNU-style
# driver, the MSVC ABI, as the ReXGlue SDK builds on Windows) and lld,
# with Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK from xwin
# (`xwin --accept-license splat --output ~/.xwin`; the license is the user's
# to accept). Used by packaging/windows/build.sh.
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Windows)
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_VERSION 10.0)
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR AMD64)

set(XWIN_ROOT "$ENV{HOME}/.xwin" CACHE PATH "xwin's splatted MSVC CRT and Windows SDK")
if(NOT EXISTS "${XWIN_ROOT}/crt/include" OR NOT EXISTS "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/um")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "No MSVC CRT and Windows SDK in ${XWIN_ROOT} (xwin --accept-license splat --output ${XWIN_ROOT})")
endif()

set(_triple x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER clang)
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER clang++)
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER_TARGET ${_triple})
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_TARGET ${_triple})
set(CMAKE_RC_COMPILER llvm-rc)
set(CMAKE_MT llvm-mt)
set(CMAKE_AR llvm-ar)  # CMake archives with ar's commands for a GNU-style driver
set(CMAKE_LINKER lld-link)
# The release DLL runtime (msvcrt, vcruntime140, msvcp140) in every
# configuration, as on Windows: xwin's CRT has no debug libraries, and the SDK's
# libraries use the same runtime.
set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreadedDLL")
set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION Release)

# Headers the code spells in another case than the SDK files (Windows
# doesn't care, Linux does): aliases in a directory of their own.
set(_case_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../out/windows-deps/include-case")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_case_dir}")
foreach(_alias "ObjBase.h=um/objbase.h" "SDKDDKVer.h=shared/sdkddkver.h")
    string(REPLACE "=" ";" _pair "${_alias}")
    list(GET _pair 0 _name)
    list(GET _pair 1 _target)
    if(NOT EXISTS "${_case_dir}/${_name}")
        file(CREATE_LINK "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/${_target}" "${_case_dir}/${_name}" SYMBOLIC)
    endif()
endforeach()

set(_xwin_includes
    "${_case_dir}"
    "${XWIN_ROOT}/crt/include"
    "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/ucrt"
    "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/um"
    "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/shared"
    "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/include/winrt")
# The SDK's headers as Visual Studio's INCLUDE puts them: after clang's own
# (-idirafter), whose intrinsics headers must win (with the SDK's first, SSE
# intrinsics became calls to functions that do not exist). Extra flags for the
# build (-march, PGO, ...) come in NG2_CROSS_FLAGS: a CMAKE_C_FLAGS given
# on the command line would replace these.
set(NG2_CROSS_FLAGS "-march=x86-64-v2" CACHE STRING "Extra C/C++ flags for the Windows cross build")
# xwin's STL (VS 17.10 and later) makes std::mutex's constructor constexpr,
# which crashes in mutex::lock with an older msvcp140.dll: off, so any
# 2015-2022 runtime works.
string(APPEND NG2_CROSS_FLAGS " -D_DISABLE_CONSTEXPR_MUTEX_CONSTRUCTOR")
set(_flags "${NG2_CROSS_FLAGS}")
foreach(_dir IN LISTS _xwin_includes)
    string(APPEND _flags " -idirafter \"${_dir}\"")
endforeach()
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS_INIT "${_flags}")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_INIT "${_flags}")
set(_xwin_libs "${XWIN_ROOT}/crt/lib/x86_64" "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/lib/um/x86_64" "${XWIN_ROOT}/sdk/lib/ucrt/x86_64")
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_LINK_DIRECTORIES ${_xwin_libs})
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_LINK_DIRECTORIES ${_xwin_libs})
set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_INIT "-fuse-ld=lld")
set(CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS_INIT "-fuse-ld=lld")
set(CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS_INIT "-fuse-ld=lld")
# The resource compiler's preprocessor (clang) finds windows.h for the version
# resource here.
set(_rc "")
foreach(_dir IN LISTS _xwin_includes)
    string(APPEND _rc " -I \"${_dir}\"")
endforeach()
set(CMAKE_RC_FLAGS_INIT "${_rc}")

# Nothing of this Linux system's: headers, libraries and CMake packages come
# from the Windows side only.
# The Windows build of the ReXGlue SDK (its install prefix) is searched too.
set(NG2_FIND_ROOTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/install/windows-x64"
    CACHE STRING "Extra Windows install prefixes to search")
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH "${XWIN_ROOT}" ${NG2_FIND_ROOTS})
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PROGRAM NEVER)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_INCLUDE ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PACKAGE ONLY)
set(PKG_CONFIG_EXECUTABLE "" CACHE FILEPATH "" FORCE)

```

`docs/cutscene-eyes.md`:

```md
# Cutscene eyes (fixed 2026-11-01, investigation notes)

Fixed: the eyelids are bones, and the renderer gave those draws palettes three frames old ("Cause
and fix" below); Sonia's shoulder hole was the Xenos multiply rule (XenosRecomp patch 0009). The
rest is the hunt, kept for what it found. The `NG2_TEST_*` switches and F8 to F12 keys it mentions
were temporary and are gone.

In the cutscene after Chapter 1's boss (Elizébet takes Sonia into a helicopter), Ryu's eyeballs sit
in front of his eyelids and Elizébet's eyes and teeth float beside her head. Xenia Edge shows the
scene correctly, so the cause is ours (recompiled CPU code or the renderer). Faces in other
cutscenes (Chapter 2's opening) are right.

## Reaching the scene in a test run

From the user's slot 2 save (Chapter 1, the statue before the last fight; `NG2_SAVE_FROM`), a test
autopilot (temporary code in `src/perf_overlay.cpp`, `NG2_TEST_AUTOPILOT`, not committed) walks Ryu
up the stairs, waits out the fight casting ninpo (Infinite Health and Ninpo on), opens the door
(RB) and casts at the boss; the cutscene follows at about 300-350 s. Steering needs the camera:
its position is at 0x84C3C3E0 (x, y, z), and stick up moves away from it with left and right
mirrored. Ryu's character object is at 0x8563EF70 in every run (record 0x84C23C70), position at
+0x270 (x, y, z).

## What draws the eyes

- Ryu's eyeballs are rigid meshes (vertex buffers 0x19DDA000 and 0x19DD9000 in the cutscene) drawn
  with vertex shader 18161E8508C7FB4D: positions from fetch slot 95, one WorldViewProj in c21-c24,
  no bones. Skinned draws (7D7B9634653FDB27 and others) read 3x4 bone matrices (12 floats each)
  from fetch slot 94 and use c21-c24 as the camera's view-projection.
- The eye's world matrix is a 4x4 (rows: basis, then translation) in a per-frame render entry pool
  (0x84E79xxx; Ryu's eyes at 0x84E79240 and 0x84E792D0 during the cutscene; the same slots hold
  other objects at other times). An entry: matrix at +0, previous entry at +0x44, a type pointer at
  +0x48, an index at +0x4C.
- In the cutscene that entry is written by sub_824805B0, called from sub_8247B728 <- sub_8247B2A8
  <- sub_8247A730 <- the frame update sub_822F16D0. (sub_8233D418 writes attached parts' world
  matrices, character+216+0x70*k, local at -88, offset at -24, times the character's root at +0,
  but not the cutscene eyes.)
- 0x859D3C60/0x859D4E30 also hold the eye matrix: the draw-time matrix state, written by
  sub_837CCC28 for every draw.

## The eye matrices are right (2026-11-01)

- sub_824805B0 (object, entry, ...) computes an attached entry's world matrix by its type,
  `*(*(entry + 0x58) + 4)`. The eyes are type 2 (info words 5, 0 or 1 for left or right), which
  calls sub_824810D0(out, object, entry, base matrix by value in r6-r10 plus the stack, v1, v2). It
  fetches a look-at target with sub_823F8448(id, slot) (Ryu looks at 62, probably Sonia) and turns
  the base matrix a few degrees toward it, keeping the translation (the eye's pivot). In the
  cutscene the two pivots are 5.7 cm apart and the turns small: the eyes are where they should be.
- So the face around them is wrong: the skinned face (bones from fetch slot 94, the facial bones
  driven by the `.fac` facial animation) sits too far back on Ryu, and Elizébet's face skin is off
  while her eyes and teeth (rigid) are in place. Next: what writes the facial bones' skinning
  matrices.
- The vector instructions checked in sub_824810D0 (vmaddfp128, vnmsubfp128, vrsqrtefp with its
  Newton step, vsel128, vmsum3fp128, vcsxwfp128, vrlimi128 with rotations 2 and 3) translate
  correctly.

## Bone palettes and the head (2026-11-01, later)

- Skinning palettes rotate through three buffers, one per frame (Ryu in the helicopter scene:
  0x1D55F000, 0x1D5BF000, 0x1D61F000; Sonia's 0x6000 lower). Physical memory is seen at
  0xA0000000 + p, 0xC0000000 + p and 0xE0000000 + p - 0x1000.
- Bones 4-71 of Ryu's palette hold one identical matrix in both the helicopter scene and the
  Chapter 2 opening (a rigid head group, or unused slots): not a symptom.
- The eye's pivot, taken into the bind space of those head bones, is the same in both scenes,
  (-0.029, 0.664, 0.078) against (-0.028, 0.660, 0.083): the eyes sit correctly on the head in the
  buggy scene too.
- The look-at in sub_824810D0 turns Ryu's eyes about 5 degrees toward character 62, close to the
  straight direction to it. If the eye mesh isn't centred on its pivot, a turn like that moves the
  eyeball forward; whether Xenia turns them by as much is the open question.
- The write trap can't watch physical memory: the SDK's handler runs before ours and takes those
  faults (it unprotects the page). Watching the palette needs our handler first.

## Closed eyelids (2026-11-01, evening)

- Ryu's eyeball mesh is static (the same 178 vertices for both eyes, centred on the pivot), and the
  eye look-at isn't the cause (copying the input matrix to the output leaves the bulge).
- The bulge shows in the medium shot of Ryu and Sonia, not in Ryu's close-ups. With the eye meshes
  hidden (`NG2_TEST_HIDEMESH`), the medium shot shows his face skin with the eyelids shut over the
  sockets: the open eyeballs then sit in front of closed lids. So the facial animation (eyelids)
  is not applied there, or shuts them. Ryu's skinned body mesh (0x19CDD000) is the same in both
  shots (no level-of-detail switch); its bind-space positions end below the eyes, so the head and
  face skin are other meshes.

- Ryu's head is rigid meshes drawn with vertex shader D7A4920F (not skinned), vertex buffers
  0x1A0F3000, 0x1A09D000, 0x1A0BB000, 0x19DDC000, 0x1A0ED000 in the helicopter scene. All are static
  except 0x19DDC000 (154 indices), whose contents change nearly every frame: the CPU morphs it,
  which makes it the eyelid or face part the facial animation drives. The game doesn't lock it
  through D3D (sub_8373E5B8 never sees it), so its writer has to be found by a write trap on
  physical memory (all four host views: 0xA0000000 + p, 0xC0000000 + p, 0xE0000000 + p - 0x1000,
  and the SDK's own physical view), which hasn't worked reliably yet.

## The changing head buffer is cloth (2026-11-01, night)

- The trap finally caught 0x19DDC000's writer once the SDK was kept from making the page writable
  again (it does that through mprotect when the game changes a physical range's protection, from
  sub_8233B420/sub_8233B638 via sub_836F1618; a temporary mprotect override keeps watched pages
  read-only). The writes come through the 0xE0000000 view from sub_836ED380, called by
  sub_836ED768 after 15 passes of sub_836ECF20 (sub_836ED858 <- sub_836EB2E0 <- sub_822F2870 <-
  sub_822F27B8): a cloth solver, writing positions (12 bytes in each 32-byte vertex). So that
  buffer is cloth (likely his scarf), not the eyelids, and the head has no CPU morph.
- So the shut eyelids in the medium shot come from which head meshes are drawn there, not from a
  morph.

## Against Xenia Edge's GPU traces (2026-11-01, night)

- Xenia Edge needs `-DXENIA_ENABLE_GPU_TRACE=ON` for F4 to write traces (the Release build only
  logs that it can't); `--trace_gpu_prefix=<dir>/` picks the folder. `tools/xtr_draws.py` replays
  a trace's register writes and memory reads and lists each draw's index count, fetch 95, chosen
  constants (`--consts`), registers (`--regs`) and index range, and dumps buffers (`--dump`).
- At matching moments (frames whose head matrices agree), the eyes' WorldViewProj relative to the
  head piece 1A0F3000 matches Xenia's within 1-2 mm and a degree. The hood (1A09D000), face
  (1A0BB000, vertex shader 9373E6B1) and 1A0F3000 keep the same matrices relative to each other.
- The eye, hood and face vertex buffers and the face's index buffer (0x1A0C1000, 0x3F4 bytes) are
  byte-identical to Xenia's; depth, blend, polygon offset and colour-control registers are the
  same; both shaders only multiply a float3 position by WorldViewProj. Texture slots 1-2 of the
  eye draws hold leftovers in both.
- So the guest side is the same as Xenia's: the difference is in our renderer. Suspect: its own
  copy of guest memory (g_guestMemory, kept in step by comparing with a shadow) holding something
  else at those addresses, such as memory-export output that the shadow comparison never sees.

- With the user's settings (render_scale 5, antialiasing 2) a test run of the current build
  (2026-11-01, run74) draws the scene right: Ryu's eyes inside his lids and Elizébet's face as in
  Xenia. The test runs' pictures before that were 320x180, too small to show the bug, and the
  user's traces (10-31 18:15) predate the vertex rounding change (patch 0008), the XMA fixes and
  scissor support. Forcing every vertex buffer to upload at every draw (`NG2_TEST_ALWAYSSYNC`)
  changed nothing visible at low resolution. Open: whether the user still sees it with the
  current build.

## The user's session (2026-11-01, afternoon)

- With the rebuilt AppImage the user still gets it (traces 7-15 in ~/ng2-trace-*, with memory and
  the GPU-copy check). In their session the eyes are at 0x19DD8000/0x19DD9000 and the hood at
  0x1A09C000 (a page lower than in Xenia and the test runs): a different allocation history. Their
  eye matrices still match Xenia's within a millimetre, their eye, face and hood buffers are
  byte-identical to Xenia's, and the renderer's GPU copies of them match guest memory (the F7
  check, `gpucheck.txt`; only cloth and hair ranges differ, written after their draws).
- The eye pixel shader (container 0x820B9550) clips by the eye texture's alpha (slot 0, DXT5
  0x19CC8000) only when boolean word 4 bit 1 is set; it is clear in Xenia, the user's run and
  the test runs alike, so the eyeball's visible part comes from depth against the face patch
  (1A0BB000, 506 indices, 128x64 skin textures: the eyelids). That patch is drawn after the eyes
  in both. Same depth control, cull key, booleans, texture bindings and draw order everywhere.
- So the difference is GPU-side state a trace can't show (depth buffer contents, a cached
  pipeline, surface or texture made earlier in their session). The trace line now also prints
  the cull key, depth format and texture, the scissor registers and the pipeline key hash.
- Reproduction attempts: the user skips the cutscene before the boss and fights with the sword;
  the autopilot gained `NG2_TEST_SKIPCUT` (Start for 12 s in the boss area) and
  `NG2_TEST_SWORD` (X instead of ninpo) to try the same.

- Reproduction attempts with the user's render settings, none showing the bug: skipping the
  cutscene before the boss (`NG2_TEST_SKIPCUT`), the boss by sword (`NG2_TEST_SWORD`), sound on
  (`NG2_TEST_AUDIO=disk`), the FPS counter on (`show_fps`, which does move the buffers to the
  user's addresses: the counter's text goes through the game's 2D lists). Next: their ng2.toml
  verbatim (fullscreen, vsync, present mode: also fine). The test runs' pictures are of the front
  buffer, so presentation can't be the difference. Next: the live test in their session: F8
  throws the render target surfaces away, F10 the pipelines and textures (both temporary, in the
  AppImage of 17:07; exercised headlessly with `NG2_TEST_FLUSHONTRACE=3`, the game goes on fine).
  If the eyes fix themselves after one of them, that cache holds the bad object.
- Neither F8 nor F10 changed anything in the user's session (17:31): surfaces (a fresh depth
  buffer), pipelines and textures are all out. The eye index buffers (Xenia 0x19E88000 and
  0x19E89000, 0x334 bytes each, a page lower in the user's session) and the hood's and 1A0F3000's
  are byte-identical to Xenia's too. The one environmental difference found so far: the user's
  game runs in a Wayland window, the test runs in an X11 one under gamescope (`NG2_TEST_WAYLAND=1`
  tries the former: also fine). The game folders are the same files. The user's process environment
  holds nothing graphics-related beyond DXVK_HUD=0 and MESA_SHADER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=16G.

## F11 fixes the faces (2026-11-01, evening)

- In the user's session, F11 (temporary: `SyncGuestMemory` uploads every range whole at every
  draw) fixes Ryu's eyes and the faces, live. So the renderer's GPU copy of some range those draws
  read is wrong at draw time, though right at the end of the frame (the earlier F7 check). The
  check now runs right after the traced frame's first eye draw instead, to catch the bad bytes.
- Sonia's hole (her right shoulder, the crouching shot) stays with F11: a separate bug.
- Xenia Edge fixes in the same area (memexport output vs guest memory in its shared memory
  buffer): d1541a57 (invalidate physical pages on allocation: reused pages kept stale GPU bytes),
  b8372465 and 16df2598 (memexport pages vs resolve output), 31a696a9 (vertex shader memexport
  output landing after the guest rewrote that memory). Ours has no record of the pages memexport
  wrote, so a skinning pass writing over a static mesh's range (the eyes sit right after Ryu's
  skinned body buffer, 0x19CDD000 + 0xE6950) would never be undone: the shadow says unchanged.

- The check at the eye draw itself (fixed to read back only after its frame is submitted;
  ~/ng2-trace-30): in the user's session the GPU copies of the eye, face, hood, 1A0F2000/1A0EC000
  pieces, Ryu's body and his palettes all match guest memory at that moment. So F11 doesn't fix
  the data; its side effect does: each of its uploads puts a barrier before the draw, which also
  ends the render pass. F12 (temporary) now does only that (a barrier before every draw, no
  upload): if it fixes the faces too, the bug is missing synchronization or a render pass
  problem between draws, not memory contents.

## Cause and fix (2026-11-01, evening)

- F12 then (temporary: only fetch 94, the bone palettes, uploaded at every draw) fixed the faces
  live: the eyelids are bones. The palettes rotate through three buffers; each comes round
  "stable" (unchanged for over a frame), so SyncGuestMemory checked it at its first draw only,
  while the game's jobs were still writing it during the frame's draws. FinishGuestMemory then
  saw it changed and checked it at every draw for one frame, but the ring moved on and three
  frames later the same buffer was stable again. CPU timing decides how far the jobs are at the
  first draw, so it showed in the user's sessions and not in the headless runs.
- First fix, `GuestMemoryRange::dynamic` (a range checked once in a frame and found written by
  its end is checked at every draw from then on): not enough, the user still saw it. F12's
  every-draw upload also kept the range's changedFrame current, so a palette written after the
  frame's draws became late; without it, a buffer the jobs fill only after the draws looks
  unchanged at them, takes FinishGuestMemory's other branch and never becomes late, and its
  draws use the bones of three frames before.
- Fix: palettes (ranges read through fetch slot 94) are late from their first draw: every draw
  of the frame gets the palette as it is just before submission, as the console's GPU would.
  Confirmed by the user (2026-11-01, 19:34 AppImage): faces right. Sonia's shoulder hole stays.

## Sonia's shoulder hole

- Where: the rooftop shot of Ryu facing the camera with Sonia's back to it, under the strap on
  her right shoulder blade: Ryu's chest (grey weave) shows through her skin. Deterministic: the
  headless runs show it too (out/run90, frame 16140); Xenia's trace of that shot (16121) doesn't.
- Her back is drawn twice, blended (SRC_ALPHA, INV_SRC_ALPHA): skinned VS 7D7B9634, 4453
  indices from VB 0x16A22000 (Xenia 0x16A23000), texture DXT5 512x512 at 0x165E0000. First pass
  without depth write or alpha test, second with depth write and alpha test (ref 0.251). Same
  state and blend in Xenia. Its pixel shader (0x82238150) takes alpha from the texture times an
  interpolant, and can clip parts listed in PS c30 (`SupDel`, 65535.1 in Xenia: none).
- Flat colour (NG2_DEBUG_HIGHLIGHT, now also <hash>,<hash>... with a colour per shader): the
  hole is geometry. 7D7B9634 is Ryu's body and Sonia's hair; her skin is VS 8282819E (container
  0x8221A3C8, VB 0x1697A000, 11 dwords a vertex), and the hole is a gap in it.
- That shader blends four position streams by constant weights (PosWeight, PosWeight2): fetch
  slots 90, 91 and 93 (0x169F6000, 0x16A0C000, 0x169E0000, 3 floats a vertex) and slot 92, which
  points at the skin's own vertex buffer read 3 dwords a vertex: garbage, with 92 NaNs, weighted
  0. On Xenos a multiply by 0 is 0 even for NaN (Shader Model 3; Xenia's ZeroIfAnyOperandIsZero
  for mul, mad, dp and the scalar muls); ours gave NaN positions and those triangles vanished.
- Fix (XenosRecomp, patch 0009): mul, mad, dp2add/dp3/dp4, muls, mulsprev and mulsc go through
  `mulz`/`dotz` in shader_common.h, which give 0 when either operand is 0 or denormal; so does
  dst's y. The helpers are `precise` (DXC doesn't carry precise into called functions; without
  it the dot products lost the no-fusion guarantee of patch 0008). Headless: the hole is gone.

## Ruled out

- Shader rounding: vertex shaders now round toward zero and don't fuse multiply-adds (as Xenos);
  the eyes were unchanged.
- XMA timing: the decoders match Xenia Edge's but for about one frame.
- In sub_8233D418: vupkd3d128 (mode 4), vpermwi128, vrlimi128 and vmsum4fp128 translate correctly.

## Tools

- F7 (or `NG2_TRACE_FILE`) traces: draws (with cull, depth target, scissor, viewport, clip and
  vertex control registers, the pipeline key), clears, pictures, the frame's memory and vertex
  shader constants.
- `tools/xtr_draws.py`: the same draws, constants and registers from a Xenia Edge GPU trace (F4 in
  a build with `-DXENIA_ENABLE_GPU_TRACE=ON`), and its buffers.
- `NG2_DEBUG_HIGHLIGHT=<hash>,<hash>,...`: those shaders flat, a colour each (logged): a hole that
  stays is geometry.
```

```md
# D3D map, part A (37 of the 74 public D3D functions)

XDK 2.0.6683, D3D range 0x83737000-0x8374D8F0. Found by reading the disassembly
(`tools/callgraph.py ... asm/callers`) and the image dump (`NG2_DUMP_IMAGE`) for
static tables. Guest args are r3, r4, ...; floats in f1 still use up a GPR slot
(PPC64 ABI), so args after a float skip one register. "dev" = D3DDevice*.
Names are XDK names (`D3DDevice_X` is shortened to `X`). "Guess" means the name
was not proved.

NG2 does not use the D3D9-compat draw calls Unleashed hooks (DrawPrimitive,
DrawIndexedPrimitive, DrawPrimitiveUP). It calls the native 360 ones:
DrawVertices, DrawIndexedVertices, BeginVertices, BeginIndexedVertices.

| 8373C1F0 | BeginIndexedVertices | r3 dev, r4 prim type, r5 base vertex, r6 vertex count, r7 index count, r8 index format (bit 2 = 32-bit), r9 stride, r10 void** ppIndexData, stack(84) void** ppVertexData; returns HRESULT | high | caller 82832C60 passes (6,0,n,n,1,16,&idx,&vtx) and memcpy's vertices/indices into the returned pointers; same packet path as BeginVertices |

Tally: 21 high, 13 medium, 3 low (two of the low ones are name guesses:
Suspend/Resume).

## Device creation (83737BB8 and game 837C62E8)

- 837C62E8 fills a D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS at 0x839D3440 (EnableAutoDepthStencil
  +0x24 = 0, DisableAutoBackBuffer +0x38 = 1, DisableAutoFrontBuffer +0x3C = 1),
  calls `Direct3D_CreateDevice(0, 1, 0, 1, &pp, &pp+128)` and keeps the device
  at renderer+92 (`lwz r3,92(rX)` before every D3D call). It then calls
  SetRingBufferParameters again on resets (837C6680, 822F2218) with pp+72.
- 83737BB8: XMemAlloc(0x5800, 0x24800000), align the result up to 128 bytes
  and store the raw pointer at dev-4, memset **0x5780 bytes = device size**
  (Unleashed's static_assert is 0x5E00, so their device is bigger). Sets
  refcount dev+0x3C = 1, qword dev+0x2A80 from 0x83BCAAC0, owner thread
  dev+0x2A88, flags dev+0x5708 = 0x0C000001, second XMemAlloc(4800) at
  dev+0x4148, then 83741F00 (engine init). Failure: Release, return
  0x8007000E.
- 83741F00 (init) calls 8373A918 (ring), 83748DC8 (worker threads),
  8373B060 (constant-reload indirect buffers), 83748F18 (default register
  shadows, all dirty), 83741B08 (video mode, gamma), **83741898 (state
  tables)**, then KickOff.

### SetRenderState / SetSamplerState tables (filled by 83741898)

Same layout as Unleashed's GuestDevice:

| Offset | Content |
| --- | --- |
| dev+0x040 | SetRenderState fn table, 0x65 entries, index = D3DRS value / 4; called as `fn(dev, value)` |
| dev+0x1D4 | SetSamplerState fn table, 0x14 entries, index = D3DSAMP value / 4; called as `fn(dev, sampler, value)` |
| dev+0x224 | GetRenderState fn table, 0x65 entries, `fn(dev)` returns the value |
| dev+0x3B8 | GetSamplerState fn table, 0x14 entries |
| dev+0x480 | 32 fetch constants x 24 bytes (texture fetch for samplers 0-25; vertex fetch slots 95-s at the top) |

The static source tables are 12-byte entries {get, set, default}:
render states at **0x83A84EE0** (101 entries), sampler states at
**0x83A853A0** (20 entries). 83741898 copies set to +0x40/+0x1D4 and get to
+0x224/+0x3B8, then calls each setter with the default (all 26 samplers).
Examples: D3DRS_ZENABLE (40, index 10): set 0x837351D0 (writes dev+0x2E5C and
the Z_ENABLE bit of RB_DEPTHCONTROL at dev+0x2934, forced 0 when there is no
depth surface), get 0x83735208, default 1. Indices 0-9 are stubs (set
0x836D87A8 = blr, get 0x837C1A60 = return 0). Sampler setters write the
fetch constant at dev+0x480+24*s and set bit (63-(32+s)) in qword dev+0x18.

**Game code calls render states through the table.** Its wrapper 837C7080
(this=renderer, r4 = D3DRS value, r5 = value; 74 callers) does
`lwz r11,64(dev+state); mtctr; bctr` with r3 = dev, r4 = value. So
Unleashed's approach (overwrite dev+0x40[...] with host thunks after
CreateDevice) works unchanged. Sampler states seem to go through dev+0x1D4
the same way (indirect loads of 468+ near mtctr in game code). Not every
call site was checked.

## Device offsets confirmed

| Offset | Meaning | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x00 / 0x08 | qword dirty masks: VS / PS float constants | 8373B1F8 / 8373B2E0 OR into them; draws flush to regs 0x4000 / 0x4400 |

| 0x3A8C | 1536-byte hardware gamma table | 837377C0 |
| 0x5708 | creation flags (0x0C000001) | 83737BB8 |
| size | 0x5780 | memset in 83737BB8 |

## Resource offsets confirmed

- Header: +0 Common (low 4 bits type: 4 = surface, 6 = VS, 7 = PS; bits
  8-11 = lock count; bit 30 on surfaces = has parent at +24), +4 RefCount
  (atomic, AddRef 8373E970), +8 Fence, +12 ReadFence, +20 BaseFlush, +24
  MipFlush or data (16:16 range in 128-byte units, 0xFFFF0000 = clean).
- Vertex buffer: +24/+28 = GPUVERTEX_FETCH_CONSTANT dwords (address \| type,
  size \| endian).
- Index buffer: +0 bit 31 = 32-bit indices, +24 = address, +28 = size.
- Surface: +24 low 2 bits = (MSAA?) kind used by Resolve, +28 =
  RB_COLOR_INFO / RB_DEPTH_INFO value, +32 = extra depth word (to dev+0x2940).
- Pixel shader: 40-byte object, shader header copy at +40, microcode phys ptr
  at +24. Vertex shader: 872-byte object, header copy at +872.
- Vertex declaration: 56-byte header + 12 bytes per element.

## Open questions

- Who calls EndVertices? BeginVertices records dev+0x3474/0x3478/0x3480. No
  public function reads them, so it is probably inline in game code; check
  before hooking BeginVertices.
- The game writes stream pointers/strides and the vertex declaration inline,
  so a renderer has to read dev+0x30A4/0x30E8/0x2E24 at draw time rather than
  rely on hooked setters alone. Same for SetVertexShaderConstantF: the hook
  must take the dirty mask in r7.
- 8373E5B8/8373E848 are called directly by game code (inline Lock/Unlock), so
  the lock/unlock hooks must go on these helpers too, not only on the
  8373EBE8/ECF8 wrappers.
- Suspend/Resume and SetShaderGPRAllocation are not proven. The meaning of the
  r4 "kind" argument of 8373E5B8 isn't known either.
```

```md
## Corrections and cross-checks for docs/renderer-plan.md and part A

- **The D3D range is wrong at both ends.** Library code starts below 0x83737000 (at least
  0x83732008; XGraphics-style size and tiling helpers go further down) and ends at about 0x8374D558
  (8374D558-8374D8E8 are XAudio). Functions in 0x83732000-0x83737000 called from the game
  that the 74-list therefore misses (the names come from reading the code; they are medium unless
  marked):
  - 837341F0 **SetTexture**(dev, r4=sampler, r5=texture, r6=u64 pending bit), 67 game callers, high.
    It copies the texture's 6-dword fetch constant (+28..+48) into dev+1152+24*sampler, stores the
    pointer at dev+12536+4*sampler, ORs the bit into pending +24 and fences the old texture.
  - 83736F48 **SetStreamSource**(dev, r4=stream, r5=vb, r6=offset, r7=stride, r8=pending bit),
    8 game callers, high. It writes vertex fetch constants at dev+8*(239-stream) (+1780), pointer at
    12452+4*stream, stride/4 byte at 12520+stream (compared with 11824+stream, then pending +16).
  - 83733E30 **CreateTexture** (52-byte header; 17 game callers) and 83733F50 **CreateSurface**
    (48 bytes, EDRAM tiles via 8373EF78; 11 callers), both high. 83741B08 shows the argument order:
    CreateTexture(w, h, levels=1, usage=1, 0, format, 0, pool=3), CreateSurface(w, h, format,
    multisample, 0).
  - 83736EC8 **SetViewport**(dev, D3DVIEWPORT9*), which converts X/Y/W/H to float and calls 83734810
    (dev, f1..f6 = X, Y, W, H, MinZ, MaxZ). The viewport is shadowed at dev+12640.
  - 83736DC8 **SetScissorRect**(dev, RECT*). The rect is stored at dev+12668 and clamped to the
    viewport into the register shadow at 10436/10440.
  - 83732DB8 **GetLevelDesc**(tex, level, D3DSURFACE_DESC*) (16 callers), 837340B8
    **D3DSurface_GetDesc** (= Unleashed GetSurfaceDesc), 837334F0/83733428 texture **LockRect**,
    83734150 surface LockRect, 83734170 surface UnlockRect. These are medium.
  - 837363D8 and 83736568: SetSamplerState setters for one state each (sampler r4, value r5). They
    write dword 3 of the fetch constant (filter fields) and the pending +24 bit. They have 55 direct
    game callers each, probably MinFilter/MagFilter (guess).
- 83737180 is **SetRenderTarget**(dev, index, surface) and 837374E8 is
  **SetDepthStencilSurface**(dev, surface): 83741B08 binds the back buffer with the first and the
  auto-depth surface with the second. renderer-plan says "837374E8 SetRenderTarget-like".
- 8373B4D8 (dev+12684) is **SetPixelShader**, not SetVertexShader. 8373B880 (dev+12688) is
  **SetVertexShader**. Evidence: IsSet maps type 6 (VS) to 12688 and type 7 (PS) to 12684. The
  12688 setter also reads a larger header (fixups at +872 against +40) and touches VS-side bits.
- Device layout differs from Unleashed's `GuestDevice` in the first 0x40 bytes. The pending masks
  are qwords +0 (VS consts), +8 (PS consts), +16 (misc: shaders, vdecl 0x80000, ...), +24 (fetch
  constants, 1 bit per fetch slot from the top), +32 and +40 (register blocks). **+48 is the ring
  write cursor, +56 the ring limit, +60 the device refcount**, so it is not "8 dirty qwords". The
  render-state function table is at +0x40 and the sampler-state table at +0x1D4 (as in Unleashed).
  Fetch constants are at +0x480 (1152), VS constants at +0x780 and PS constants at +0x1780.
  Bindings: IB 12428, RT0-3 12432-12444, DS 12448, streams 12452[16], stream strides (bytes)
  12520, textures 12536[26], PS 12684, VS 12688, vdecl 11812 (Unleashed: 0x2E2C = 11820, so 8
  bytes earlier here), viewport 12640 (Unleashed 0x3168 = 12648), scissor 12668.
  Present params copy: 13528. Frame buffers: 14808 auto depth, 14812 front texture, 14816 back
  buffer. GPU register shadows sit around 10112-10440 with dirty bits in +32/+40. The fence
  counter is at 10908 and the last inserted fence at 10928.

## D3D functionality reached outside the 74 public functions

Many XDK calls in NG2 are inlined into game code. The XDK's inline headers explain part of it,
and link-time code generation of the D3D library may explain the rest (a guess). The inlined
calls write straight into the device shadow and pending masks. A hook-only renderer will not see
these calls. Every one of them still ends in a draw or a resolve that reads the device, so the
practical approach is to hook the draws (8373BD50, 8373C1F0, 8373C720, 8373CB08, part A) and
Resolve (8373D570) and **read the state from the device at that moment**: bindings, fetch
constants, shader constant shadows and register shadows. Do not rely on Set* hooks. The patterns
found:

1. **SetVertexDeclaration, inlined, no refcount.** `stw decl,11812(dev); ld r,16(dev); oris r,r,8;
   std r,16(dev)` appears in 59 game functions, for example 8231B3B0, 82805030, 837E9CC8,
   8361B580 and 837C6680 (which sets NULL). No library SetVertexDeclaration is called. Hook
   creation instead (CreateVertexDeclaration is likely one of 8373B3C8/8373B790/8373BBE0, the
   creators in part A's share; guess) and read dev+11812 at draw time. The device embeds its own
   declaration at dev+12184 (837ECC30 compares against it), probably for the UP draws.
2. **Shader constants, inlined.** VS constants are written with `stfs` into dev+0x780+16*reg plus
   `ld/ori 8192/std` on pending +0 (for example 82805030 writes c232 at dev+5120..5132). PS
   constants are written into dev+0x1780+16*reg plus `or` of a bit into +8 (8231B3B0 writes
   dev+6500.. = c30). Pending +0 is written by 39 game functions and +8 by 48. The library
   SetVertexShaderConstantF 8373B1F8 is used only for the non-constant cases.
3. **Render states and sampler states through the device function tables.** The game's state cache
   flush 837C6F90 (14 callers) calls `*(dev + 0x40 + D3DRS)` with (dev, value) and
   `*(dev + 0x1D4 + 4*(type-1))` with (dev, sampler, value). D3DRS values are byte offsets
   (multiples of 4). The table entries are the many small functions at 0x83734A78-0x837368xx, which
   update the register shadow and the pending +32/+40 bits. Hooking those addresses catches the
   table calls. A few states are also written directly:
   - fetch-constant edits at dev+1152 with `oris 0x8000` on +24 (82331348, sampler 0 address and
     clamp bits; 70 game functions touch +24);
   - register-shadow edits at dev+10112/10120 with a bit in +32 (8282D300; 34 functions touch +32).
4. **Texture and stream unbinding plus resource fencing, inlined.** 837C6680 (game present) and
   836552E0 loop over textures 12536.. and streams 12452.., clear the slots, and tag each old
   resource with the current fence (res+8 = dev+10908). When fence tracking is off they append a
   tag to the block at dev+13508, growing it with 837397E0 and 83745B20, which inlines 8373F180.
   This amounts to SetTexture(NULL)/SetStreamSource(NULL) for everything.
5. **Fences and kickoff, inlined.** 822F16D0 and 837C6680 read dev+10908, store it to 10928 and
   call 8373A3D0. This looks like InsertFence (guess). 837C6680 also writes ring packets directly
   through 8373A5A8 (callback 0x837C59C8) and `stw r3,48(dev)`. This is the only game-side PM4
   writing found: no game function was found writing `stwu` packets into the ring at dev+48.
6. **Present is done by the game itself.** 837C6680 does Resolve (8373D570) into its own
   front-buffer textures (double-buffered at obj+1304/1308), then the unbind loops from item 4,
   then SynchronizeToPresentationInterval-like 83744D90, then Swap 837452C0(dev, tex, 0).
   837459D8 (Present) is used only by 8377E620/83873B80. Swap is therefore the hook to take for
   frame presentation.
7. **Device Reset, inlined** in 822F2218 and 837C6680 (see 83741DC0).
8. **State capture.** 837ECC30 reads streams, IB (AddRef 8373E970), VS 12688, PS 12684, vdecl
   11812 and viewport 12640 directly. This is an inline equivalent of Get* and StateBlock. If the
   renderer replaces the guest objects, these fields must still hold valid guest pointers.
9. **Predicated tiling and Z pass** come through 8374C728/8374CA98/8374CF50/8374D1E0 (above),
   called from the game's 837DF208 and 837DF3B8 (and 822F16D0). A PC-style renderer can make
   BeginTiling/EndTiling one untiled pass plus a resolve, and make the Z pass a no-op or a depth
   prepass.

Not found in the game: DrawPrimitiveUP-style inline writes. UP draws presumably go through the
library draw functions (part A).

## Open questions

- How large is the 0x83728000-0x83737000 library block exactly (XGraphics vs D3D), and which other
  functions there does the game call? The 39 game-called functions in 0x83732000-0x83737000 are
  listed by the scan; only those named above were read.
- Names and argument order of the creators 8373B3C8/8373B790/8373BBE0 (vertex declaration and
  shader creation; part A's share).
- 83744D90 (SynchronizeToPresentationInterval?) and 8374CF50/8374D1E0 (Z pass?) are named from
  structure only.
- Whether any game code inlines Release (an atomic decrement on res+4) instead of calling
  8373E9E8. If it does, DestructResource 8373E3B8 is still the right hook, since it is reached only
  through 8373E9E8.
- The exact meaning of pending-mask bits in +16/+32/+40. They are needed to know which register
  shadows to re-read at draw time.

```
