```md
## 1. Where the library starts

The D3D/XGraphics code starts at **0x83732250**. Evidence:

- 83730408-83732248 is one other module. 83730408 builds a 0x7880-byte object, 83730538 checks
  `+0 == 0x7880 && +4 == 6` and a 0x01234567 change sentinel, and every function from 83731E70 to
  83732168 calls 83730538. None of them touches a device, a resource header or a fetch constant.
  83732168 ends at 0x83732248.
- 83732250 (format block size), 837322E8 (max mip count), 83732370/83732490 (level sizes),
  83732800/837329F0/83732EB8/83732FB8 (level dimensions, pitches, addresses) are the shared
  texture-layout helpers that CreateTexture, LockRect, GetLevelDesc and Resolve (8373D570 calls
  83732FB8) use. They are called only by library code and by the XG code at 0x8385xxxx.
- Library-internal callers of these helpers sit directly above: 83733428 onwards (resource
  methods), 83734370-837368C0 (viewport/scissor internals, render- and sampler-state table
  functions), 83736DC8-83736F48 (Set* entry points), then part A's range from 83737068.

The **public XGraphics API is elsewhere, in the game-side code range** (XG is a separate lib):
8385CF58 = XGSetTextureHeader (24 game callers), 8385CFC8 = XGSetTextureHeaderEx (1 caller,
82332238), 8385CD58 = their common body (calls 83732250 and 83733628), 8385D0C0 =
XGOffsetResourceAddress (32 callers), 8385D058 = XGOffsetBaseTextureAddress. The functions
8382C738-83836F28 and 8385B6A0-8385E620 that call 83732370/83732800/83732898/83733D58/83733E28
look like more XG/D3DX texture code (tiling, fill, load). This is a guess; they were not read.

## 2. Textures: who creates them, object layout, SetTexture

**Both paths are used.** CreateTexture 83733E30 has 18 call sites (render-target copies, front
buffers in 83741B08, dynamic textures). Asset textures are built on game-owned memory with
XGSetTextureHeader. Example: 8231B008 calls `XGSetTextureHeader(128, 128, 1, 0, fmt, 0, 0,
0xFFFFFFFF, 0, &hdr, 0, 0)` (returns the size), then `XGOffsetResourceAddress(hdr, dataPtr)`, then
8380F110 = XPhysicalProtect(data, size, 2) (MmSetAddressProtect). The headers live inside game
structures, so a hook on CreateTexture alone will miss most of the textures the game draws with.
A host renderer has to work from the header passed to SetTexture (or from the fetch constant in
the device) and look up or upload by address, or also hook 8385CD58 and 8385D0C0.

Texture object (D3DBaseTexture, 52 bytes):

| Offset | Field |
| --- | --- |
| +0 | Common: type in bits 0-3 (3 texture; 17-20 come from GetType, not stored), 0x00100000 always, 0x00200000 / 0x00400000 from usage bits, lock count in bits 8-11 |
| +4 | RefCount (1 at creation) |
| +8 / +12 | Fence / ReadFence |
| +16 | Identifier (not written by the creators) |
| +20 / +24 | BaseFlush / MipFlush dirty ranges, 0xFFFF0000 = clean |
| +28 | fc dword0: type (2 = texture), signs, clamp (bits 10-18, overwritten by the device at SetTexture), pitch>>5 (bits 22-30), tiled (bit 31) |
| +32 | fc dword1: format (bits 0-5), endian (6-7), stacked (10), **base address, CPU virtual, bits 12-31** |
| +36 | fc dword2: size-1 per axis (1D 24 bits; 2D 13/13 + stack depth; 3D 11/11/10) |
| +40 | fc dword3: num format, swizzle (1-12), exp adjust (13-18), filters (19-30, from the device), border (31) |
| +44 | fc dword4: mip_min_level (2-5), mip_max_level (6-9) = levels-1, lod bias etc. from the device |
| +48 | fc dword5: dimension (bits 9-10: 0 1D, 1 2D, 2 3D, 3 cube), packed mips (11), **mip address, CPU virtual, bits 12-31** |

Addresses in the header are CPU virtual addresses (XPhysicalAlloc or game pointers).
SetTexture translates them for the GPU: `phys = (va & 0x1FFFFFFF) + (va >= 0xE0000000 ? 0x1000 : 0)`.

**SetTexture 837341F0 (dev, s, tex, bit)**: fc = dev+1152+24*s.

- dword0 = tex dword0 with bits 10-21 (clamp_x/y/z) kept from the device, so address modes are sampler state.
- dword1 = physical(tex dword1) with bit 11 (nearest clamp policy) from the device.
- dword2 = tex dword2.
- dword3 = tex dword3 with bits 19-30 (mag/min/mip/aniso/arbitrary filter) from the device.
- dword4 = tex dword4 with bits 0-1 and 10-31 from the device. mip_min_level = max(tex, MAXMIPLEVEL byte dev+11942+s), mip_max_level = min(tex, MINMIPLEVEL byte dev+11968+s).
- dword5 = physical(tex dword5 bits 9-28) with bits 0-8 (border colour, tri clamp, aniso bias) from the device.

The dirty bit is supplied by the caller in r6: **qword dev+24 bit (31-s)**, the same bit the
sampler-state setters compute (`(1<<63) >> (s+32)`). SetTexture(NULL) leaves the fetch constant
and the dirty mask unchanged and only clears the slot.

Surface (48 bytes): +0 Common type 4 (bit 31 = owns EDRAM tiles, bit 30 = texture level with
parent), +24 hi16 = MSAA type (bits 0-1) and width in EDRAM tile units, lo16 = tile count (or parent
pointer for level surfaces), +28 = RB_COLOR_INFO / RB_DEPTH_INFO (EDRAM base in bits 0-11; for level
surfaces, level in bits 28-31 and face in 22-27), +32 = HiZ word (depth), +36 = (w-1)<<18 \| (h-1)<<3,
+40 = D3DFORMAT.

## 3. Pending masks +0x10, +0x18, +0x20, +0x28

Read from the flush at the top of DrawVertices 8373C720, which runs before every draw and zeroes
each mask it handles. 837431A8(dev, mask << n, first reg, shadow) writes one register per set bit,
MSB first. "bit b <-> reg R" below means bit b set = re-send register R from its shadow.

**qword dev+0x10 (16)**

| Bits | Meaning | Shadow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0-11 | bit 11-k <-> reg 0x2200+k: 0x800 RB_DEPTHCONTROL, 0x400 RB_BLENDCONTROL0, 0x200 RB_COLORCONTROL, 0x100 RB_HIZCONTROL, 0x80 PA_CL_CLIP_CNTL, 0x40 PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL, 0x20 PA_CL_VTE_CNTL, 0x10 VGT_CURRENT_BIN_ID_MIN, 0x8 RB_MODECONTROL, 0x4/0x2/0x1 RB_BLENDCONTROL1/2/3 | dev+10548.. |
| 12-16 | bit 16-k <-> reg 0x2180+k: 0x10000 SQ_PROGRAM_CNTL, 0x8000 SQ_CONTEXT_MISC, 0x4000 SQ_INTERPOLATOR_CNTL, 0x2000 SQ_WRAPPING_0, 0x1000 SQ_WRAPPING_1 | dev+10528.. |
| 17-20 | derived state, resolved by 837442E0 before the register writes: 0x20000 depth/stencil/HiZ recompute (83742C10; set by ZENABLE, ZFUNC, stencil states, SetDepthStencilSurface), 0x40000 alpha test (ALPHATESTENABLE), 0x80000 vertex shader / declaration / stream stride changed, 0x100000 pixel shader changed. 837442E0 rebuilds SQ_PROGRAM_CNTL/CONTEXT_MISC/INTERPOLATOR, RB_MODECONTROL and RB_COLOR_INFO from dev+12688 (VS), 12684 (PS), 11812 (vdecl) and sets those bits | - |
| 21-41 | bit 41-k <-> reg 0x2100+k (k 0-20): VGT_MAX/MIN_VTX_INDX, VGT_INDX_OFFSET, IB reset index (bit 38), RB_COLOR_MASK (bit 37), RB_BLEND_RGBA (36-33), fog colour, RB_STENCILREFMASK_BF (0x20000000, bit 29), RB_STENCILREFMASK (bit 28), RB_ALPHA_REF (bit 27), viewport scale/offset PA_CL_VPORT_* (bits 26-21) | dev+10444.. |
| 42-57 | bit 57-k <-> reg 0x2000+k: RB_SURFACE_INFO (57), RB_COLOR_INFO (56), RB_DEPTH_INFO (55), RB_COLOR1-3_INFO (54-52), COHER_DEST_BASE_0-7, PA_SC_SCREEN_SCISSOR_TL/BR (43-42) | dev+10368.. |
| 58-63 | not consumed by the flush | - |

**qword dev+0x18 (24)**

| Bits | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0-31 | bit 31-k <-> fetch constant k (6 dwords at dev+1152+24k, written to regs 0x4800+6k by 837433E8). Texture sampler s = constant s, so bit 31-s. Vertex stream s uses fetch slot 95-s, i.e. constant (95-s)/3, so bit s/3 (streams 0-2 share bit 0) |
| 34-54 | bit 54-k <-> reg 0x2280+k (k 0-20): PA_SU_POINT_SIZE, POINT_MINMAX, LINE_CNTL, ..., VGT_HOS_CNTL (bit 49, D3DRS 228), tessellation levels, VGT_GROUP_*, PA_SC_VIZ_QUERY, VGT_ENHANCE; shadow dev+10596.. |
| 32-33, 55-63 | not consumed by the flush |

So part A's "high 32 bits = fetch constants" should read "low 32 bits". Part B's "1 bit per fetch slot from the top" was correct.

**qword dev+0x20 (32)**

| Bits | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0-37 | bit 37-k <-> reg 0x2300+k: PA_SC_LINE_CNTL, PA_SC_AA_CONFIG, PA_SU_VTX_CNTL, guard band, SQ_VS_CONST/SQ_PS_CONST, PA_SC_AA_MASK (bit 19, D3DRS 196 = MULTISAMPLEMASK), RB_COPY_* and clear registers, RB_SAMPLE_COUNT_*; shadow dev+10680.. |
| 38-45 | bit 45-k <-> reg 0x2380+k: PA_SU_POLY_OFFSET_FRONT/BACK_SCALE/OFFSET (depth bias), point radius/size/cull; shadow dev+10832.. |
| 49-54 | bit 54-k <-> user clip plane k, PA_CL_UCP_k_X..W (regs 0x2388+4k), written by 83743268 from dev+10272+16k |
| 56 | all bool and loop constants, regs 0x4900-0x4927 (40 dwords) from dev+10112 (0x2780) |
| others | not consumed by the flush |

**qword dev+0x28 (40)**: not a dirty mask. It is a filter on the +0x10 bits. At draw time
`if (dev[40] & dev[16]) 83742E10(...)` handles those registers through a special path (predicated
per-tile writes and HiZ) instead of a plain block write. Only three bits are ever set. 0x100
(RB_HIZCONTROL) is set or cleared by D3DRS 388, a HiZ-related state whose name is unverified.
1<<37 (RB_COLOR_MASK) and 1<<57 (RB_SURFACE_INFO) are set by BeginZPass 8374CF50. BeginZPass and
EndZPass 8374D1E0 are the only other writers (besides the default state setup 8373BAF0/837423D0).

**What a draw-time snapshot has to re-read.** The flush clears +0x00 ... +0x20 inside the draw, so
a hook that runs before the original draw sees the bits for this draw only. Since the game writes
many shadows inline (part B), a renderer should not try to track bits. The simpler rule:

- At every draw, read the full shadows: register blocks dev+10368 (0x2000-0x200F), 10444
  (0x2100-0x2114), 10528 (0x2180-0x2184), 10548 (0x2200-0x220B), 10596 (0x2280-0x2294), 10680
  (0x2300-0x2325), 10832 (0x2380-0x2387).
- Also read: fetch constants dev+1152 (32 x 24 bytes); VS/PS constants dev+0x780/0x1780; bool and
  loop constants dev+10112; clip planes dev+10272; bindings (VS 12688, PS 12684, vdecl 11812,
  streams 12452/12520, IB 12428, RT 12432-12444, DS 12448, textures 12536).
- Use the masks only as a cache hint: bit 31-k of +0x18 tells which fetch constants changed;
  +0x00 and +0x08 tell which shader constants changed.
- The derived bits 17-20 of +0x10 are resolved inside the draw (837442E0). A pre-draw read of
  RB_MODECONTROL / SQ_* / RB_COLOR_INFO can therefore be one shader change stale. Read those
  after the original flush runs, or derive them from the bound shaders yourself.
- Window scissor (0x2080-0x2082) does not go through any mask: SetScissorRect / SetViewport emit
  it directly (83734530). Take it from dev+12668 (rect), 11848 (enable) and 12640 (viewport).

## 4. Shader and declaration creation

| Function | Args as the game calls it | Pointer source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CreateVertexShader 8373B790 | r3 = const DWORD* shader container; returns D3DVertexShader* | .rdata, header 0x102A1101 |
| CreatePixelShader 8373B3C8 | r3 = const DWORD* shader container; returns D3DPixelShader* | .rdata, header 0x102A1100 |
| CreateVertexDeclaration 8373BBE0 | r3 = const D3DVERTEXELEMENT9* (ends with stream 0xFF); returns decl | .rdata or a stack array built at run time (837DBB18) |

None of the three take the device. The game reaches them two ways:

- **Directly** with an `lis/addi` constant in r3, for example 8361A508 (VS 0x821B33E8), 82806720,
  837DBB18 (VS 0x8206D2A8).
- **Through out-of-line HRESULT wrappers** `(dev r3, pFunction r4, ppOut r5)`. They do `mr r3,r4`,
  call the creator, store the result to *r5 and return E_OUTOFMEMORY on NULL:
  - 8231AD88 (VS, 23 callers), 82319CB0 (PS, 19), 8231ADE8 (decl, 8);
  - vtable-only copies 8377E648 / 8377E698 / 8377E6E8 (0 direct callers);
  - 82319D10 (PS, caller 822F3708).

Every pointer checked lands on a shader container in the .rdata range 0x8200AC88-0x82240698.

- 8231B208: base 0x8223FA80. VS at 0x8223E728 and 0x8223F1C0 (header `102A1101`), PS at 0x8223EBF0
  ... 0x8223FA80 (`102A1100`), decl at 0x8223FC70 (`{0,0,FLOAT3 0x2A23B9,...}{0,12,FLOAT2 0x2C23A5,...}`
  then `00FF0000` end).
- 83614B90: VS 0x821B5168, PS 0x821B5258.

So the creators can be hooked as in Unleashed (`CreateVertexShader(const be<uint32_t>* function)`).
The container address works as a stable key for precompiled host shaders, which fits XenosRecomp's
container scan (tools/extract_shaders.py). Not all 50 call sites were read. Shaders built from
loaded files, if any, would show up as heap pointers.

## Corrections to parts A and B

- B: CreateTexture's arguments are (w, h, depth, levels, usage, format, pool, type). 83741B08 passes
  (w, h, 1, 1, 0, fmt, 0, 3), and r10 = 3 is D3DRTYPE_TEXTURE, not a pool.
- A: fetch-constant dirty bits are the low 32 bits of dev+0x18 (bit 31-k), not the high 32.
- B: +0x28 is not a register-block dirty mask (section 3).
- 83734810 is the inner viewport setter (float args). 83736EC8 is the public SetViewport(D3DVIEWPORT9*).
- 83736F48 is the full SetStreamSource. Part A's 83737950 is a separate partial one (no stride or pointer).

## Open questions

- 83730408-83732248 (the 0x7880-byte object) is unidentified. It is outside D3D, but its callers
  (823F09C0, 82455D40, 8246A500, ...) were not traced.
- 83733628's stack arguments s84-s124 (border, exp bias, pitch) are read from slot order, not from
  a caller passing distinct values. 83732898's exact XG name is a guess.
- Texture vs cube alias for 83732DB8 / 83733E28 is unproven (they behave the same).
- D3DRS 304 = VIEWPORTENABLE and the state at 388 (HiZ-related) are named from the 360 enum order
  as remembered, not from a header.
- Bits not consumed by the DrawVertices flush (+0x10 58-63, +0x18 32-33/55-63, +0x20 46-48/55/57-63)
  may be used by other draw paths (BeginVertices, DrawIndexedVertices 8373CB08, Resolve). Not checked.
- Which of the 8382C738-8385E620 functions are XGraphics and which are D3DX was not established.
```

`docs/menus.md`:

```md
# Menus (notes for RECOMP SETTINGS)

Goal: the title menu's "Xbox LIVE Marketplace" becomes "RECOMP SETTINGS",
opening pages of ours in the game's own Options menu (as the NGB recomp does).

## Title menu

- Selection handler: `sub_8364D0C0` (ng2_recomp.499.cpp). Menu state at
  0x83386F10: entry count +0x15F0, cursor +0x15F4, entries from +0x814,
  0x140 bytes each; an entry's first word is its action type, dispatched
  through the jump table at 0x8364D284.
- Action types: 0 NEW GAME (screen 2), 1 LOAD GAME (screen 1, or message 10
  when signed out), 2 probably MISSIONS (screen 6), 3 LEADERBOARDS (7 / 11),
  4 NINJA CINEMA (8 / 12), 5 OPTIONS (screen 9), 6 Xbox LIVE Marketplace
  (XamShowMarketplaceUI via thunk 0x8380DEF8 when signed in, else message 13).
- Screens and messages open through `sub_8364CFC8(*(menu + 4), id)`;
  `sub_8364CA08` is the signed-in check.
- Plan: when type 6 is chosen, open screen 9 (Options) in a "recomp
  settings" mode instead of message 13.

## Labels

- Title entries are pictures: one 520x990 8-bit atlas (EXIT DEMO, NEW GAME,
  LOAD GAME, LEADERBOARDS, NINJA CINEMA, OPTIONS, MISSIONS, the difficulty
  names) and a separate 520x90 texture for "Xbox LIVE Marketplace", drawn by
  the generic sprite renderer (`837DCCB0` <- `8366BED8` <- `8366CF54` <-
  `8366B1E8`). Every letter of RECOMP SETTINGS is in the atlas, so the new
  label can be composed at runtime from the game's own glyphs (no shipped
  art), e.g. in the renderer when the label texture's content hash is seen.

## Options screen

- Categories: Game Settings, Controller Settings, Camera Settings, Screen
  Settings, Audio Settings, Copyright Information, Restore Defaults, Return
  to Main Menu. Rows are two-choice toggles or "<- value ->" lists.
- Its text is a UTF-16BE string table loaded from other.ng2 (physical
  0xC454D70 onwards in one run): preceded by a table of byte lengths, so
  strings are referenced by index. Still to map: the screen's update/draw
  code, its page and row structures, and how a row names its strings.

## Options screen internals (mapped 10-29)

- Screens live in a manager (one at 0x852E1428 in a run) as 8-byte objects
  at mgr+8*k; `sub_8364C6F0(mgr, id)` maps an id to its object (jump table
  at 0x8364C708), `sub_8364CFC8` pushes it on a stack at mgr+136 (count at
  +48) and calls vtable[1] (enter); vtable[2] is the per-frame update.
  Title menu: vtable 0x82280014, update `sub_8364D0C0`. Options (id 9,
  mgr+0x48): vtable 0x822800C8, enter `sub_8364DDF8` (sets the UI mode word
  at 0x83386F10+12 to 11; leave sets 5), update `sub_8364DEF0`.
- The Options pages are an object-oriented widget framework: widgets are
  built by constructors such as `sub_836ACF70` (the controller diagram,
  storing the label table 0x83BB8D18 / 0x83BB8E20 in the object) and keep
  string pointers resolved at runtime.
- Option strings: table 2, id 0x00020000 + index; the strings are stored
  back to back, each padded to 16 bytes, from "Game Settings" (index 0).
  0x0002009B is "Quick Attack". A grid of row string ids (Aspect Ratio
  16:9/4:3, Color/Monochrome, Gamma, Brightness...) sits at 0x83A936D8 in
  the image but nothing reads it after boot (gdb hardware watchpoints never
  fired there, nor on a known-read address: they don't work on this binary).
- Cheapest native path found so far: reuse existing pages in "recomp mode",
  rewriting their strings in place (same padded slot sizes) and mapping our
  settings onto the rows' values, restoring both on leaving.

## Options state (10-29)

- 0x83CEB414: the selected category (0 Game Settings, 1 Controller, 2
  Camera, ...); 0x83CEB418 + 4 * category: that page's cursor row.
- Option values are not in the image's data: changing 1st/3rd-Person Camera
  Controls or Subtitles changed no word there; heap and physical diffs
  showed no clean candidate either (they may live in widget objects, or be
  committed on leaving the page).
- Page layouts: Camera Settings has two four-choice rows (Default /
  Vertical Inverted / Horizontal Inverted / All Inverted) and two sliders;
  Game Settings has a language list, a two-choice row and five On/Off-style
  rows; Screen Settings: Aspect Ratio, Video Adjustment, "???"; Audio: three
  sliders, Speaker Output (5.1 / Stereo), "???".

## Options pages (mapped 10-29, second pass)

- Page handlers (input, per frame): 0 category list `sub_823E5B60`, 1 Game
  `sub_823E6490`, 2 Controller `6AD8`, 3 Camera `7040`, 4 Screen `74E8`, 5
  Audio `5DB8`, 7 `80B8`, 11 `7A18`; 0xFF (the list's Back) ends the loop.
  0x83CEB3FC is the page before this frame, 0x83CEB400 the depth, and
  0x83CEB414 + 4 * page each page's cursor. The loop runs the handler only
  while the menu model's event is idle (`sub_836827B0`).
- Handler helpers: `sub_823E3448(*0x84F41264, pad byte 0x84B5030A, 1, 0,
  dir)` a direction (0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left); `sub_823E3D78(&pad,
  cursor, enabled[], 0)` Confirm; `sub_823E3ED0(&pad, cursor, n, 0)` Back;
  `sub_823E3FD0(&pad)` Y (a row's default); `sub_82429DA8(id)` with f1 =
  *(float*)0x8206EE58 a sound (2 cursor, 3 choice).
- `sub_83682750(n, flag)`: transition table at 0x82181618 on the model
  0x85313E30 (5 stores the choice direction flag at model+0x380, 6 enter,
  7 back); `sub_83681830(model, lastPage, page, cursors, values, n)` keeps
  cursors and values as (current, previous) pairs (values of page p at
  0x85313EB0 + 0x40 * p) and raises page / cursor / value events.
- Page builders run once as Options opens; the category list's is
  `sub_836B10B8` (label ids as data at +0x34...), the Game page's
  `sub_836AC710` (vtable 0x822810F4). A choice row is a widget whose
  choices are added with `sub_836AA270(widget, string id)` (two per line,
  so any count works), then `sub_836AB540(page, label id, widget)` appends
  it as the next row. widget+0x14 is the selected choice (first set from
  the model at build), +0x600 = 1 marks the game's On/Off rows, whose value
  1 is the first choice.

## RECOMP SETTINGS (built 10-29, reworked twice the same day)

- src/recomp_settings.cpp: sub_8364CFC8 turns the Marketplace message (13)

  track name slots (0x63-0x96); "Total Play Time" is blanked and the play

- Title menu (sub_8364CBE8, entries of 0x140 bytes from 0x85387600: action
  +0x124, place +0x128, Xbox LIVE flag +0x130): LEADERBOARDS removed, our

- The Options header ("OPTIONS", a 172x58 8-bit picture, hash

  fullscreen plus exclusive_fullscreen, the SDL display mode set first on

  mailbox, FIFO relaxed through plume's setPresentMode), Show FPS.
- Graphics also has Anti-Aliasing (antialiasing: 0, 2, 4, 8 samples for
  the targets the game multisamples, its 1120x584 main picture at 2x;
  stepped down to what the device supports; list made at Game page +0xA60).
- In gameplay, Back opens "IN-GAME MANUAL AND OPTIONS"; Start the
  inventory. The list's strings are table 4 (0x40000 + index: 0 View
  In-Game Manual ... 22 Quit Game, 23 NINJA CINEMA, 24 Return to Game).

- RECOMP SETTINGS there is shown after Save Method: rows are drawn at the
  place their index gives them (set at setup, vt slot 0), so ours and

- RECOMP SETTINGS there (src/recomp_settings.cpp, end): a 13th row (label

- Since 10-31 the in-game RECOMP SETTINGS is laid out as the title's: the

## Other languages (11-05)

The game has ten text languages; its text lookup sub_837578C8(language, id)
numbers them 0 Japanese, 1 English, 2 French, 3 German, 4 Italian, 5 Spanish,
6 Traditional Chinese, 7 Korean, 8 Polish, 9 Russian (sub_8367F948 gives the
current one; the console's user_language 9 and 10, Portuguese and Simplified
Chinese, fall back to English).
- RECOMP SETTINGS' texts: our strings are made once in guest memory, and the
  lookup's hook (src/storage_prompt.cpp) hands them out for the Options
  table's ids ours uses (spare ids from 0x20063, the categories, the play time
  name, the note slot), in every language and with no room needed.
- "Change Storage Device": per id, the English text is looked up once; where
  it has "@[pad:..] Change Storage Device", that button's segment (tag to next
  tag) is cut from whichever language's string is handed out.
- The title menu's entries are pictures in every language: one 520x990 atlas
  and a 520x90 Marketplace label per language, all in Main_Menu.spr, which is
  loaded whole, so the English atlas is in memory whatever the language
  (0x1037A000 with this game's packages). Another language's atlas has the
  English one found by the hash of its first 4 KB as stored, decoded alike,
  and its letters make RECOMP SETTINGS and EXIT GAME (src/gpu/menu_label.cpp
  lists each language's atlas, label and Options header hashes). The in-game
  list's header differs per language too (600x58 in most; its hashes are
  listed as well). Korean's
  Options header isn't one of these pictures and stays Korean.
```

`docs/ngb-reuse.md`:

```md
# What to take from the Ninja Gaiden Black port

Survey of ~/ngb-recomp (2026-10-28) for reuse here. NGB is GPL-3.0-or-later
(its xboxrecomp runtime is MIT with LGPL/GPL xemu parts); NG2 can take its
code once NG2 is GPL-3.0-or-later as well.

Worth taking, best first:

1. Windows cross build: `packaging/windows/build.sh`, `deps.txt`,
   `dlldeps.py`, `cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-llvm-mingw.cmake`, `ngb.rc`,
   manifest, icon. llvm-mingw + MSYS2 CLANG64 sysroot, DLL discovery, zip with
   licences. Adapt (names, SDL3). Check ReXGlue builds with mingw first.
2. AppImage: `packaging/appimage/build.sh` and `Dockerfile` (Ubuntu 22.04,
   static libstdc++, "never bundle" list, patchelf, zsync updates). Adapt:
   SDL3, no glib/epoxy; keep the Qt dialog layer (no GTK: the user prefers Qt).
3. Disc install: `src/install.c` (already handles the XGD2 offset, .7z/.zip,
   `.partial` install dirs, zenity/kdialog/GetOpenFileName pickers). Adapt the
   XBE check to an XEX/title ID check (544307D5); replaces
   `tools/xdvdfs_extract.py` for players.
4. Config/save/log dirs and portable mode (`portable.txt`): `src/port.h`,
   `src/main.c`. Copy with renames, after checking ReXGlue's own paths.
5. Test rig: headless gamescope and Proton (umu-run) scripts, the timed/live
   pad-file input parser (`xboxrecomp/src/usb/usb_gamepad.c`, ~200 lines of
   plain C) to wire into ReXGlue's input layer, save loaders. NG2 has no
   input injection yet; this is the piece needed to test past the title.
6. Rebindable controls (`src/bindings.c`, `keyboard.c`, `controls.ini`) and
   Xelu button prompt art (CC0, `assets/prompts/`).
7. Settings list and ini format (Graphics/Display/Sound/Gameplay/Cheats/
   Controls pages). NGB's menus patch the game's own menu engine; NG2 would
   build them in ImGui like Unleashed, so only the list and the ini carry over.
8. Ideas only: widescreen HUD anchoring heuristics (docs/TECHNICAL.md), the
   F7 draw trace, cheats/memdump hooks (`src/cheats.c`), issue templates.

Not applicable: the x86 lifter and xboxrecomp runtime, the NV2A/D3D8 renderer
(`src/d3d`), Morton swizzle, DirectSound/APU audio.

Things to look for in NG2 because NGB had them: a fixed render-node pool
(NGB's HUD vanished in busy fights), play-time cap.

```

`docs/renderer-plan.md`:

```md
# Native renderer plan

Goal: draw NG2 with Vulkan from hooked D3D calls, in the spirit of Unleashed
Recompiled's `gpu/video.cpp` (plume RHI, Vulkan only), instead of emulating
the Xenos GPU. It draws by default; ReXGlue's xenos plugin (`NG2_RENDERER=xenos
--gpu_plugin=xenos`) stays as the reference picture.

## Architecture (as built)

- **The game's D3D library keeps running.** Much of NG2's D3D use is inlined
  in game code (vertex declarations, streams, constants written straight into
  the device), so hooking setters alone would miss state. Instead the library
  runs unmodified. Since 2026-11-03 there is no GPU emulation at all: no GPU
  plugin is loaded (src/gpu/native_gpu.cpp is the graphics system). Direct3D's
  command stream is reported consumed at each kick and never read; what the
  game can see of the GPU (fences, the callback handshakes, the flip and its
  vsync wait, vblank interrupts) is done at the Direct3D calls that ask for it
  (InsertFence 8375F810, the handshake 8375FD30, the flip 8376A518; TU3
  addresses). Before that the xenos plugin's null backend (SDK patch 0001)
  parsed the ring for them: about 5% of the CPU in a fight.
- **The renderer hooks the points where work happens** (src/gpu/d3d_hooks.cpp):
  DrawVertices 8373C720, DrawIndexedVertices 8373CB08, BeginVertices
  8373BD50, BeginIndexedVertices 8373C1F0, Clear 837390C8, Resolve 8373D570,
  Swap 837452C0. Each calls the original, then reads the device.
- **State comes from the device's GPU register shadows**, which the D3D
  setters keep in Xenos register format (dev+0x2880 + 4*(reg-0x2000):
  RB_COLOR_INFO, RB_DEPTHCONTROL, RB_BLENDCONTROL, PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL,
  viewport and scissor registers, ...), the fetch constants (dev+0x480, 32 x
  24 bytes: textures and vertex streams), the shader objects (dev+0x3190 VS,
  dev+0x318C PS), the float constants (dev+0x780, dev+0x1780) and bool
  constants (dev+0x2780). Xenos semantics are documented in ReXGlue's
  include/rex/graphics/xenos.h and registers; this keeps the translation
  independent of D3D enums.
- **Shaders** are translated ahead of time (docs/shaders.md); the renderer
  maps a shader object to its cache entry by hashing the container the game
  passed to CreateVertexShader/CreatePixelShader (hook those).
- **Presentation**: Vulkan device and swapchain on the game window through
  plume (patched for Wayland, patches/plume), Wayland or X11.

## Status (2026-10-28)

The title screen renders natively and matches the xenos reference:
render targets, Clear, Resolve (copy, MSAA resolve, format conversion by
draw), Swap/present, draws (DrawVertices, DrawIndexedVertices, inline
BeginVertices/BeginIndexedVertices), shaders from the ahead-of-time cache,
2D/1D textures (base level), rect lists (geometry shader), quad lists.
Debug aids: NG2_TRACE_FRAME=<n>[+count] (ng2.log rotates at 5 MB: read ng2.1.log first), NG2_DUMP_TEXTURES=<dir> (DXT as DDS),
NG2_DEBUG_WHITE_TEXTURES=1.

## Next

- Gameplay: test runs can now press buttons (NG2_PAD_SCRIPT/NG2_PAD_LIVE).
  Start, A x3 reaches the Chapter 1 card and the first 3D scene renders;
  next is comparing in-game frames with xenos.
- Performance (2026-10-28): the opening cutscene runs at 60 fps with
  ~650 draws and ~33 resolves a frame (NG2_PROFILE=1: about 150 ms a second
  in the renderer on the game thread). Guest memory is synced only for the
  fetch constants a shader reads (XenosRecomp's per-shader mask plus the
  declaration's streams). A range unchanged for a frame is checked once a
  frame; one that changed recently (dynamic buffers filled in batches) on
  every draw; inline data always. Not handled: overlapping ranges with
  separate hashes, CPU uploads overwriting memexport results, more than 16
  declared elements.
- The xenos plugin draws the in-game cutscene black (only the credits), so
  in-game frames have no emulated reference; judge them on their own.
- Depth resolves: copied by a draw (sample 0 when multisampled) into
  R32_FLOAT. Resolved textures are keyed by address and shape (two shadow
  map sizes share an address), with the latest resolve per address as a
  fallback for other views.
- Multiple render targets: targets 0-3 while they match target 0's shape,
  per-target format, blend and color mask; a target the pixel shader
  doesn't write keeps its contents. Clear handles targets 1-3.
- EDRAM aliasing, first step: surfaces are keyed by host format, so guest
  formats sharing one (2_10_10_10_FLOAT and its AS_16_16_16_16 view, the two
  depth formats) share a texture; the main pass draws through both. Not
  handled: overlapping surfaces of different sizes or host formats.
- Movies (src/movie, 2026-10-28): the XMedia2 player is replaced by host
  decoding (FFmpeg) behind the player's method wrappers; the original's GPU
  assisted WMV decoder stalled or cut movies short. The stand-in has to
  make the original's physical allocations at create: without them the
  title movie's texture setup clears the archive's table of contents
  (0xEBEB0000, a latent game bug the original layout hides) and the title
  never loads its font and sprites. Full-screen movies (+80, drawn by the
  player itself) are not drawn yet.
- Opening stalls (fixed 2026-10-28): (1) ~97 s, the game's job system lost
  a wake-up: ReXGlue's semaphores gave released units to whoever looked
  first and SignalAndWait wasn't atomic (patches/rexglue-sdk/0005);
  NG2_DEBUG_WAITS=1 (src/debug_waits.cpp) found it. (2) ~139 s, a GPU
  hang: a vertex fetch with a garbage index read past the 512 MB guest
  memory buffer (page fault, ring timeout); addresses now wrap at 512 MB
  (patches/xenosrecomp/0003). The opening now plays into gameplay.
- Gameplay (Chapter 1 start) renders: Ryu, enemies, level, HUD, blood.
  The "missing characters" were a depth bug: the game uses a reversed
  viewport depth range (negative zScale) and the renderer sorted min/max,
  so far geometry won over near. The range now goes to Vulkan as is.
  Still to check: distant buildings look flat and untextured.
  NG2_DEBUG_HIGHLIGHT=<vs hash> or cycle:<seconds> paints a vertex
  shader's draws magenta (finding which draws are which); =all paints each
  skinned vertex shader in its own color (legend in the log).
- Characters (10-29): faces and clothes showed their insides because the
  cull mapping assumed plume's front face was counter-clockwise (it is
  clockwise; Xenos's is counter-clockwise unless PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL.face).
  Hair was black where a 1x1 tint texture read as black: small textures
  with packed mips keep their base level in the mip tail, and base rows
  are aligned to 32 blocks. Draws without a pixel shader (depth only) are drawn now.
- Gameplay (10-29): textures have their mips now (Xenia's guest layout), so
  distant windows and floors no longer shimmer; shadow casters get the
  game's polygon offset (no acne). Lines at the HUD's edges were the last
  row of tiled textures cut off: a tiled level can reach past pitch x rows
  (Xenia's GetTiledAddressUpperBound2D). Not done: anisotropy (not enabled
  on the device) and per-fetch LOD overrides (XenosRecomp samples with
  implicit LOD).
- Brightness (10-29): the whole picture was brighter than Xenia (menu
  included) because the display gamma table was never applied. D3D's
  SetGammaRamp leaves it at dev+0x3A8C (3 x 256 u16, already adjusted for the
  BT.709 display the kernel reports); the present shader applies it. 7e3
  render targets resolve through a shader that clamps and rounds to 7e3 and
  2-bit alpha (no visible change here). Not done: the PWL form of the table
  (10-bit front buffers), blend constants (plume pipelines keep them at 0).
- Settings (10-29), as cvars in ng2.toml or on the command line:
  render_scale 1-4 (render targets and their resolves at that many times the
  game's size; guest pixel values scaled where they reach the host; shaders
  see guest pixels and texels via XenosRecomp patch 0007; changes apply
  between frames), vsync, anisotropic_filtering (-1 game, 0 off, 1-5 for
  1x-16x). The present shader box-filters a front buffer bigger than the
  window. bloom 0/1/2 (off, half, on) acts on the bloom texture read from
  slot 1 by tone mapping (ps 2CB124864F1A4460) and the final composite (ps
  EAE805C57979C8A5); the temporal pass still reads it all. half_pixel_offset
  moves geometry half a pixel for D3D pixel centers (default on, as Xenia).
- The xenos plugin draws the in-game 3D black (only the HUD shows), so it
  is no reference for gameplay either.
- Movie audio is pushed as it decodes, paced by the video queue (about
  200 ms ahead): a long hitch underruns it and audio then trails video.
- Resolved textures are never freed (one per address and shape); a later
  CPU texture at a once-resolved address keeps sampling the GPU copy.
- The opening still looks dim and flat; with no emulated reference in-game,
  check against captures from hardware.
- Mipmaps, cube and 3D textures, the formats that need conversion
  (5_6_5, 1_5_5_5, 4_4_4_4, 2_10_10_10, 10_11_11, 11_11_10).
- Depth resolves, polygon offset, MSAA
  alpha-to-coverage, gamma (k_8_8_8_8_GAMMA, PWL ramp).
- EDRAM aliasing between surfaces that share EDRAM (Xenia's render target
  cache is the reference).
- Performance: done. Vulkan work on a thread of ours (11-03), textures and vertex ranges
  rechecked less often (see the sections below).
- Review notes for the present path (window size on the UI thread, acquire
  timeout, window handle from ReXGlue).
- From the draw path review (2026-10-28), not done yet:
  - guest memory sync: only the fetch constants the shader reads, dirty-page
    tracking instead of hashing, ranges written by memory export owned by
    the GPU (a CPU upload must not overwrite skinning results);
  - textures: eviction, cheaper invalidation than hashing every frame,
    resolved textures should honour the fetch's swizzle/format, depth
    resolves, Resolve's level/slice arguments (r8/r9);
  - blend constant color, alpha test function, RB_STENCILREFMASK_BF,
    stencil reference out of the pipeline key, quad strips and indexed quad
    lists, signed texture components, packed mip tails;
  - Present holds the renderer mutex through swapchain acquire;
  - pipelines are created on the game thread (hitches until a pipeline
    cache exists). Fixed since: async_pipelines.

Audio: ReXGlue's SDL3 output with its XMA decoder (libavcodec); Unleashed's
SDL driver only if this turns out worse.

License: copying Unleashed code makes this project GPL-3.0-or-later
(Unleashed is GPL-3.0; ReXGlue is BSD-3-Clause; plume and XenosRecomp MIT).

## Stutter: pipelines (10-30)

- log_hitches (or NG2_HITCHES=1) logs frames over 25 ms (and 1.6x the one
  before: cutscenes run at 30 fps) with the time per renderer stage and what
  was made. On a first run (no driver cache) the level load spent 764 ms
  making 62 pipelines and new areas 75-600 ms; single pipelines take 17-75
  ms on RADV. Textures were small by comparison.
- Pipelines are now made on worker threads (async_pipelines, on by default):
  a draw whose pipeline isn't made yet is left out until it is (a frame or
  two). Every pipeline key made is appended to ng2-pipelines.bin next to the
  config (header "NG2P", version, key size; whole 96-byte keys, a torn last
  one trimmed), and those are asked of the workers at start, behind any a
  draw needs. With the list from one run, the next had no pipeline hitches.
- Left: game-side frames (loading, renderer ~1 ms) and the title's label
  drawing from the atlas glyphs (~48 ms once).

## Performance against GPU emulation and Xenia (10-30)

Same scene (Chapter 1's first fight, from the scripted pad), headless gamescope 1280x720, RX 9070
(RADV), 30 s windows; GPU busy from amdgpu's gpu_busy_percent (the desktop adds about 5%), CPU from
the process's /proc time. All ran at 60 fps (Xenia's not logged, held visually).

| | GPU 1x | GPU 3x | CPU cores 1x / 3x |
|---|---|---|---|
| native (NG2_RENDERER=native, render_scale) | 13% | 21% | 3.04 / 2.78 |
| recomp on the xenos plugin (draw_resolution_scale) | 80% | 85% | 3.49 / 3.43 |
| Xenia Edge (draw_resolution_scale) | 18% | 54% | 2.35 / 2.34 |

Scripts: a sampler following the test run's own process (the player's game may run too), the
recomp's pad script, and for Xenia xdotool keys inside gamescope (`--keybind_a=J`: the default A key,
semicolon, doesn't reach it there; its sign-in prompt is Right, Return). The SDK's GPU emulation is
much heavier than current Xenia Edge; the recomp's own CPU time is higher than Xenia's (its threads
spin more), worth a look. Fixed since: see Threads and the Steam Deck (0.4 cores against
Xenia's 2.3).

CPU (10-30): the recomp used more than Xenia because the game's D3D wait for
the GPU (sub_8373A4D0, stepping sub_83737AE0 until the GPU's read pointer
passes a fence) spins until the next vblank, a whole core on the title screen
(95% of one thread, per perf -t). After 64 steps each step now sleeps 100 us:
title 106% -> 16% of a core, the Chapter 1 fight 3.04 -> 2.36 cores, still 60
fps.

## Audio stopping in play (10-30)

The sound sometimes stopped for good while the game ran on: two threads spun
forever in XAudio2's voice processing barrier (sub_8374F078, from
sub_8374EF40: the main pass sub_8374E740/EDE8 and a worker sub_8374E808).
Each thread sets its processor's byte (PCR r13+0x10C) in a 64-bit mask and
waits for it to hold all of them; the first to see that clears it. A thread
only left on seeing the mask whole or zero, so if the OS paused it there, the
other could clear the mask, start the next pass and set its byte in the same
mask again first, leaving both waiting (the console's hardware threads aren't
paused). The hook in d3d_hooks.cpp lets a thread also leave once its own byte
is cleared (only a completed barrier does that) and clears with a CAS from the
whole value it saw. Caught in a gdb soak 5 min in (tools: a watcher signalling
SIGUSR1 to gdb when two threads spin 30 s); two 30-min soaks clean after.
The barrier hook uses byte accesses only (the masks are 4 mod 8: an 8-byte
lock could split a cache line, which Linux may throttle): only the lowest
taking part clears, a byte at a time, its own last. Another 30-min soak clean.
Test audio (NG2_TEST_AUDIO=disk) is ~70 MB a minute: keep it off a full /tmp.

Latency (NG2_LATENCY_LOG=1, frame start to present, Chapter 1 fight): 16.63 ms
average, 18.75 worst with the GPU-wait sleep, 16.63 / 18.60 spinning; CPU 2.36
vs 3.03 cores. On Windows the sleep is a yield (a sleep there is >= 1 ms).

## Renderer CPU (11-03)

Measured in Chapter 1's first fight on a 9800X3D (NG2_PROFILE, ms of each second): the draw stage
162 -> 51, resolve 36 -> 5.5. What did it:
- each shader's float constants and texture slots, recorded by XenosRecomp (patch 0011): a draw
  byte-swaps only the constant registers its shaders read (median 10 of 480) and looks up only the
  slots they sample (1.06 on average, against every slot holding a texture before);
- a per-frame memo of texture lookups by fetch constant (a resolve forgets only the textures at its
  destination, found by base address);
- textures unchanged for 120 frames re-hashed every 8th frame they're drawn with, vertex ranges
  unchanged for 600 frames compared every 4th frame (a rewrite in place after that shows up to that
  many frames late);
- resolve destinations' guest memory hashed by sample (first and last 4 KB and 64 pieces);
- guest reads translated inline.

## Threads and the Steam Deck (11-03 to 11-04)

On the Steam Deck (4 cores, 8 threads) frame drops came from the game's render thread running out
of time, not the GPU (it waited ~0 ms on the GPU). Measured with the per-thread line of
NG2_PROFILE; in a heavy fight frame the renderer's share was 12-21 ms.
- Busy-waits that held cores: the game's main loop handing frames to the render thread
  (sub_822F34C0), the render thread's vblank limiter (sub_822F0BF8), the SDK's alertable waits (a
  sub-millisecond timeout rounded down to 0) and its timer queue (SDK patch 0014): they now pause, yield and sleep.
- Guest registers as locals in the generated code (ng2_codegen.toml, SDK patch 0015 keeps the
  vector registers some functions take from their callers shared): main thread -40%.
- The Vulkan work on a thread of ours ("Render Commands"): the hooks still read guest memory on
  the game's render thread, everything for Vulkan is queued (a RenderCommandList that copies its
  arguments) and replayed there.
- D3D's writers of constant packets (sub_83767670, sub_83767A10) are skipped with the native
  renderer: nothing reads its command stream any more.
- The texture memo indexed by address: a resolve (about 30 a frame) no longer walks the whole memo.
  The stage timers read the CPU's time stamp counter instead of clock_gettime.
- File reads the game asks to be asynchronous run on an I/O thread (SDK patch 0016): with reads
  slowed to SD card speed, Chapter 1's loading hitches went from 33 (3 s) to 3 (0.1 s).
- Untiling a run of texels at a time: a 1280x720 8-bit texture 4.9 -> 0.55 ms.
What's left on the Deck: the game itself only starts a frame on a vblank, so a frame that needs
more than 16.7 ms is shown for 33; heavy effects (fire, many particles) still do that for a second
or two. Tried and dropped: zero-copy guest memory (fences, inline vertices and memory export would
all have to change, for ~10-15%), checking long-unchanged vertex ranges less often at the end of a
frame (a pooled buffer reused mid-frame would draw stale for up to 8 frames).

Compared on the desktop on 11-04 (README table): same Chapter 1 fight, headless gamescope at
1280x720, over 30 s the card's power (hwmon power1_average; 27-33 W idle) and the game process's CPU
time. The port: 40 W / 57 W at 1x / 3x, 0.4 cores. Xenia Edge: 51 W / 84 W, 2.3 cores. GPU busy %
(gpu_busy_percent) was dropped: at light loads it follows the clock more than the work (both read
15% at 1x). Xenia's first-start dialogs (profile, "add games") come in a varying order, so its runs
start from a folder where they were already answered, and the keys wait for the storage dialog by
screenshot: runs on fixed timings drifted at 3x, and those froze in cutscenes (Xenia's watchdog
showed every guest thread blocked).

On the Steam Deck (11-04, LCD, Game Mode, battery, sound on, the same fight, 30 s; Steam's overlay
logging via mangohudctl set log_session, an output_folder added to its runtime config): port 60.0 fps
average, 1% low 55.4, 0.1% low 52.6, CPU 32%, GPU 48% (7 W), Deck 11 W from the battery; Xenia Edge
(e9a7e47 Linux AppImage) 58.2 / 27.5 / 18.1, CPU 51%, GPU 81% (15 W), Deck 22 W. The port's window
ran into the end of the fight (lighter last seconds). Xenia was driven by XTest keys from Python
(CachyOS's xdotool needs a newer CPU than the Deck's) and starts with a small picture under
--fullscreen in Game Mode until F11 is pressed twice; its storage prompt needs a real A press.

## Draw worker (NG2_DRAW_WORKER=1, off by default; 11-04)

The game's render thread records each Direct3D call and a worker draws them (src/gpu/video.cpp, "The
draw worker"). On the Steam Deck the game's render thread went from about 675 to 400 ms of CPU a
second and play hitches from 9-13 to 2.5 a minute. Known limits before it can be the default:
- an immediate-mode draw (BeginVertices) of over 2 MB of vertices or indices doesn't fit the
  staging half and is dropped (none seen in Chapter 1);
- a GPU step (a fence, the handshake) made on another thread than the one with an inline draw
  pending counts the calls before that draw only: its fence could signal before the draw's data
  was copied.
```

`docs/shaders.md`:

```md
# Shaders

NG2's shaders are translated ahead of time, as Unleashed Recompiled does it:
XenosRecomp turns each Xbox 360 shader container into HLSL and DXC compiles
that to SPIR-V. The result is linked into the executable as a zstd-compressed
cache (`ng2_shaders`, from `src/gpu/shader_cache.h`), and the renderer looks
shaders up by the XXH3 hash of the guest container. No DXIL: Vulkan only.

## Where the shaders are

All 663 containers (426 vertex, 237 pixel; 625 distinct) are in the XEX's
read-only data, 0x8200AC88-0x82240698. The `.ng2` archives contain none that a
byte scan can see, but they mix raw and compressed blocks; the renderer's
CreateVertexShader/CreatePixelShader hooks must report any hash missing from
the cache, so a shader that only appears at runtime is noticed.

## Build

`CMakeLists.txt` does it on every build where the inputs changed:

1. `ng2_dump_image` loads `game_files/default.xex` with ReXGlue in tool mode
   and writes the decrypted, decompressed image (identical to the one the game
   runs with).
2. XenosRecomp (built as an ExternalProject from `thirdparty/XenosRecomp`,
   upstream 990d03b plus `patches/xenosrecomp/`) scans it and writes
   `shaders/ng2_shader_cache.cpp` in the build directory. Any shader that fails
   to compile fails the build.

`NG2_GAME_DIR` points at another extraction of the game.

Debugging single shaders: `tools/extract_shaders.py <image> <dir>` writes each
container to its own file; `XenosRecomp <file> <out.hlsl> shader_common.h`
translates one.

## What NG2 needed beyond Unleashed

The patch (`patches/xenosrecomp/0001-*.patch`):

- Memory export. 64 vertex shaders are GPU passes drawn one vertex per output
  (skinning and the like): they read their inputs by index and write results
  with `eA`/`eM#` exports, which later draws use as vertex buffers. Ported
  from Xenia's SPIR-V translator (format packing, endian swap, bounds).
- Raw vertex fetches: 330 vertex shaders fetch without a declared vertex
  element; those fetches read guest memory through the vertex fetch
  constants. Full fetches latch the index for the mini fetches after them.
- The vertex index in r0.x, as the hardware provides it (Unleashed only
  needed it for instancing).
- Bool-conditional exec blocks (`cexec`) were run unconditionally upstream;
  NG2 has about 4000 of them.
- Bool constants as the hardware addresses them: 256 bits (VS b0-127, PS
  b128-255). Unleashed packed 16 per stage; NG2 uses at least b33 and
  unnamed ones.
- 32 texture fetch slots (vertex textures use s16/s17) and 1D textures,
  sampled as Nx1 2D textures. Vertex shaders sample mip 0.
- No vertex input attributes: every vertex fetch reads guest memory. Fetches
  of declared elements are placeholders in the microcode (D3D patches them
  from the vertex declaration on the console), so the renderer supplies each
  element slot's fetch constant, offset, stride and format at draw time.
- An NDC transform in every vertex shader (identity with the hardware
  viewport transform, pixels to NDC without it).
- Interpolator order TEXCOORD0-7, COLOR0-1, TEXCOORD8-15, so the rectangle
  list geometry shader can pass what pixel shaders read (TEXCOORD0-7,
  COLOR0-1) within 64 input components.

## Contract with the renderer

Push constants are three GPU addresses (vertex constants, pixel constants,
shared constants), as in Unleashed. Shared constants, in bytes:

| Offset | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | texture descriptor indices, `[2D, 3D, Cube, 1D][32 slots]` (uint) |
| 512 | sampler descriptor indices `[32]` |
| 640 | bool constants, 8 uints, bit N = hardware bool address N |
| 672 | swapped texcoords mask |
| 676 | alpha threshold |
| 680 | half pixel offset (float2) |
| 688 | guest memory base (uint64): GPU address of guest physical address 0 |
| 696 | the 96 vertex fetch constants, 2 dwords each |
| 1464 | 16 declared vertex elements (uint4): fetch constant, offset and stride in dwords, format flags |
| 1720 | NDC transform (float4) |
| 1736 | alpha test function (RB_COLORCONTROL alpha_func) |

The D3D12/DXIL side of the patch is not maintained (Vulkan only).

Consequence for the renderer: memexport targets and raw-fetched vertex data
are addressed by guest physical address, so vertex buffers live in one GPU
buffer laid out like guest physical memory (`g_GuestMemoryBase`), filled from
CPU writes on unlock, written by skinning shaders, and bound with offsets for
draws. Shaders need `bufferDeviceAddress` and `vertexPipelineStoresAndAtomics`.

## Multiplying by zero

Xenos multiplies as Shader Model 3: +-0 or a denormal times anything, an
infinity or NaN too, is 0 (Xenia's ZeroIfAnyOperandIsZero). Ninja Gaiden II
relies on it: Sonia's skin blends a garbage position stream (NaN) with a
weight of 0, and plain multiplies turned those vertices into NaN (a hole in
her shoulder). mul, mad, dp2add/dp3/dp4, dst's y, muls, mulsprev and mulsc go
through `mulz`/`dotz` in shader_common.h (patch 0009); they are `precise`,
since DXC doesn't carry `precise` into called functions.

## Rounding

Xenos vertex ALUs round sums and products toward zero and never fuse a
multiply and an add (Xenia Edge 3390fc219, 043a7cb40): games split vertex and
bone indices with a multiply then trunc, and round to nearest can push one
into the next. Vertex shaders therefore ask for SPIR-V's RoundingModeRTZ
(32-bit) and declare their registers and outputs `precise` (NoContraction).
DXC only declares the capability for an instruction that asks for it, so each
vertex shader has one `ps + 0` through such a declared instruction. On a GPU
without shaderRoundingModeRTZFloat32 the renderer removes the mode, its
capability and extension from the SPIR-V (video.cpp DropRoundTowardZero); the
log says which at startup ("vertex shaders round toward zero").

## Predicate counters

Xenos shaders nest conditions with a counter in a register: `setp_*_push`
starts a level, `setp_pop` ends one, `setp_inv` flips the innermost. The
translator had `setp_inv` turn a count of 1 into 1 (it must give 0), so the
instructions after it saw the wrong nesting. NG2's point and spot light code
(the vertex shader of rigid pieces such as the archers' bows) runs only with
point lights near, so the bows were lit in bands of colour under the fire
ninpo. Patch 0010 fixes it, and takes the pushes' test from `.w` and result
from `.x` of their sources as Xenos does (NG2's shaders replicate one
component, so their output didn't change).

## Control flow

Xenos jumps are translated as structured `if` blocks wherever they nest: a
forward conditional jump opens a block that ends at its target, and an
unconditional jump that is the last instruction of such a block and lands
past its end, within the enclosing block, is that block's `else`; one that
lands on the next instruction (an empty else) does nothing (patch 0018).
Only shaders with anything else (a jump back, overlapping blocks) are
emitted as Unleashed did, a `while (true) { switch (pc) { ... } }` state
machine. Before 0018 every shader with an unconditional jump took the loop;
NG2's jumps all nest, so none does now (301 of its 663 shaders have an else,
the skinning and lighting vertex shaders among them).

The loop is expensive on AMD's Windows driver (#2): it compiled the vertex
shaders among those to 256 VGPRs and spilled the rest to scratch, up to
23 KB a vertex (vs 8282819E0F311055), so a few skinned draws took most of a
frame whatever the resolution (RX 6800: 55-125 ms of GPU time a frame in
Chapter 1's first fight). Structured, the same shaders use 50-121 VGPRs and
no scratch, and the frame takes 2-4 ms. `NG2_PIPELINE_STATS=1` logs these
numbers from the driver.

```

```md
# Title updates

Since 2026-11-03 the port runs Ninja Gaiden II with Title Update 3 (0.0.3.4), the last update for
the World disc (media ID 69F555CB): the update's `default.xexp` sits next to `default.xex` and the
SDK applies it, both when generating the code and when the game starts. The installers ask for
the update package (`TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4`, 2,486,272 bytes) once, extract its
`default.xexp` (2,416,640 bytes, SHA-1 `e9df578781355d9a25e1c0adba8fbb859333456a`) and check it;
an earlier install's TU2 is replaced. The Japanese release's TU3
(`TU_1A461UL_000000C000000.00000000000O3`, media ID 0E6FB1CE) has the same size but patches that
disc's 1.0 (version 3), not this one's (version 4), so it is refused.

What the updates changed isn't documented. Reports from 2008 tell of a late-July update that came
with the Mission Mode DLC and froze cutscenes in chapters 10, 12 and 14 for players on Xbox Live,
and a patch at the end of August that fixed those freezes and sped up the cutscene transitions;
TU2 and TU3 are most likely those two (an inference: the files carry no dates).

## Addresses, TU2 to TU3

TU3 moves less than TU2 did (most addresses by under 0x900 bytes; the game's data, the 2D buckets,
the menus' models and views, the title menu's entries don't move). The table maps every address
the code used under TU2 (in `src/` and `ng2_codegen.toml`) that TU3 moves.
`ng2_pointer_funcs.toml` was regenerated (`tools/find_pointer_funcs.py`, 48 functions; TU2: 45).

`ng2_dump_image`), then checked by hand:
- read-only data by content (vtables by the functions their slots point to, the stage table by
  its strings); the title menu's picture table moved by 8 bytes (TU3 adds two entries before it);

## Title Update 2 (2026-11-02 to 2026-11-03)

From 2026-11-02 the port ran Title Update 2 (0.0.2.4, `TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000G4`,
its `default.xexp` 2,318,336 bytes, SHA-1 `22d3be744cc43316e6f93d3d17834a814dd28062`), then taken
for the last update for this disc.

### Addresses, 1.0 to TU2

The update moves most of the game's code and data. Notes written before the move (the other files
in `docs/`, older commit messages) use 1.0 addresses; the table below maps every address the code
used then in `src/` and `ng2_codegen.toml` to its TU2 one (`ng2_pointer_funcs.toml` is
regenerated by `tools/find_pointer_funcs.py` instead).

How they were mapped: `tools/map_addresses.py <1.0 image> <TU2 image> <repo>` (images dumped
with `NG2_DUMP_IMAGE`, the TU2 one with the update in place) matches code by instruction windows
with branch offsets and lis-built address immediates masked out, and data through the code that
builds each address (lis + addi/load/store). Checked by hand: small identical functions the
linker shares (vtable thunks: found through the vtables or by their exact bytes), struct fields
reached as base + offset (the in-game menu's views were wrong in the first pass), and `kReturnZero`,
which must be a function the code generator knows.

## DLC

Content packages under the game folder's `dlc/` (any depth, so the console's
`544307D5/00000002/` folders can be copied in as they are) are installed into the user data
folder once, at launch (`src/dlc.cpp`); only this game's DLC (content type 2) is taken.
```

`docs/xenia-notes.md`:

```md
# Notes from Xenia (Edge)

Xenia Edge (https://github.com/has207/xenia-edge, BSD-3-Clause; a fork of
Xenia Canary) is a reference for GPU and kernel behaviour alongside the
Xenia-derived code in ReXGlue. Its compatibility list entry for NG2 (title
544307D5, issue 296): state "Gameplay", labels gpu-drawing-missing,
gpu-drawing-corrupt, kernel-save-file-errors, vsync-off-speedup,
requires_protect_zero_false, gpu-driver-issues-nvidia,
requires_clear_memory_page_state_true.

What NG2 does with that:

- protect_zero: NG2 sets it to false by default (src/ng2_app.h); the game
  reads the zero page.
- clear_memory_page_state: already true by default in ReXGlue (it only
  affects the xenos plugin).
- Xenia writes 0x2A6E3F38 at 0x8000001C because NG2 reads it; ReXGlue does
  the same (src/system/xmemory.cpp).
- Save file errors: to check when saving is reached.

```

`generated/rexglue.cmake`:

```cmake
# Auto-generated by rexglue - DO NOT EDIT

# SDK version
# Set REXSDK_VERSION to pin a specific SDK version.
# Otherwise, the version of the SDK that generated this file is used.
set(REXSDK_VERSION "" CACHE STRING "Override SDK version (leave empty for default)")

# Find SDK
set(REXSDK_DIR "" CACHE PATH "Path to rexglue-sdk source tree")
if(REXSDK_DIR)
    add_subdirectory("${REXSDK_DIR}" rexglue-sdk)
    message(STATUS "Using ReXGlue SDK from source tree: ${REXSDK_DIR}")
else()
    if(REXSDK_VERSION)
        find_package(rexglue ${REXSDK_VERSION} EXACT QUIET CONFIG)
    else()
        find_package(rexglue 0.10.0 QUIET CONFIG)
    endif()
    if(NOT rexglue_FOUND)
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "ReXGlue SDK not found. Either:\n"
            "  - Set REXSDK_DIR to the rexglue-sdk source tree (e.g. thirdparty/rexglue-sdk)\n"
            "  - Install the SDK package and ensure it is on CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH")
    endif()
    message(STATUS "Found ReXGlue SDK ${REXGLUE_VERSION_STRING} at ${rexglue_DIR}")
endif()

# Host target name used by the codegen-emitted dll_targets.cmake to colocate
# guest DLLs with the host EXE. Defaults to PROJECT_NAME (which the
# manifest-first init flow sets equal to the host target name).
if(NOT DEFINED REXGLUE_HOST_TARGET)
    set(REXGLUE_HOST_TARGET ${PROJECT_NAME})
endif()

set(REXGLUE_RECOMP_DEBUG_INFO "line-tables-only" CACHE STRING
    "Debug info level for generated code: line-tables-only, full, or none")

# Guest SEH scopes emit __try/__except, which traps hardware faults only under
# asynchronous EH. clang++ spells that flag the GNU way.
set(REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS "")
if(WIN32)
    if(MSVC)
        list(APPEND REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS /EHa)
    elseif(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
        list(APPEND REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS -fasync-exceptions)
    endif()
endif()
if(REXGLUE_RECOMP_DEBUG_INFO STREQUAL "none")
    list(APPEND REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS
        $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:Clang,AppleClang,GNU>:-g0>)
elseif(REXGLUE_RECOMP_DEBUG_INFO STREQUAL "line-tables-only")
    list(APPEND REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS
        $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:Clang,AppleClang>:-gline-tables-only>)
endif()

# Include entrypoint generated code if codegen has been run.
if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default/sources.cmake")
    include(generated/default/sources.cmake)
    set(REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_GENERATED_SOURCES ${GENERATED_SOURCES})
    set(REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_INCLUDE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default")

    # Carried on the sources so they hold for whichever target compiles them.
    set_source_files_properties(${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_GENERATED_SOURCES}
        PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "${REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS}")
endif()

# The options go on the target as well: CMake compiles the header from its own
# cmake_pch.hxx.cxx, which carries none of the source properties above, and
# clang rejects a PCH whose EH mode disagrees with the TU including it.
function(rexglue_apply_recomp_settings target_name pch_header)
    target_precompile_headers(${target_name} PRIVATE "${pch_header}")
    target_compile_options(${target_name} PRIVATE ${REXGLUE_RECOMP_OPTIONS})
endfunction()

# Configure a rexglue target with SDK libraries and platform settings.
# Call after add_executable() in your CMakeLists.txt.
# Usage: rexglue_setup_target(<target> [GPU_PLUGINS xenos])
macro(rexglue_setup_target target_name)
    if(REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_GENERATED_SOURCES)
        add_library(${target_name}_recomp OBJECT
            ${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_GENERATED_SOURCES})
        target_include_directories(${target_name}_recomp PRIVATE
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src
            ${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_INCLUDE_DIR}
        )
        target_link_libraries(${target_name}_recomp PRIVATE rex::runtime)
        rexglue_apply_target_settings(${target_name}_recomp)
        rexglue_apply_recomp_settings(${target_name}_recomp
            "${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_INCLUDE_DIR}/ng2_pch.h")
        add_dependencies(${target_name}_recomp ng2_codegen)
        target_link_libraries(${target_name} PRIVATE
            ${target_name}_recomp)
    endif()
    # Also on the host, so a tree that has never run codegen still generates it.
    add_dependencies(${target_name} ng2_codegen)
    target_include_directories(${target_name} PRIVATE
        ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
        ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src
        ${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_INCLUDE_DIR}
    )
    target_link_libraries(${target_name} PRIVATE rex::runtime)
    if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/metadata/icons")
        rexglue_embed_metadata(${target_name}
            DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/metadata/icons"
            PREFIX "icons")
    endif()
    rexglue_configure_target(${target_name} ${ARGN})
endmacro()

# Codegen runs as part of the build, re-running only when an input in codegen.d
# changes. Build it alone with 'cmake --build . --target ng2_codegen'.
# Listing the sources as outputs orders any target that compiles them after
# codegen, including one a project assembles itself rather than taking the
# library rexglue_setup_target() builds. The stamp comes first: the DEPFILE
# names it.
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default/codegen.build.stamp"
           ${REXGLUE_ENTRYPOINT_GENERATED_SOURCES}
    COMMAND $<TARGET_FILE:rex::rexglue> codegen ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ng2_manifest.toml
    DEPFILE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default/codegen.d"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    COMMENT "Generating recompiled code for ng2"
    VERBATIM
)
add_custom_target(ng2_codegen
    DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default/codegen.build.stamp")

# Include DLL module shared library targets if codegen has generated them
if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/generated/default/dll_targets.cmake")
    include(generated/default/dll_targets.cmake)
endif()

```

`ng2_codegen.toml`:

```toml
# Ninja Gaiden II (544307D5, default.xex 2008-05-09 with Title Update 3) codegen overrides.
# Included from ng2_manifest.toml.

# Guest registers as C++ locals where they don't carry values between functions:
# the compiler can keep them in host registers instead of the shared context.
# Non-volatile registers (r14-r31, f14-f31, v14-v31, v64-v127) are each
# function's own (its prologue/epilogue save helpers are dropped); SEH funclets
# keep the shared ones. The vector registers below are read before being
# written by functions that take values in them from their callers (the video
# codec's transform kernels: v64, v65, v69, v72; sub_83795F68: v29, v30), found
# by scanning the generated code, so they stay in the shared context.
ctr_as_local = true
xer_as_local = true
cr_as_local = true
reserved_as_local = true
non_volatile_as_local = true
shared_vector_registers = [29, 30, 64, 65, 69, 72]

# MSVC CRT; libjpeg's error_exit longjmps out of the decoder.
setjmp_address = 0x8397B4E0
longjmp_address = 0x8397B1C0

[functions]
# this-adjustor thunks (addi r3,r3,N; b ...) the analysis skipped
0x83780438 = { size = 8 }
0x83781800 = { size = 8 }
# ends in a no-return KeBugCheck; SwitchToFiber starts right after it
0x8383E8F0 = { size = 0x10 }
```
