`packaging/appimage/AppRun`:

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ninja Gaiden II launcher: game files, writable settings/logs/saves, then
# the game. Extra arguments go to the game (ReXGlue options).
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
config_dir=${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/ng2-recomp
data_dir=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/ng2-recomp
# Portable mode: with portable.txt next to the AppImage, everything (settings,
# saves, the log, a copied game) goes in a userdata folder next to it. The
# first start offers it when that folder can be written.
beside=${APPIMAGE:+$(dirname "$APPIMAGE")}

# Dialogs: kdialog (KDE), else qarma or zenity (other desktops, such as GNOME,
# Cinnamon or Xfce), else questions in the terminal the AppImage was started
# from. ui_* return non-zero when the player cancels.
ui= markup=()
if command -v kdialog >/dev/null; then ui=kdialog
elif command -v qarma >/dev/null; then ui=qarma
elif command -v zenity >/dev/null; then ui=zenity markup=(--no-markup)
elif [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then ui=terminal
fi
ui_message() {  # <title> <text>
  case $ui in
    kdialog) kdialog --title "$1" --msgbox "$2" ;;
    qarma|zenity) "$ui" --info "${markup[@]}" --title "$1" --text "$2" --width 480 2>/dev/null ;;
    terminal) printf '\n%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
ui_error() {  # <text>: shown, also on the terminal
  echo "$1" >&2
  case $ui in
    kdialog) kdialog --title "Ninja Gaiden II" --error "$1" || true ;;
    qarma|zenity) "$ui" --error "${markup[@]}" --title "Ninja Gaiden II" --text "$1" --width 480 \
                    2>/dev/null || true ;;
  esac
  return 0
}
ui_yesno() {  # <title> <yes label> <no label> <text>: 0 for yes
  case $ui in
    kdialog) kdialog --title "$1" --yes-label "$2" --no-label "$3" --yesno "$4" 2>/dev/null ;;
    qarma|zenity) "$ui" --question "${markup[@]}" --title "$1" --ok-label "$2" --cancel-label "$3" --text "$4" \
                    --width 480 2>/dev/null ;;
    terminal)
      local answer
      printf '\n%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$4"
      read -r -p "[1] $2  [2] $3: " answer || return 1
      case $answer in 1|y|Y|yes|Yes) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
ui_path() {  # a typed or dropped path (quoted by the terminal, ~ for home): as a path
  local path=$1
  path=${path%"${path##*[![:space:]]}"}  # trailing spaces
  case $path in
    \'*\') path=${path:1:${#path}-2} ;;
    \"*\") path=${path:1:${#path}-2} ;;
  esac
  case $path in "~"|"~/"*) path="$HOME${path:1}" ;; esac
  [ -n "$path" ] && printf '%s\n' "$path"
}
ui_file() {  # <title> <kdialog filter>: the chosen file's path
  case $ui in
    kdialog) kdialog --title "$1" --getopenfilename "$HOME" "$2" ;;
    qarma|zenity) "$ui" --file-selection --title "$1" --filename "$HOME/" 2>/dev/null ;;
    terminal)
      local path
      read -r -e -p "$1, path: " path || return 1
      ui_path "$path" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
ui_folder() {  # <title>: the chosen folder's path
  case $ui in
    kdialog) kdialog --title "$1" --getexistingdirectory "$HOME" ;;
    qarma|zenity) "$ui" --file-selection --directory --title "$1" --filename "$HOME/" 2>/dev/null ;;
    terminal)
      local path
      read -r -e -p "$1, folder: " path || return 1
      ui_path "$path" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
if [ -n "$beside" ] && [ ! -f "$beside/portable.txt" ] && [ ! -f "$config_dir/game_dir" ] &&
   [ ! -f "$config_dir/portable_asked" ] &&
   [ -z "${NG2_GAME_DIR:-}" ] && [ -w "$beside" ] && [ -n "$ui" ]; then
  if ui_yesno "Ninja Gaiden II" "Portable" "Normal" \
      "Keep the settings, saves and the installed game in a userdata folder next to the AppImage ($beside), instead of in your home folder?"; then
    : > "$beside/portable.txt"
  else
    mkdir -p "$config_dir" && : > "$config_dir/portable_asked"  # (Normal: not asked again)
  fi
fi
if [ -n "$beside" ] && [ -f "$beside/portable.txt" ]; then
  config_dir=$beside/userdata
  data_dir=$beside/userdata
fi
mkdir -p "$config_dir" "$data_dir/user" 2>/dev/null || {
  msg="Can't write $data_dir. In portable mode the folder next to the AppImage must be writable (or delete portable.txt there)."
  ui_error "$msg"
  exit 1
}

error() {
  ui_error "$1"
  exit 1
}

# A disc image or package into a folder, with kdialog's progress bar when
# qdbus is there to drive it; 130 if the player cancelled.
extract() {
  local qdbus ref pid percent
  qdbus=$(command -v qdbus6 || command -v qdbus || true)
  if [ "$ui" != kdialog ] || [ -z "$qdbus" ] || ! ref=$(kdialog --title "Ninja Gaiden II" \
      --progressbar "Copying the game from the disc..." 100 2>/dev/null); then
    [ "$ui" = terminal ] && echo "Copying the game from the disc..."
    python3 -I "$here/usr/bin/xdvdfs_extract.py" "$1" "$2" 2>"$data_dir/extract.log"
    return
  fi
  "$qdbus" $ref showCancelButton true >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  python3 -I "$here/usr/bin/xdvdfs_extract.py" "$1" "$2" --progress \
    >"$data_dir/extract.progress" 2>"$data_dir/extract.log" &
  pid=$!
  while kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null; do
    sleep 0.5
    percent=$(tail -1 "$data_dir/extract.progress" 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$percent" ] && "$qdbus" $ref Set "" value "$percent" >/dev/null 2>&1
    if [ "$("$qdbus" $ref wasCancelled 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; then
      kill $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
      "$qdbus" $ref close >/dev/null 2>&1
      rm -f "$data_dir/extract.progress"
      return 130
    fi
  done
  wait $pid; local status=$?
  "$qdbus" $ref close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f "$data_dir/extract.progress"
  return $status
}

# The game files: NG2_GAME_DIR, the remembered folder, or ask: default.xex in
# an extracted copy, or a disc image or Games on Demand package (its header
# file, next to the .data folder), which is extracted into the data folder.
game=${NG2_GAME_DIR:-}
if [ -z "$game" ] && [ -f "$config_dir/game_dir" ]; then
  game=$(cat "$config_dir/game_dir")
  # The copy in the data folder, where the remembered folder is gone (a
  # portable folder moved, a drive mounted elsewhere).
  if [ ! -f "$game/default.xex" ] && [ -f "$data_dir/game/default.xex" ]; then
    game=$data_dir/game
    printf '%s\n' "$game" > "$config_dir/game_dir"
  fi
fi
# An extracted copy next to the AppImage is taken without asking (unless
# NG2_GAME_DIR names another folder).
if [ -z "${NG2_GAME_DIR:-}" ] && { [ -z "$game" ] || [ ! -f "$game/default.xex" ]; } && [ -n "$beside" ]; then
  for dir in "$beside" "$beside/game_files" "$beside/game"; do
    if [ -f "$dir/default.xex" ]; then game=$dir; printf '%s\n' "$game" > "$config_dir/game_dir"; break; fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$game" ] || [ ! -f "$game/default.xex" ]; then
  [ -n "$ui" ] ||
    error "Put the extracted game (the folder with default.xex) next to the AppImage, set NG2_GAME_DIR to it, or start the AppImage from a terminal to be asked."
  ui_message "Ninja Gaiden II" \
    "Choose your copy of the game: a disc image (.iso), the Games on Demand package (the file in 544307D5/00007000, next to its .data folder), or default.xex in an extracted copy. A disc image or package is copied into $data_dir/game." || exit 0
  choice=$(ui_file "Ninja Gaiden II: game files" \
    "*|Disc image, Games on Demand package or default.xex") || exit 0
  [ -e "$choice" ] || error "There's no $choice."
  name=$(basename "$choice")
  case "${name,,}" in
    default.xex) game=$(dirname "$choice") ;;
    *)
      game=$data_dir/game
      rm -rf "$game.part"
      extract "$choice" "$game.part" || {
        status=$?
        rm -rf "$game.part"
        [ $status -eq 130 ] && exit 0  # cancelled
        error "Could not read the game from that file: $(tail -1 "$data_dir/extract.log")"
      }
      [ -f "$game.part/default.xex" ] || { rm -rf "$game.part"; error "There's no default.xex on that disc."; }
      # The new copy replaces the old one, which is set aside first and only
      # deleted once its downloadable content and title update are moved over.
      # One left by a swap that failed halfway: its content first.
      for keep in dlc default.xexp; do
        if [ ! -e "$game/$keep" ] && [ -e "$game.old/$keep" ]; then mv "$game.old/$keep" "$game.part/$keep"; fi
      done
      rm -rf "$game.old"
      if [ -e "$game" ]; then
        mv "$game" "$game.old" || { rm -rf "$game.part"; error "Can't replace $game."; }
      fi
      mv "$game.part" "$game" || { mv "$game.old" "$game" 2>/dev/null; error "Can't write to $game."; }
      kept=1
      for keep in dlc default.xexp; do
        if [ -e "$game.old/$keep" ]; then mv "$game.old/$keep" "$game/$keep" || kept=; fi
      done
      [ -n "$kept" ] && rm -rf "$game.old"
      ;;
  esac
  [ -f "$game/default.xex" ] || error "No default.xex in $game."
  printf '%s\n' "$game" > "$config_dir/game_dir"
fi

tu3_sha1=e9df578781355d9a25e1c0adba8fbb859333456a  # the World disc's (media ID 69F555CB)
tu2_sha1=22d3be744cc43316e6f93d3d17834a814dd28062  # what earlier builds ran: replaced
# Title Update 3 (default.xexp next to default.xex): ask for the update
# package (or an extracted default.xexp) once and put it in the game folder.
if [ -f "$game/default.xexp" ] && [ "$(sha1sum "$game/default.xexp" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$tu2_sha1" ]; then
  mv "$game/default.xexp" "$game/default.xexp.tu2" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ ! -f "$game/default.xexp" ]; then
  [ -n "$ui" ] ||
    error "Title Update 3 is missing: put default.xexp in $game, or start the AppImage from a terminal to be asked."
  ui_message "Ninja Gaiden II: Title Update 3" \
    "This port runs the game with Title Update 3 (for the World release, media ID 69F555CB). Choose the update: its package (TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4) or an extracted default.xexp." || exit 0
  update=$(ui_file "Ninja Gaiden II: Title Update 3" "TU_* default.xexp|Title update or default.xexp") || exit 0
  [ -f "$update" ] || error "There's no $update."
  [ -w "$game" ] || error "Can't write to $game: copy default.xexp there yourself."
  case "$(basename "$update")" in
    *.xexp|*.XEXP) cp "$update" "$game/default.xexp.part" || error "Can't copy to $game." ;;
    *) python3 -I "$here/usr/bin/stfs_extract.py" "$update" default.xexp "$game/default.xexp.part" ||
         error "That file isn't the title update." ;;
  esac
  # Title Update 3's default.xexp for this disc, nothing else (the Japanese
  # release's TU3, another update or game's wouldn't fit this build).
  if [ "$(sha1sum "$game/default.xexp.part" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "$tu3_sha1" ]; then
    rm -f "$game/default.xexp.part"
    error "That isn't Title Update 3 for this disc (the World release's: TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4)."
  fi
  mv "$game/default.xexp.part" "$game/default.xexp"
fi
[ "$(sha1sum "$game/default.xexp" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$tu3_sha1" ] ||
  error "$game/default.xexp isn't Title Update 3 for this disc. Remove it to choose the update again."

# Downloadable content, offered once: the packages in a chosen folder (at any
# depth, as the console keeps them) copied into the game folder's dlc/, which
# the game installs from at start.
if [ ! -f "$config_dir/dlc_asked" ] && [ -n "$ui" ]; then
  touch "$config_dir/dlc_asked"
  if ui_yesno "Ninja Gaiden II: downloadable content" "Add DLC" "Skip" \
      "Add downloadable content? Choose the folder with the packages (for example 544307D5/00000002). You can also put them in the dlc folder inside the game folder later."; then
    from=$(ui_folder "Ninja Gaiden II: downloadable content") || from=
    if [ -n "$from" ]; then
      # One of each name, none from the game's own dlc folder.
      target=$(realpath -m "$game/dlc")
      packages=()
      declare -A seen=()
      while IFS= read -r package; do
        name=$(basename "$package")
        case "$(realpath -m "$package")" in "$target"/*) continue ;; esac
        [ -n "${seen[$name]:-}" ] && continue
        seen[$name]=1
        packages+=("$package")
      done < <(python3 -I "$here/usr/bin/find_dlc.py" "$from")
      if [ ${#packages[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        ui_error "There's no downloadable content for this game in $from."
      elif ! { mkdir -p "$game/dlc" && cp -f "${packages[@]}" "$game/dlc/"; }; then
        ui_error "Can't copy the downloadable content to $game/dlc."
      fi
    fi
  fi
fi

export NG2_CONFIG=${NG2_CONFIG:-$config_dir/ng2.toml}
exec "$here/usr/bin/ng2" --game_data_root="$game" --user_data_root="$data_dir/user" \
  --log_file="$data_dir/ng2.log" "$@"

```

`packaging/appimage/Dockerfile`:

```
# Build environment for the portable Ninja Gaiden II AppImage (packaging/appimage/build.sh): Ubuntu 22.04, so the program needs no glibc newer than 2.35 and runs on SteamOS,
# Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12, Fedora 36+ and other current systems.
# The first RUN matches the Ninja Gaiden Black and Wind Waker AppImages' environment layer for
# layer, so they share Docker's cache.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

ARG LLVM_VERSION=22
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates wget gnupg lsb-release software-properties-common git file \
        python3 python3-pip pkg-config \
    && add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        g++-13 libstdc++-13-dev \
        libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxfixes-dev libxi-dev libxss-dev libxtst-dev \
        libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev wayland-protocols libdecor-0-dev libegl1-mesa-dev libgl-dev \
        libgbm-dev libdrm-dev libvulkan-dev libpulse-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libasound2-dev libdbus-1-dev \
        libudev-dev \
    && wget -qO /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh \
    && bash /tmp/llvm.sh ${LLVM_VERSION} \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends clang-${LLVM_VERSION} lld-${LLVM_VERSION} llvm-${LLVM_VERSION} \
    && for tool in clang clang++ ld.lld llvm-strip llvm-profdata; do \
           ln -sf /usr/bin/${tool}-${LLVM_VERSION} /usr/local/bin/${tool}; done \
    && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir "cmake>=3.25,<4" ninja patchelf \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* /tmp/llvm.sh

# What the ReXGlue SDK and the game need besides: zstd (the shader cache), xcb for X11,
# nasm for FFmpeg's assembly.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        libzstd-dev libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev nasm xz-utils make \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# FFmpeg for the game's movies (ASF files with WMV3/VC-1 video and WMA/WMA Pro sound): an LGPL
# shared build with only those, bundled into the AppImage. (The SDK builds its own FFmpeg for
# the game's XMA audio.)
ARG FFMPEG_VERSION=9.0.2
RUN wget -qO /tmp/ffmpeg.tar.xz https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}.tar.xz \
    && tar -xJf /tmp/ffmpeg.tar.xz -C /tmp \
    && cd /tmp/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
    && ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --cc=clang --enable-shared --disable-static \
         --disable-programs --disable-doc --disable-network --disable-autodetect \
         --disable-everything --disable-avdevice --disable-avfilter \
         --enable-demuxer=asf --enable-protocol=file --enable-parser=vc1 \
         --enable-decoder=wmv1,wmv2,wmv3,vc1,wmav1,wmav2,wmapro,wmavoice \
         --enable-swscale --enable-swresample \
    && make -j"$(nproc)" && make install \
    && mkdir -p /usr/local/share/ffmpeg \
    && cp LICENSE.md COPYING.LGPLv2.1 /usr/local/share/ffmpeg/ \
    && cd / && rm -rf /tmp/ffmpeg.tar.xz /tmp/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}

```

`packaging/appimage/build-local.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ninja Gaiden II (static recompilation) as an AppImage, for testing on the
# machine that built it (packaging/appimage/build.sh makes the portable one).
#
#   packaging/appimage/build-local.sh [out-dir]      (default out/appimage-local)
#
# Packs the current release build (out/build/linux-amd64-release): the game,
# ReXGlue's runtime and GPU plugin (looked up next to the executable), the
# ISO extractor and a launcher. FFmpeg, Vulkan, the GPU drivers, SDL's
# window-system libraries and glibc come from the system, so this is not a
# portable release (that needs an older-glibc container build and a small
# static FFmpeg with the WMV/WMA decoders). No game data is included: the
# first launch asks for the extracted game folder or the disc image.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
build=$repo/out/build/linux-amd64-release
out=$(mkdir -p "${1:-$repo/out/appimage-local}" && cd "${1:-$repo/out/appimage-local}" && pwd)
tool=${APPIMAGETOOL:-$(command -v appimagetool || true)}

[ -x "$build/ng2" ] || { echo "No build at $build: build the release preset first." >&2; exit 1; }
[ -x "$tool" ] || { echo "appimagetool not found (set APPIMAGETOOL)." >&2; exit 1; }

app=$out/AppDir
rm -rf "$app"
mkdir -p "$app/usr/bin"
cp "$build/ng2" "$build/librexruntime.so" "$app/usr/bin/"  # no GPU plugin: no GPU emulation
[ -f "$build/libTracyClient.so" ] && cp "$build/libTracyClient.so" "$app/usr/bin/"
strip --strip-unneeded "$app/usr/bin/"*
cp "$repo/tools/xdvdfs_extract.py" "$repo/tools/stfs_extract.py" "$repo/tools/find_dlc.py" "$app/usr/bin/"
cp "$here/AppRun" "$app/AppRun"
chmod +x "$app/AppRun"
cp "$here/ng2.desktop" "$app/"
cp "$here/ng2.png" "$app/ng2.png"

ARCH=x86_64 "$tool" --no-appstream "$app" "$out/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage" >/dev/null
echo "$out/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage"

```

`packaging/appimage/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ninja Gaiden II for Linux as a portable AppImage (the one for releases and testing).
#
#   packaging/appimage/build.sh [out-dir]      (default out/appimage)
#
# Builds the ReXGlue SDK and the game in an Ubuntu 22.04 container (Dockerfile here), so the
# AppImage needs only glibc 2.35 (SteamOS, Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12, Fedora 36+), and packs
# <out-dir>/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage with the libraries a system may lack: FFmpeg (a small
# LGPL build of 9.0.2 with the movies' codecs, see the Dockerfile); libstdc++ is linked in.
# glibc, zstd, the Vulkan loader and drivers, and the X11/Wayland libraries are the system's.
#
# The build runs in out/portable (NG2_PORTABLE_DIR): a copy of the sources in src/ (the code
# generator writes into the tree), with the SDK patches already applied in thirdparty/, and
# the SDK's and the game's build trees. The game's default.xex (and
# default.xexp) are read from game_files/ (NG2_GAME_DIR) for the code and shaders. No game data
# goes into the AppImage. packaging/appimage/build-local.sh is the quick, unportable build for
# this machine.
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
dest=$(mkdir -p "${1:-$repo/out/appimage}" && cd "${1:-$repo/out/appimage}" && pwd)
out=$(mkdir -p "${NG2_PORTABLE_DIR:-$repo/out/portable}" && cd "${NG2_PORTABLE_DIR:-$repo/out/portable}" && pwd)
# The sources are copied into $out/src with rsync --delete: never into the sources themselves.
case "$out/" in
    "$repo/out/"?*) ;;
    "$repo/"*) echo "NG2_PORTABLE_DIR must be outside the sources, or under out/." >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
game=$(cd "${NG2_GAME_DIR:-$repo/game_files}" && pwd)
image=ng2-build:jammy
jobs=${JOBS:-$(nproc)}
tool=${APPIMAGETOOL:-$(command -v appimagetool || true)}

[ -f "$game/default.xex" ] && [ -f "$game/default.xexp" ] ||
    { echo "No default.xex and default.xexp in $game (NG2_GAME_DIR)." >&2; exit 1; }
[ -x "$tool" ] || { echo "appimagetool not found (set APPIMAGETOOL)." >&2; exit 1; }
# (appimagetool skips the .zsync without a word when zsyncmake is missing: checked before the build)
command -v zsyncmake >/dev/null || { echo "zsyncmake is needed for the .zsync file (zsync package)" >&2; exit 1; }

docker build -q -t "$image" "$here" >/dev/null

# The sources, without build trees and the reference checkouts (copies share blocks on btrfs).
mkdir -p "$out/src"
rsync -a --delete --exclude /out --exclude /game_files --exclude /thirdparty/xenia-edge \
    --exclude 'thirdparty/*/out' --exclude /.git --exclude '/*.log' \
    "$repo/" "$out/src/"
mkdir -p "$out/src/game_files"  # the game's files are mounted here (the manifest's path)

docker run --rm -m 24g --shm-size=4g -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp \
    -v "$out":/out -v "$game":/out/src/game_files:ro "$image" bash -euc '
flags="-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc -fuse-ld=lld"
# The SDK for any x86-64 PC since about 2009 (x86-64-v2: SSE4.2); the game twice, for those
# and for AVX2 machines (x86-64-v3: the Steam Deck, any Ryzen, Intel since Haswell), which
# the first hands over to where the CPU has it (src/cpu_handover.cpp).
arch="-march=x86-64-v2"
sdk=/out/src/thirdparty/rexglue-sdk
# A step that fails shows the end of its log.
step() { log=$1; shift; "$@" >"$log" 2>&1 || { echo "== $log" >&2; tail -20 "$log" >&2; exit 1; }; }
step /out/sdk-configure.log cmake -S "$sdk" -B /out/sdk-build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=23 \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$arch" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$arch" \
    -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="$flags" -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="$flags" \
    -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/out/sdk-install -DREXGLUE_ENABLE_TRACY=OFF
step /out/sdk-build.log ninja -C /out/sdk-build -j'"$jobs"'
step /out/sdk-install.log cmake --install /out/sdk-build

game() {  # <build dir> <march>
    step $1.configure.log cmake -S /out/src -B $1 -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=$2" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=$2" \
        -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="$flags" -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="$flags" \
        -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/out/sdk-install;/usr/local" -DNG2_GAME_DIR=/out/src/game_files
    step $1.log ninja -C $1 -j'"$jobs"' ng2
}
game /out/build-v2 x86-64-v2
game /out/build x86-64-v3
'

# The AppDir: the program and the SDK's runtime and GPU plugin, the launcher and its tools, and
# the libraries a system may lack (found with ldd in the container).
app=$out/AppDir
rm -rf "$app"
mkdir -p "$app/usr/bin" "$app/usr/lib" "$app/usr/share/licenses/ng2"
# (no GPU plugin: no GPU emulation; the runtime the baseline build's, for both)
cp "$out/build-v2/ng2" "$out/build-v2/librexruntime.so" "$app/usr/bin/"
cp "$out/build/ng2" "$app/usr/bin/ng2-avx2"
cp "$repo/tools/xdvdfs_extract.py" "$repo/tools/stfs_extract.py" "$repo/tools/find_dlc.py" "$app/usr/bin/"
cp "$here/AppRun" "$app/AppRun"
chmod +x "$app/AppRun"
cp "$here/ng2.desktop" "$app/"
cp "$here/ng2.png" "$app/ng2.png"
cp "$here/ng2.png" "$app/.DirIcon"
cp "$repo/LICENSE" "$repo/THIRD_PARTY.md" "$app/usr/share/licenses/ng2/"
# The pipelines recorded playing the game (tools/collect_pipelines.sh), made in the background at
# the first start so new objects and effects don't pop in.
mkdir -p "$app/usr/share/ng2"
cp "$repo/packaging/ng2-pipelines-seed.bin" "$app/usr/share/ng2/"

docker run --rm -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp -v "$out":/out "$image" bash -euc '
app=/out/AppDir
llvm-strip --strip-unneeded "$app"/usr/bin/ng2 "$app"/usr/bin/ng2-avx2 "$app"/usr/bin/*.so
# The licence of the bundled FFmpeg (LGPL 2.1 or later, source ffmpeg.org 9.0.2).
cp /usr/local/share/ffmpeg/LICENSE.md "$app/usr/share/licenses/ng2/LICENSE-FFmpeg.md"
cp /usr/local/share/ffmpeg/COPYING.LGPLv2.1 "$app/usr/share/licenses/ng2/COPYING-FFmpeg.LGPLv2.1"
# Never bundled: glibc, GPU, X11/Wayland, font and session libraries, which must come from
# the system (as in the Ninja Gaiden Black AppImage).
system_lib="^(ld-linux|libc\.so|libm\.so|libdl\.so|librt\.so|libpthread|libresolv|libutil\.so|libstdc\+\+|libgcc_s|libGL|libEGL|libGLX|libGLdispatch|libOpenGL|libdrm|libgbm|libvulkan|libX11|libXau|libXdmcp|libXext|libXrender|libxcb\.so|libxcb-(shm|render|xfixes|randr|shape|sync|xkb|xinput|glx|dri2|dri3|present)\.so|libwayland-|libfontconfig|libfreetype|libharfbuzz|libexpat|libz\.|libdbus-1|libudev|libsystemd|libgpg-error|libselinux|libmount|libblkid|libffi|liblzma|liblz4|libzstd|libgcrypt|libcap|libbsd|libmd\.)"
for bin in "$app"/usr/bin/ng2 "$app"/usr/bin/ng2-avx2 "$app"/usr/bin/*.so; do
    missing=$(LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$app/usr/bin:/usr/local/lib" ldd "$bin" | grep "not found" || true)
    [ -z "$missing" ] || { echo "$bin: $missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$app/usr/bin:/usr/local/lib" ldd "$bin" | awk "/=>/ {print \$3}" | while read -r lib; do
        b=$(basename "$lib")
        case "$lib" in "$app"/*) continue ;; esac
        echo "$b" | grep -Eq "$system_lib" && continue
        [ -e "$app/usr/lib/$b" ] || cp -L "$lib" "$app/usr/lib/"
    done
done
for so in "$app"/usr/lib/*.so*; do patchelf --set-rpath "\$ORIGIN" "$so"; done
patchelf --set-rpath "\$ORIGIN:\$ORIGIN/../lib" "$app"/usr/bin/ng2 "$app"/usr/bin/ng2-avx2 "$app"/usr/bin/*.so
echo "Bundled:"; ls "$app/usr/lib"
echo "Needs from the system:"
for bin in "$app"/usr/bin/ng2 "$app"/usr/bin/ng2-avx2 "$app"/usr/bin/*.so "$app"/usr/lib/*.so*; do
    readelf -d "$bin" | sed -n "s/.*NEEDED.*\[\(.*\)\]/\1/p"
done | sort -u | grep -vxF -f <(ls "$app/usr/lib"; ls "$app/usr/bin") | tr "\n" " "; echo
echo "Newest glibc symbol:"
for bin in "$app"/usr/bin/ng2 "$app"/usr/bin/ng2-avx2 "$app"/usr/bin/*.so "$app"/usr/lib/*.so*; do
    objdump -T "$bin" | grep -o "GLIBC_[0-9.]*"
done | sort -uV | tail -1
'

# Update information for AppImageUpdate and the like: the newest release on GitHub, by the .zsync
# made beside the AppImage (zsyncmake, in the current folder), which goes up with each release.
rm -f "$dest/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage" "$dest/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage.zsync"  # (never a stale pair)
(cd "$dest" && ARCH=x86_64 "$tool" --appimage-extract-and-run --no-appstream \
    -u "gh-releases-zsync|gamboozino|ng2recomp|latest|NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage.zsync" "$app" \
    "$dest/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage" >"$out/appimagetool.log" 2>&1) ||
    { tail -20 "$out/appimagetool.log"; exit 1; }
ls -la "$dest/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage" "$dest/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage.zsync"

```

`packaging/windows/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ninja Gaiden II for Windows x64, cross-compiled on Linux.
#
#   packaging/windows/build.sh
#
# Builds the ReXGlue SDK for Windows (thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/install/windows-x64) when it
# isn't there, fetches FFmpeg's Windows build into out/windows-deps once, builds the game
# (cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-clang-xwin.cmake: clang and lld against Microsoft's C runtime
# and Windows SDK from xwin in ~/.xwin) and packs out/windows/NinjaGaiden2/ -- the program and
# the DLLs it needs that Windows doesn't ship -- into out/windows/NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip.
# No game data: the first launch installs the game and asks for Title Update 3.
#
# Needs: a native build first (out/build/linux-amd64-release: its code generator output and
# shader cache are used), cmake, ninja, clang, lld, curl, bsdtar, cabextract, and xwin's splat
# (`xwin --accept-license splat --output ~/.xwin`: the license is yours to accept).
set -euo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
toolchain=$repo/cmake/toolchains/windows-x64-clang-xwin.cmake
sdk=$repo/thirdparty/rexglue-sdk
deps=$repo/out/windows-deps
out=$repo/out/windows
ffmpeg=ffmpeg-n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0
ffmpeg_url=https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08/$ffmpeg.zip
ffmpeg_sha256=7157177b8a6cb2174c1650ba8c71b363f2c78cba5330f88c4c02cf5b2b880646
# Microsoft's Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime 14.44.35211 (x64): its DLLs go next to ng2.exe, so a
# PC without the redistributable installed runs the game too.
vcredist_url=https://download.visualstudio.microsoft.com/download/pr/990c720a-46ce-4dc7-87b9-c2eb615d34b9/CC0FF0EB1DC3F5188AE6300FAEF32BF5BEEBA4BDD6E8E445A9184072096B713B/VC_redist.x64.exe
vcredist_sha256=cc0ff0eb1dc3f5188ae6300faef32bf5beeba4bdd6e8e445a9184072096b713b
vcruntime_dlls=(msvcp140 msvcp140_atomic_wait vcruntime140 vcruntime140_1)
mkdir -p "$deps" "$out"

[ -f "$repo/out/build/linux-amd64-release/shaders/ng2_shader_cache.cpp" ] ||
    { echo "No native build: build out/build/linux-amd64-release first (README)." >&2; exit 1; }

# The SDK for Windows (its D3D12 backend off: the game draws with its own Vulkan renderer),
# brought up to date every time (cheap when nothing changed).
if [ ! -f "$sdk/out/build/windows-x64/build.ninja" ]; then
    cmake -S "$sdk" -B "$sdk/out/build/windows-x64" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$toolchain" \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=23 \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$sdk/out/install/windows-x64" \
        -DREXGLUE_USE_D3D12=OFF -DREXGLUE_USE_VULKAN=ON -DREXGLUE_ENABLE_TRACY=OFF \
        >"$out/sdk-configure.log"
fi
cmake --build "$sdk/out/build/windows-x64" -j"${JOBS:-$(nproc)}" >"$out/sdk-build.log"
cmake --install "$sdk/out/build/windows-x64" >/dev/null

# FFmpeg (LGPL shared build: headers, import libraries, DLLs)
if [ ! -f "$deps/ffmpeg/lib/avformat.lib" ]; then
    [ -s "$deps/$ffmpeg.zip" ] || curl -fL -o "$deps/$ffmpeg.zip" "$ffmpeg_url" ||
        { echo "FFmpeg's build is gone from $ffmpeg_url: put $ffmpeg.zip in $deps." >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "$ffmpeg_sha256  $deps/$ffmpeg.zip" | sha256sum -c --quiet
    rm -rf "$deps/ffmpeg" && mkdir -p "$deps/ffmpeg"
    bsdtar -xf "$deps/$ffmpeg.zip" -C "$deps/ffmpeg" --strip-components 1
fi

# The runtime DLLs, out of the redistributable's installer: cabinets appended to the exe hold the
# MSI packages and their cabinets, where the x64 files are named <dll>_amd64.
if [ "$(cat "$deps/vcruntime/.sha256" 2>/dev/null)" != "$vcredist_sha256" ]; then
    exe=$deps/VC_redist.x64-$vcredist_sha256.exe
    if [ ! -s "$exe" ]; then
        curl -fL -o "$exe.tmp" "$vcredist_url" ||
            { echo "The VC++ redistributable is gone from $vcredist_url: put it in $exe." >&2; exit 1; }
        mv "$exe.tmp" "$exe"
    fi
    echo "$vcredist_sha256  $exe" | sha256sum -c --quiet ||
        { rm -f "$exe"; echo "$exe isn't the pinned VC++ redistributable (removed)." >&2; exit 1; }
    tmp=$deps/vcredist.tmp
    rm -rf "$tmp" && mkdir -p "$tmp/dll"
    for at in $(LC_ALL=C grep -obUaP 'MSCF\x00\x00\x00\x00' "$exe" | cut -d: -f1); do
        tail -c +$((at + 1)) "$exe" > "$tmp/cab"
        cabextract -q -d "$tmp/c$at" "$tmp/cab" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    for payload in "$tmp"/c*/*; do
        cabextract -q -d "$tmp/dll" -F '*_amd64' "$payload" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    rm -rf "$deps/vcruntime" && mkdir -p "$deps/vcruntime"
    for dll in "${vcruntime_dlls[@]}"; do
        cp "$tmp/dll/$dll.dll_amd64" "$deps/vcruntime/$dll.dll"
    done
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    echo "$vcredist_sha256" > "$deps/vcruntime/.sha256"
fi

# The bundled runtime must be at least as new as the C++ library the game is built against
# (the DLLs next to ng2.exe are found before a newer one in System32).
# (Same xwin as the toolchain: ~/.xwin.)
stl=$(sed -n 's/^#define _MSVC_STL_UPDATE *\([0-9]*\)L.*/\1/p' "$HOME/.xwin/crt/include/yvals_core.h" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$stl" ] || { echo "Can't read the MSVC version from ~/.xwin/crt/include/yvals_core.h." >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$stl" -le 202503 ] ||
    { echo "xwin's MSVC ($stl) is newer than the bundled runtime 14.44: update vcredist_url." >&2; exit 1; }

# The game twice: for any x86-64 PC since about 2009 (x86-64-v2, the toolchain's default) and for
# AVX2 machines (x86-64-v3), which the first hands over to where the CPU has it
# (src/cpu_handover.cpp); the SDK is built once, for the first.
build=$repo/out/build/windows-x64
build_avx2=$repo/out/build/windows-x64-avx2
cmake -S "$repo" -B "$build" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$toolchain" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$sdk/out/install/windows-x64" \
    -DNG2_FFMPEG_DIR="$deps/ffmpeg" >"$out/configure.log"
cmake --build "$build" -j"${JOBS:-$(nproc)}" --target ng2 >"$out/build.log"
cmake -S "$repo" -B "$build_avx2" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$toolchain" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$sdk/out/install/windows-x64" \
    -DNG2_CROSS_FLAGS="-march=x86-64-v3" \
    -DNG2_FFMPEG_DIR="$deps/ffmpeg" >"$out/configure-avx2.log"
cmake --build "$build_avx2" -j"${JOBS:-$(nproc)}" --target ng2 >"$out/build-avx2.log"

pkg=$out/NinjaGaiden2
rm -rf "${pkg:?}"
mkdir -p "$pkg/licenses"
llvm-strip -o "$pkg/ng2.exe" "$build/ng2.exe"
llvm-strip -o "$pkg/ng2-avx2.exe" "$build_avx2/ng2.exe"
cp "$sdk/out/install/windows-x64/bin/"{rexruntime,SDL3}.dll "$pkg/"
cp "$deps/ffmpeg/bin/"{avformat-63,avcodec-63,avutil-61,swresample-7,swscale-10}.dll "$pkg/"
for dll in "${vcruntime_dlls[@]}"; do cp "$deps/vcruntime/$dll.dll" "$pkg/"; done
# The pipelines recorded playing the game (tools/collect_pipelines.sh), made in the background at
# the first start.
cp "$repo/packaging/ng2-pipelines-seed.bin" "$pkg/"
cp "$repo/LICENSE" "$repo/THIRD_PARTY.md" "$pkg/licenses/"
cp "$deps/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt" "$pkg/licenses/LICENSE-FFmpeg.txt"
cat > "$pkg/README.txt" <<'TXT'
Ninja Gaiden II - static recompilation for Windows (Vulkan)

Run ng2.exe. The first time it asks about portable mode (below), then installs the game:
  1. Your copy of the game: a disc image (.iso), the Games on Demand package (the file in
     544307D5\00007000, next to its .data folder), or default.xex in an extracted copy.
     A disc image or package is copied into %LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2\game (about 7 GB).
  2. Title Update 3 for the World release: its package (TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4)
     or default.xexp.
  3. Downloadable content, optional: the folder with the packages (544307D5\00000002).
     More can be added later in the "dlc" folder inside the game folder.

Needs a CPU with SSE4.2 and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers. The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs
are included. ng2.exe starts ng2-avx2.exe, the faster build, where the CPU has AVX2.

Settings, saves and the log are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2. Portable mode: with a file named
portable.txt next to ng2.exe, they go in a "userdata" folder next to it instead (the folder must be
writable, so not inside Program Files). No game data is included.
TXT
rm -f "$out/NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip"
(cd "$out" && bsdtar -a -cf NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip NinjaGaiden2)
echo "$out/NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip"

```

`patches/plume/0001-Vulkan-Wayland-surfaces-on-Linux-re-clamp-swapchain-.patch`:

```patch
From 3715e2f681765ca72f8c065201e9450f53143d0b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:41:55 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Vulkan: Wayland surfaces on Linux; re-clamp swapchain image
 count on resize

RenderWindow on Linux can carry a Wayland display and surface instead of an
X11 window, with a callback for the size in pixels (Wayland has no query).
VK_KHR_wayland_surface is enabled when the loader offers it.

The surface's minimum image count can rise after creation (e.g. once a
Wayland or gamescope surface is mapped): clamp the count again on resize.
```

```patch
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 22:48:20 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Swapchain present modes: immediate, FIFO, mailbox, FIFO
 relaxed

setPresentMode() asks for a mode on the next resize, as setVsyncEnabled()
does, and reports whether the surface has it (else FIFO). The Vulkan
backend keeps the surface's supported modes; the others keep the vsync
```

```patch
 NG2_PRECISE_BARRIERS=1

MEMORY_READ | MEMORY_WRITE on both sides flushes and invalidates every cache
at each barrier; the layouts say which accesses the image takes part in.
Behind a switch, to compare on drivers where that costs.

 1 file changed, 46 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/plume_vulkan.cpp b/plume_vulkan.cpp

+++ b/plume_vulkan.cpp
@@ -708,6 +708,44 @@ namespace plume {
         }
     }
 
+    // The accesses an image in this layout takes part in, for barriers that
+    // flush and invalidate only those caches (the default, MEMORY_READ |
+    // MEMORY_WRITE on both sides, flushes everything). On with
+    // NG2_PRECISE_BARRIERS=1, for comparing.
+    static VkAccessFlags toAccessFlags(RenderTextureLayout layout) {
+        switch (layout) {
+        case RenderTextureLayout::UNKNOWN:
+            return 0;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::SHADER_READ:
+            return VK_ACCESS_SHADER_READ_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::COLOR_WRITE:
+            return VK_ACCESS_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::DEPTH_WRITE:
+            return VK_ACCESS_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::DEPTH_READ:
+            return VK_ACCESS_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_SHADER_READ_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::COPY_SOURCE:
+        case RenderTextureLayout::RESOLVE_SOURCE:
+            return VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_READ_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::COPY_DEST:
+        case RenderTextureLayout::RESOLVE_DEST:
+            return VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::PRESENT:
+            return 0;
+        case RenderTextureLayout::GENERAL:
+        default:
+            return VK_ACCESS_MEMORY_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT;
+        }
+    }
+
+    static bool preciseBarriers() {
+        static const bool on = [] {
+            const char *v = getenv("NG2_PRECISE_BARRIERS");
+            return v != nullptr && v[0] == '1';
+        }();
+        return on;
+    }
+
     static VkImageAspectFlags toViewAspectFlags(const RenderTextureFlags flags) {
```

```patch
     }

+    std::string VulkanGraphicsPipeline::getStatistics() const {
+        std::string out;
+        if ((vk == VK_NULL_HANDLE) || !device->capabilities.pipelineExecutableInfo) {
+            return out;
+        }
+
+        VkPipelineInfoKHR pipelineInfo = {};
+        pipelineInfo.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_INFO_KHR;
+        pipelineInfo.pipeline = vk;
+        uint32_t executableCount = 0;
+        if (vkGetPipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR(device->vk, &pipelineInfo, &executableCount, nullptr) != VK_SUCCESS) {
+            return out;
+        }
+
+        std::vector<VkPipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR> executables(executableCount);
+        for (VkPipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR &executable : executables) {
+            executable.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_PROPERTIES_KHR;
+        }
+
+        vkGetPipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR(device->vk, &pipelineInfo, &executableCount, executables.data());
+        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < executableCount; i++) {
+            VkPipelineExecutableInfoKHR executableInfo = {};
+            executableInfo.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_INFO_KHR;
+            executableInfo.pipeline = vk;
+            executableInfo.executableIndex = i;
+            uint32_t statisticCount = 0;
+            vkGetPipelineExecutableStatisticsKHR(device->vk, &executableInfo, &statisticCount, nullptr);
+            std::vector<VkPipelineExecutableStatisticKHR> statistics(statisticCount);
+            for (VkPipelineExecutableStatisticKHR &statistic : statistics) {
+                statistic.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_STATISTIC_KHR;
+            }
+
+            vkGetPipelineExecutableStatisticsKHR(device->vk, &executableInfo, &statisticCount, statistics.data());
+            out += executables[i].name;
+            out += " (subgroup " + std::to_string(executables[i].subgroupSize) + "):";
+            for (const VkPipelineExecutableStatisticKHR &statistic : statistics) {
+                out += " ";
+                out += statistic.name;
+                out += "=";
+                switch (statistic.format) {
+                case VK_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_STATISTIC_FORMAT_BOOL32_KHR:
+                    out += statistic.value.b32 ? "true" : "false";
+                    break;
+                case VK_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_STATISTIC_FORMAT_INT64_KHR:
+                    out += std::to_string(statistic.value.i64);
+                    break;

+                    out += std::to_string(statistic.value.u64);
+                    break;
+                case VK_PIPELINE_EXECUTABLE_STATISTIC_FORMAT_FLOAT64_KHR:
+                    out += std::to_string(statistic.value.f64);
+                    break;
+                default:
+                    break;
+                }
+            }
+
+            out += "\n";
+        }
```

`patches/rexglue-sdk/0006-gpu-no-pending-commands-after-the-ring-buffer-is-rep.patch`:

```patch
From 1f54a6cd9809e61e1fb63d819517391a189ef47c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 01:48:11 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] gpu: no pending commands after the ring buffer is replaced

A title can call VdInitializeRingBuffer again while the command processor
runs (Ninja Gaiden II does after its intro movie, resetting its device).
InitializeRingBuffer reset the read pointer but kept the old write pointer,
so a worker waking up before the title's first write pointer update ran
the new ring's stale memory from 0 to the old write pointer, failed on a
bad packet and left the title waiting on its fences forever.

Park the write pointer at the worker's existing 'nothing written' value
instead, and count ring generations under a mutex so a worker that was
mid-way through the old ring drops the read pointer it computed for it
rather than overwriting the new ring's.

+  // it computed for the previous ring. ring_mutex_ orders the two.
+  std::mutex ring_mutex_;
+  uint32_t ring_generation_ = 0;

   // packets. Preserve these values so dependent packet logic can still observe

+      generation = ring_generation_;

 void CommandProcessor::InitializeRingBuffer(uint32_t ptr, uint32_t size_log2) {
+  // A title can replace the ring while the worker runs (after a device
+  // reset). Until the title writes the new ring's write pointer, nothing is
+  // pending: with the old write pointer left in place the worker would run
+  // whatever memory the new ring holds from 0 up to it.
```

```patch
+// Once a second at most, when the output went wrong: frames the game hadn't
+// made in time (played as silence), the longest wait between callbacks (the
+// sound server asking late) and the deepest queue. Garbled or broken-up sound
+// in play can then be lined up with the log.
+void SDLAudioDriver::NoteCallback() {
+  using clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
+  const auto now = clock::now();
+  if (last_callback_.time_since_epoch().count() != 0) {
+    max_gap_ = std::max(max_gap_, now - last_callback_);
+  }
+  last_callback_ = now;
+  if (now - last_report_ < std::chrono::seconds(1)) {
+    return;
+  }
+  const auto gap_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(max_gap_).count();
+  if (late_frames_ || gap_ms > 50.0) {
+    REXAPU_WARN("audio out: {} late frames (played as silence), longest callback gap {:.1f} ms, queue up to {}",
+                late_frames_, gap_ms, max_queued_);
+  }
+  last_report_ = now;
+  late_frames_ = 0;
+  max_queued_ = 0;
+  max_gap_ = {};
```

```patch
+// test_read_delay_us_per_mb: a slower disk, for measuring loads on a fast one.
+void TestReadDelay(uint32_t bytes) {
+  if (int32_t us = REXCVAR_GET(test_read_delay_us_per_mb); us > 0) {
+    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(int64_t(us) * bytes / (1 << 20)));
+  }
+}
+
+// Reads the game asked to be asynchronous (a file opened without
+// FILE_SYNCHRONOUS_IO_*): done in order on one guest thread of their own, then
+// completed as the console does: the status block, the event, the file's wait
+// handle and completion ports, and the APC to the thread that asked.
+class AsyncReader {
+ public:
+  struct Job {
+    object_ref<XFile> file;
+    object_ref<XEvent> event;
+    object_ref<XThread> thread;
+    uint32_t buffer, length;
+    uint64_t offset;
+    uint32_t apc_routine, apc_context, io_status_block;
+  };
+
+  // Never destroyed: its thread may still be waiting when the process exits.
+  static AsyncReader& Get() {
+    static AsyncReader* reader = new AsyncReader;
+    return *reader;
+  }
+
+  void Push(Job job) {
+    {
+      std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
+      if (!thread_) {
+        thread_ = object_ref<XHostThread>(new XHostThread(REX_KERNEL_STATE(), 128 * 1024, 0,
+                                                          [this] { return Main(); }));
+        thread_->set_name("Async File Reads");
+        thread_->Create();
+      }
+      jobs_.push_back(std::move(job));
+    }
+    cv_.notify_one();
+  }
+
+ private:
+  int Main() {
+    while (true) {
+      Job job;
+      {
+        std::unique_lock lock(mutex_);
+        cv_.wait(lock, [&] { return !jobs_.empty(); });
+        job = std::move(jobs_.front());
+        jobs_.pop_front();
+      }
+      Run(job);
+    }
+    return 0;
+  }
+
+  void Run(Job& job) {
+    uint32_t bytes_read = 0;
+    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    // Completed below, once the status block is written.
+    X_STATUS result = job.file->Read(job.buffer, job.length, job.offset, &bytes_read,
+                                     job.apc_context, /*notify_completion=*/false);
+    TestReadDelay(bytes_read);
+    if (int32_t slow_ms = REXCVAR_GET(log_slow_reads); slow_ms > 0) {
+      double ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() -
+                                                            start)
+                      .count();
+      if (ms >= slow_ms) {
+        REXKRNL_INFO("slow read: {:.1f} ms, {} KB of {} on the I/O thread", ms,
+                     bytes_read / 1024, job.file->path());
+      }
+    }
+    if (job.io_status_block) {
+      auto* iosb = REX_KERNEL_MEMORY()->TranslateVirtual<X_IO_STATUS_BLOCK*>(job.io_status_block);
+      iosb->information = bytes_read;
+      // The status last: a game polling it then sees the count and the data.
+      std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
+      iosb->status = result;
+    }
+    job.file->Complete(job.apc_context, bytes_read, result);
+    if (job.event) {
+      job.event->Set(0, false);
+    }
+    if (job.apc_routine && job.apc_context && result == X_STATUS_SUCCESS && job.thread) {
+      job.thread->EnqueueApc(job.apc_routine, job.apc_context, job.io_status_block, 0);
+    }
+  }
+
+  std::mutex mutex_;
+  std::condition_variable cv_;
+  std::deque<Job> jobs_;
+  object_ref<XHostThread> thread_;
+};
+
+}  // namespace
```

```patch
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 00:57:43 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] content: Xenia and console save headers no longer hide the
 save

ListContent counted a header read's failure as success (its Win32
codes don't set the high bit XSUCCEEDED tests), so a save folder
```

```patch
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:18:02 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Support Ninja Gaiden II shaders

- memory export (eA/eM#) to guest memory through a buffer device address,
  after Xenia's SPIR-V translator (NG2 skins on the GPU with it)
- vertex shaders get the vertex index in r0.x, as on the hardware
- vertex fetches without a declared element read guest memory through the
  vertex fetch constants; full fetches latch the index for mini fetches
- bool constants addressed like the hardware (256 bits, VS 0-127, PS 128-255)
- bool-conditional exec blocks (cexec) are conditional; CondExecPredCleanEnd
  ends the shader
- 32 texture fetch slots, generic names for slots without reflection data,
  1D textures (with offset) sampled as Nx1 2D textures
- vertex shaders sample mip 0 (no implicit LOD outside pixel shaders)
- NG2 vertex input locations (up to four position/normal streams) when
  UNLEASHED_RECOMP is not defined; unmapped semantics are an error
- 8-byte aligned 64-bit constant loads (Vulkan validation)
- SPIR-V compile failures are fatal in release builds

The DXIL (D3D12) path is not updated for the new shared constant layout.

+uint memExportSwap32(uint v, uint endian)
+{
+    if (endian == 1)
+        return ((v & 0x00FF00FFu) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00FF00FFu);
+    if (endian == 3)
+        return (v << 16) | (v >> 16);
+    if (endian == 2 || endian == 4 || endian == 5)
+        return (v << 24) | ((v & 0xFF00u) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0xFF00u) | (v >> 24);
+    return v;
+}
+
+uint4 memExportSwap(uint4 v, uint endian)
+{
+    v = uint4(memExportSwap32(v.x, endian), memExportSwap32(v.y, endian),
+        memExportSwap32(v.z, endian), memExportSwap32(v.w, endian));
+    if (endian == 4)
+        v = v.yxwz;
+    else if (endian == 5)

+    return v;

+// Vertex fetch without a declared element, after Xenia: the fetch constant
+// gives the dword address (dword 0) and endianness (dword 1, bits 0-1).
+uint vfetchLoad(uint byteAddress, uint endian)
+{
+#ifdef __spirv__
+    return memExportSwap32(vk::RawBufferLoad<uint>(g_GuestMemoryBase + byteAddress), endian);
+#else
+    return 0;
+#endif

+float4 vfetchNormalize(uint4 c, uint4 widths, bool isSigned, bool isInteger)
+{
+    float4 v;
+    if (isSigned)
+    {
+        int4 shift = 32 - int4(widths);
+        int4 sc = (int4(c) << shift) >> shift;
+        v = float4(sc);
+        if (!isInteger)
+            v = max(v / float4((1u << (widths - 1u)) - 1u), -1.0);
+    }
+    else
+    {
+        v = float4(c);
+        if (!isInteger)
+            v /= float4((1u << widths) - 1u);
+    }
+    return v;
+}

+float4 vfetchRaw(float indexValue, uint fetchConstant, uint stride, int offset, uint format,
+    bool isSigned, bool isInteger, int expAdjust, bool isIndexRounded)
+{
+#ifdef __spirv__
+    uint2 constant = g_VertexFetch(fetchConstant);
+#else
+    uint2 constant = 0;
+#endif
+    uint endian = constant.y & 3;
+    int index = int(floor(isIndexRounded ? indexValue + 0.5 : indexValue));
+    uint address = (constant.x & 0xFFFFFFFCu) + uint(index * int(stride) + offset) * 4;
+
+    uint d0 = vfetchLoad(address, endian);
+    // Components a format lacks read as 0 (the fetch swizzle supplies constants).
+    float4 v = 0.0;
+    switch (format)
+    {

+        v = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0, d0 >> 8, d0 >> 16, d0 >> 24) & 0xFF, 8, isSigned, isInteger);
+        break;
+    case 7: // k_2_10_10_10
+        v = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0 & 0x3FF, (d0 >> 10) & 0x3FF, (d0 >> 20) & 0x3FF, d0 >> 30),
+            uint4(10, 10, 10, 2), isSigned, isInteger);
+        break;
+    case 16: // k_10_11_11
+        v.xyz = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0 & 0x7FF, (d0 >> 11) & 0x7FF, d0 >> 22, 0),
+            uint4(11, 11, 10, 1), isSigned, isInteger).xyz;
+        break;
+    case 17: // k_11_11_10
+        v.xyz = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0 & 0x3FF, (d0 >> 10) & 0x7FF, d0 >> 21, 0),
+            uint4(10, 11, 11, 1), isSigned, isInteger).xyz;
+        break;
+    case 25: // k_16_16
+        v.xy = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0 & 0xFFFF, d0 >> 16, 0, 0), 16, isSigned, isInteger).xy;
+        break;
+    case 26: // k_16_16_16_16
+    {
+        uint d1 = vfetchLoad(address + 4, endian);
+        v = vfetchNormalize(uint4(d0 & 0xFFFF, d0 >> 16, d1 & 0xFFFF, d1 >> 16), 16, isSigned, isInteger);
+        break;
+    }
+    case 31: // k_16_16_FLOAT
+        v.xy = f16tof32(uint2(d0, d0 >> 16));
+        break;
+    case 32: // k_16_16_16_16_FLOAT
+    {
+        uint d1 = vfetchLoad(address + 4, endian);
+        v = f16tof32(uint4(d0, d0 >> 16, d1, d1 >> 16));
+        break;
+    }
+    case 33: // k_32
+        v.x = isSigned ? float(int(d0)) : float(d0);
+        break;
+    case 34: // k_32_32

+    case 35: // k_32_32_32_32

+    case 38: // k_32_32_32_32_FLOAT

+// A fetch of a declared vertex element, set up at draw time from the vertex
+// declaration. Components a format lacks read as (0, 0, 0, 1) like D3D9.
+float4 vfetchElement(float indexValue, uint slot)
+{
+#ifdef __spirv__
+    uint4 element = g_VertexElement(slot);
+#else
+    uint4 element = 0;
+#endif
+    uint flags = element.w;
+    float4 v = vfetchRaw(indexValue, element.x, element.z, int(element.y), flags & 0xFF,
+        (flags & 0x100) != 0, (flags & 0x200) != 0, 0, false);
+    uint format = flags & 0xFF;
+    // Formats with fewer than four components get w = 1.
+    if (format == 36 || format == 37 || format == 57 || format == 25 || format == 31 ||
+        format == 33 || format == 34 || format == 16 || format == 17)
+        v.w = 1.0;
+    if ((flags & 0x800) != 0)
+        v = v.zyxw;
+    return v;
+}

+// Memory export (eA/eM#), after Xenia's SPIR-V translator. eA comes from
+// "mad eA, index, const0100, stream constant": x = base in dwords, y = element
+// index, z = format info, w = element count. Elements of 32, 64 and 128 bits
+// are stored; narrower formats would need atomics and are skipped.
+
+// Converts to integers of the given widths (D3D rounding) and masks them.
+uint4 memExportToInt(float4 v, uint4 widths, bool isSigned, bool isNorm)
+{
+    v = select(isnan(v), 0.0, v);
+    uint4 mask = (1u << widths) - 1u;
+    if (isSigned)
+    {
+        float4 maxValue = float4((1u << (widths - 1u)) - 1u);
+        if (isNorm)
+            v = clamp(v, -1.0, 1.0) * maxValue;
+        else
+            v = clamp(v, -maxValue - 1.0, maxValue);
+        return uint4(int4(v + select(v < 0.0, -0.5, 0.5))) & mask;
+    }
+    float4 maxValue = float4(mask);
+    if (isNorm)
+        v = saturate(v) * maxValue;
+    else
+        v = clamp(v, 0.0, maxValue);
+    return uint4(v + 0.5) & mask;
+}
+
+void memExportStore(uint byteAddress, uint dword)
+{
+#ifdef __spirv__
+    vk::RawBufferStore<uint>(g_GuestMemoryBase + byteAddress, dword);
+#endif
+}
+
+void memExport(float4 eA, float4 eM0, float4 eM1, float4 eM2, float4 eM3, float4 eM4, uint written)
+{
+    uint4 address = asuint(eA);
+    if (written == 0 || any((address >> uint4(30, 23, 23, 23)) != uint4(1, 0x96, 0x96, 0x96)))
+        return;
+
+    uint info = address.z;
+    uint format = (info >> 8) & 0x3F;
+    bool isSigned = (info & (1u << 16)) != 0;
+    bool isNorm = (info & (1u << 17)) == 0;
+    bool swapRedBlue = (info & (1u << 19)) != 0;
+    uint endian = info & 7;
+    uint index = address.y & 0x7FFFFF;
+    uint count = address.w & 0x7FFFFF;
+
+    float4 elements[5] = { eM0, eM1, eM2, eM3, eM4 };
+    for (uint i = 0; i < 5; i++)
+    {
+        if ((written & (1u << i)) == 0 || index + i >= count)
+            continue;
+
+        float4 e = swapRedBlue ? elements[i].zyxw : elements[i];
+        uint4 packed = 0;
+        uint dwords = 1;
+        switch (format)
+        {
+        case 6: // k_8_8_8_8
+        case 14: // k_8_8_8_8_A
+        case 50: // k_8_8_8_8_AS_16_16_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, 8, isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.x = c.x | (c.y << 8) | (c.z << 16) | (c.w << 24);
+            break;
+        }
+        case 7: // k_2_10_10_10
+        case 54: // k_2_10_10_10_AS_16_16_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, uint4(10, 10, 10, 2), isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.x = c.x | (c.y << 10) | (c.z << 20) | (c.w << 30);
+            break;
+        }
+        case 16: // k_10_11_11
+        case 55: // k_10_11_11_AS_16_16_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, uint4(11, 11, 10, 1), isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.x = c.x | (c.y << 11) | (c.z << 22);
+            break;
+        }
+        case 17: // k_11_11_10
+        case 56: // k_11_11_10_AS_16_16_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, uint4(10, 11, 11, 1), isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.x = c.x | (c.y << 10) | (c.z << 21);
+            break;
+        }
+        case 25: // k_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, 16, isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.x = c.x | (c.y << 16);
+            break;
+        }
+        case 26: // k_16_16_16_16
+        {
+            uint4 c = memExportToInt(e, 16, isSigned, isNorm);
+            packed.xy = c.xz | (c.yw << 16);
+            dwords = 2;
+            break;
+        }
+        case 31: // k_16_16_FLOAT
+            packed.x = f32tof16(e.x) | (f32tof16(e.y) << 16);
+            break;
+        case 32: // k_16_16_16_16_FLOAT
+            packed.xy = f32tof16(e.xz) | (f32tof16(e.yw) << 16);
+            dwords = 2;
+            break;
+        case 36: // k_32_FLOAT
+            packed.x = asuint(e.x);
+            break;
+        case 37: // k_32_32_FLOAT
+            packed.xy = asuint(e.xy);
+            dwords = 2;
+            break;
+        case 38: // k_32_32_32_32_FLOAT
+            packed = asuint(e);
+            dwords = 4;
+            break;
+        default:
+            return;
+        }
+
+        packed = memExportSwap(packed, endian);
+        uint byteAddress = (address.x << 2) + (index + i) * dwords * 4;
+        for (uint j = 0; j < dwords; j++)
+            memExportStore(byteAddress + j * 4, packed[j]);
+    }
+}

 #endif
 
 #endif

+// Memory export (eA = 32, eM0-eM4 = 33-37). Writing eA starts a new export:
+// whatever the previous one wrote to eM# is stored first. Code emitted here
+// lands before the write itself. Returns "" for other registers.
+const char* ShaderRecompiler::memExportRegister(uint32_t exportRegister)
+{
+    static const char* const names[] = { "eA", "eM0", "eM1", "eM2", "eM3", "eM4" };
+    if (exportRegister < 32 || exportRegister > 37)
+        return "";
+
+    hasMemExport = true;
+    // Bit 5 of the spec constants mask (unused by the shaders) tells the
+    // renderer the shader writes memory.
+    specConstantsMask |= SPEC_CONSTANT_MEMEXPORT;
+    indent();
+    if (exportRegister == 32)
+        out += "memExport(eA, eM0, eM1, eM2, eM3, eM4, eMWritten); eMWritten = 0;\n";
+    else
+        println("eMWritten |= {}u;", 1u << (exportRegister - 33));
+
+    return names[exportRegister - 32];
+}
```

```patch
 // Vertex fetch without a declared element, after Xenia: the fetch constant
 // gives the dword address (dword 0) and endianness (dword 1, bits 0-1).
+// Alpha test with RB_COLORCONTROL's function (never, <, ==, <=, >, !=, >=,
+// always) against the reference value.
+bool alphaTestPasses(float alpha)
+{
+#ifdef __spirv__
+    uint func = g_AlphaFunc;
+#else
+    uint func = 6;
+#endif
+    float reference = g_AlphaThreshold;
+    switch (func)
+    {
+    case 0: return false;
+    case 1: return alpha < reference;
+    case 2: return alpha == reference;
+    case 3: return alpha <= reference;
+    case 4: return alpha > reference;
+    case 5: return alpha != reference;
+    case 6: return alpha >= reference;
+    default: return true;
+    }
+}
```

```patch
From 536c273e3cdb586bc0fad5712d8124881c12e69e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: gambuzino24 <gambuzino24@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 21:50:23 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Barycentric variant: Flat taken off the inputs read per
 vertex

DXC decorates a nointerpolation input read with GetAttributeAtVertex both
Flat and PerVertexKHR. With both, RADV killed nearly every pixel of the
shaders that hide cut-off parts (characters' bodies missing). Without Flat
they draw normally there. Taken out of the SPIR-V before it is encoded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

     fclose(file);
 }
 
+// DXC decorates a nointerpolation input read with GetAttributeAtVertex both
+// Flat and PerVertexKHR: Flat is taken out, the input is read per vertex.
+static std::vector<uint32_t> withoutFlatOnPerVertexInputs(const void* spirv, size_t size)
+{
+    constexpr uint32_t OP_DECORATE = 71, DECORATION_FLAT = 14, DECORATION_PER_VERTEX = 5285, HEADER_WORDS = 5;
+
+    const uint32_t* words = static_cast<const uint32_t*>(spirv);
+    const size_t count = size / sizeof(uint32_t);
+
+    std::vector<uint32_t> perVertex;
+    for (size_t i = HEADER_WORDS; i < count; i += words[i] >> 16)
+    {
+        if ((words[i] & 0xFFFF) == OP_DECORATE && words[i + 2] == DECORATION_PER_VERTEX)
+            perVertex.push_back(words[i + 1]);
+    }
+
+    std::vector<uint32_t> out(words, words + HEADER_WORDS);
+    for (size_t i = HEADER_WORDS; i < count; i += words[i] >> 16)
+    {
+        const bool isFlatOnPerVertex = (words[i] & 0xFFFF) == OP_DECORATE && words[i + 2] == DECORATION_FLAT &&
+            std::find(perVertex.begin(), perVertex.end(), words[i + 1]) != perVertex.end();
+        if (!isFlatOnPerVertex)
+            out.insert(out.end(), words + i, words + i + (words[i] >> 16));
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+

 {
     uint8_t* data = nullptr;
```

`src/aspect.cpp`:

```cpp
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// Aspect Ratio (Display page of RECOMP SETTINGS): the game draws for 16:9.
//
// 3D: the game's only 16:9 float (0x8228EBFC) is the aspect its projections
// are built with (the camera update sub_822FA8C8 builds them from the field
// of view at camera +176). It is set to the chosen aspect: wider screens see
// more at the sides; narrower ones (16:10, 4:3) keep the sides and get a taller
// field of view (Vert+), set around that update.
//
// The picture is still drawn into the game's 16:9 targets, and the
// presenter stretches it to the chosen aspect (src/gpu/video.cpp), so 2D is
// drawn squeezed by the inverse, around the centre of the game's 1280x720
// space, to look right once stretched: sprites and gauges (their four
// pixel-space vertices, 24 bytes apart, at the quad draw sub_8368EFF8),
// text (the 4x4 transform the text pass hands sub_8370DD70 by value in
// r4..r10, a row-vector matrix: column 0 the high words of r4/r6/r8/r10,
// column 1 their low words) and movies (sub_83660FC8 builds a movie's quad
// in clip space: four vertices 16 bytes apart).

#include "aspect.h"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>

#include <fmt/format.h>
#include <rex/logging.h>

#include <rex/cvar.h>
#include <rex/hook.h>

#include "gpu/guest.h"

REXCVAR_DEFINE_INT32(aspect_ratio, 0, "Display", "0: 16:9, 1: 16:10, 2: 21:9, 3: 32:9, 4: 4:3");

namespace {

using ng2::guest::Load32;
using ng2::guest::Virtual;

constexpr float kNative = 16.0f / 9.0f;
constexpr uint32_t kAspectConstant = ng2::aspect::kConstantAddress;
constexpr uint32_t kCameraFov = 176;

float LoadFloat(uint32_t address) {
  uint32_t bits = Load32(address);
  float value;
  std::memcpy(&value, &bits, 4);
  return value;
}

void StoreFloat(uint32_t address, float value) {
  uint32_t bits;
  std::memcpy(&bits, &value, 4);
  uint8_t* p = Virtual(address);
  p[0] = uint8_t(bits >> 24), p[1] = uint8_t(bits >> 16), p[2] = uint8_t(bits >> 8),
  p[3] = uint8_t(bits);
}

// How much 2D is squeezed along each axis.
struct Squeeze {
  float x = 1.0f, y = 1.0f;
  bool active() const { return x != 1.0f || y != 1.0f; }
};

Squeeze CurrentSqueeze() {
  float aspect = ng2::aspect::Aspect();
  Squeeze s;
  if (aspect > kNative) {
    s.x = kNative / aspect;
  } else if (aspect < kNative) {
    s.y = aspect / kNative;
  }
  return s;
}


// The 2D pass (sub_8368E2E8) draws 91 buckets in order; bucket i's items
// are a list (item +4: next) from [kBuckets + parity * 728 + 4 * i],
// parity = [kBuckets + 1456] ^ 1, each drawn by its vtable +4 method. Every
// bucket also holds a placeholder (draw method 0x83705CE8). The bucket of
// the item being drawn says what it is (the HUD's pieces have their own).
constexpr uint32_t kBuckets = 0x85325ED8;
constexpr int kBucketCount = 91;
constexpr uint32_t kPlaceholderDraw = 0x83705CE8;

std::unordered_map<uint32_t, int> g_itemBucket;  // render pass thread
int g_drawBucket = -1;
uint32_t g_drawItem = 0;

// Where a HUD item stays when the screen is wider (or taller): -1 at the
// left (top) edge, 1 at the right (bottom), 0 the centre. Decided by the
// first piece it draws.
struct Anchor {
  int x = 0, y = 0;
  // Placed by the game's projection (already where the widened 3D picture
  // has it): kept at its own centre (cx, cy), its shape squeezed about that.
  bool projected = false;
  float cx = 0.0f, cy = 0.0f;
};
std::unordered_map<uint32_t, Anchor> g_itemAnchor;
bool g_hud = false;  // the gameplay HUD is up this frame (health bar buckets 57-59)
std::atomic<bool> g_hudShown{false};  // the same, for other threads

// Diagnostic (NG2_BUCKET_LOG=1): each bucket's 2D box, once a second.
struct Box {
  float x0 = 1e9f, y0 = 1e9f, x1 = -1e9f, y1 = -1e9f;
  int draws = 0;
};
Box g_boxes[kBucketCount];


std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point g_boxesLogged;
bool BucketLog() {
  static const bool on = std::getenv("NG2_BUCKET_LOG") != nullptr;
  return on;
}

void ScanBuckets() {
  g_itemBucket.clear();
  uint32_t parity = Load32(kBuckets + 1456) ^ 1;
  uint32_t heads = kBuckets + parity * 728;
  bool hud = false;
  for (int i = 0; i < kBucketCount; i++) {
    int guard = 0;
    for (uint32_t item = Load32(heads + 4 * i); item && guard < 4096; item = Load32(item + 4), guard++) {
      g_itemBucket[item] = i;
      if (BucketLog()) {
        // Each bucket's draw methods, once (what draws a HUD piece).
        static std::unordered_map<uint64_t, bool> seen;
        uint32_t method = Load32(Load32(item) + 4);
        if (seen.try_emplace(uint64_t(i) << 32 | method, true).second) {
          REXLOG_INFO("2D bucket {} draw method {:08X}", i, method);
        }
      }
      if (i >= 57 && i <= 59 && Load32(Load32(item) + 4) != kPlaceholderDraw) {
        hud = true;
      }
    }
  }
  g_hud = hud;
  g_hudShown.store(hud, std::memory_order_relaxed);
  // Decided again each frame: the items are render copies from a pool, so
  // an address can be another piece the next frame.
  g_itemAnchor.clear();
}



void NotePoint(float x, float y) {
  if (g_drawBucket < 0) {
    return;
  }
  if (!BucketLog()) {
    return;
  }
  Box& b = g_boxes[g_drawBucket];
  b.x0 = std::min(b.x0, x), b.x1 = std::max(b.x1, x);
  b.y0 = std::min(b.y0, y), b.y1 = std::max(b.y1, y);
}

void NoteQuad(uint32_t vertices, uint32_t stride) {
  if (g_drawBucket < 0) {
    return;
  }
  if (BucketLog()) {
    g_boxes[g_drawBucket].draws++;
  }
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    NotePoint(LoadFloat(vertices + i * stride), LoadFloat(vertices + i * stride + 4));
  }
}

void LogBoxes() {
  auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  if (!BucketLog() || now - g_boxesLogged < std::chrono::seconds(1)) {
    return;
  }
  g_boxesLogged = now;
  std::string line;
  for (int i = 0; i < kBucketCount; i++) {
    Box& b = g_boxes[i];
    if (b.draws) {
      line += fmt::format(" {}:{}[{:.0f},{:.0f}-{:.0f},{:.0f}]", i, b.draws, b.x0, b.y0, b.x1, b.y1);
    }
    b = Box{};
  }
  REXLOG_INFO("2D buckets{}:{}", g_hud ? " (HUD)" : "", line);
}

// Draws an item with its bucket known.
void DrawTagged(PPCContext& ctx, uint8_t* base, void (*draw)(PPCContext&, uint8_t*)) {
  auto it = g_itemBucket.find(ctx.r3.u32);
  int saved = g_drawBucket;
  uint32_t savedItem = g_drawItem;
  g_drawBucket = it == g_itemBucket.end() ? -1 : it->second;
  g_drawItem = ctx.r3.u32;
  draw(ctx, base);
  g_drawBucket = saved;
  g_drawItem = savedItem;
}

// Buckets of the HUD's left column (karma panel 39-41, health bar and ki
// 57-61), and menus' (never moved: pause and inventory 49-50, in-game
// options 70-72, loading and title screens 20, 80-86).
constexpr int kKarmaBucket = 40;
bool LeftHud(int bucket) {
  return (bucket >= 39 && bucket <= 41) || (bucket >= 57 && bucket <= 61);
}
// The frame-rate counter's layer (src/perf_overlay.cpp): the top left corner.
constexpr uint32_t kCounterLayer = 0x15;
bool MenuBucket(int bucket) {
  return bucket == 20 || bucket == 49 || bucket == 50 || (bucket >= 70 && bucket <= 72) ||
         (bucket >= 80 && bucket <= 86);
}

// The combo counter ("12 HITS", its number at 210,240 and its word at 340,240,
// and their animated copies) is drawn with the karma panel too: it stays with
// the left column, not where the bow's reticle would be.
bool ComboCounter(float x, float y) {
  return x < 1280.0f / 3.0f && y > 190.0f && y < 290.0f;
}

// The anchor of the item being drawn, from a point of its first piece.
Anchor ItemAnchor(float x, float y) {
  // The counter's words (copies of its text item, which keep its layer at
  // +8; the game files them in another bucket) are at the top.
  if (g_drawItem && Load32(g_drawItem + 8) == kCounterLayer && y < 48.0f) {
    return {-1, -1};
  }
  if (!g_hud || g_drawBucket < 0 || MenuBucket(g_drawBucket)) {
    return {};
  }
  auto [it, added] = g_itemAnchor.try_emplace(g_drawItem);
  if (added) {
    Anchor& a = it->second;
    if (g_drawBucket == kKarmaBucket && y >= 480.0f) {
      a = {0, 1};  // the boss's health bar, drawn with the karma panel: bottom centre
    } else if (g_drawBucket == kKarmaBucket && x > 2560.0f / 3.0f) {
      a = {1, -1};  // the projectile count, top right
    } else if (g_drawBucket == kKarmaBucket && y > 175.0f && !ComboCounter(x, y)) {
      a = {0, 0, true, x, y};  // the bow's aiming reticle, where the aim points
    } else if (LeftHud(g_drawBucket)) {
      a = {-1, -1};
    } else {
      a.x = x < 1280.0f / 3.0f ? -1 : x > 2560.0f / 3.0f ? 1 : 0;
      a.y = y < 720.0f / 3.0f ? -1 : y > 1440.0f / 3.0f ? 1 : 0;
    }
  }
  return it->second;
}

// v squeezed by k (the presenter stretches it back), kept at its edge.
float Map(float v, float k, int anchor, float size) {
  if (anchor < 0) {
    return v * k;
  }
  if (anchor > 0) {
    return size - (size - v) * k;
  }
  return size * 0.5f + (v - size * 0.5f) * k;
}
// The same as an affine map v * k + offset.
float MapOffset(float k, int anchor, float size) {
  return anchor < 0 ? 0.0f : anchor > 0 ? size * (1.0f - k) : size * 0.5f * (1.0f - k);
}

// Squeezes a quad (4 vertices, x and y first) in place. A quad covering the
// whole screen (a background, a fade) is instead zoomed evenly, about the
// centre, until it covers the wider (or taller) screen: cropped, not
// stretched out of shape.
void SqueezeQuad(uint32_t vertices, uint32_t stride, Squeeze s) {
  float x0 = 1e9f, x1 = -1e9f, y0 = 1e9f, y1 = -1e9f;
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    float x = LoadFloat(vertices + i * stride), y = LoadFloat(vertices + i * stride + 4);
    x0 = std::min(x0, x), x1 = std::max(x1, x), y0 = std::min(y0, y), y1 = std::max(y1, y);
  }
  float kx = s.x, ky = s.y;
  if (x0 <= 1.0f && x1 >= 1279.0f && y0 <= 1.0f && y1 >= 719.0f) {
    float cover = 1.0f / std::min(s.x, s.y);
    kx = cover * s.x, ky = cover * s.y;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      uint32_t at = vertices + i * stride;
      StoreFloat(at, Map(LoadFloat(at), kx, 0, 1280.0f));
      StoreFloat(at + 4, Map(LoadFloat(at + 4), ky, 0, 720.0f));
    }
    return;
  }
  Anchor a = ItemAnchor((x0 + x1) * 0.5f, (y0 + y1) * 0.5f);
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    uint32_t at = vertices + i * stride;
    float x = LoadFloat(at), y = LoadFloat(at + 4);
    if (a.projected) {
      StoreFloat(at, a.cx + (x - a.cx) * kx);
      StoreFloat(at + 4, a.cy + (y - a.cy) * ky);
    } else {
      StoreFloat(at, Map(x, kx, a.x, 1280.0f));
      StoreFloat(at + 4, Map(y, ky, a.y, 720.0f));
    }
  }
}

// High and low 32-bit halves of a 64-bit register as floats.
float High(uint64_t value) {
  uint32_t bits = uint32_t(value >> 32);
  float f;
  std::memcpy(&f, &bits, 4);
  return f;
}
float Low(uint64_t value) {
  uint32_t bits = uint32_t(value);
  float f;
  std::memcpy(&f, &bits, 4);
  return f;
}
uint64_t Pair(float high, float low) {
  uint32_t h, l;
  std::memcpy(&h, &high, 4);
  std::memcpy(&l, &low, 4);
  return uint64_t(h) << 32 | l;
}

}  // namespace

namespace ng2::aspect {

namespace {
bool g_constantWritable = false;
}  // namespace

bool HudShown() {
  return g_hudShown.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

float SqueezeX() {
  return CurrentSqueeze().x;
}
float SqueezeY() {
  return CurrentSqueeze().y;
}

uint32_t AspectIndex() {
  int32_t index = REXCVAR_GET(aspect_ratio);
  return index >= 0 && index < 5 ? uint32_t(index) : 0;
}

void SetConstantWritable(bool writable) {
  g_constantWritable = writable;
}

// Width / height of the window (0 until the first present).
std::atomic<float> g_windowShape{0.0f};

void SetWindowShape(uint32_t width, uint32_t height) {
  if (height) {
    g_windowShape.store(float(width) / float(height), std::memory_order_relaxed);
  }
}

float Aspect() {
  if (!g_constantWritable) {
    return kNative;  // the 3D would stay 16:9
  }
  switch (AspectIndex()) {
    case 1:
      return 16.0f / 10.0f;
    case 2: {
      // "21:9" monitors are a little wider than 21:9 (2560x1080 2.37, 3440x1440
      // 2.39, 3840x1600 2.4): in a window of about that shape, its own shape,
      // so the picture fills it; else (a 21:9 picture in a 16:9 window) 21:9.
      float window = g_windowShape.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
      return window >= 2.2f && window <= 2.6f ? window : 21.0f / 9.0f;
    }
    case 3:
      return 32.0f / 9.0f;
    case 4:
      return 4.0f / 3.0f;
    default:
      return kNative;
  }
}

}  // namespace ng2::aspect

// The camera's update (sub_822FA8C8, r3 the camera): its projection
// (sub_822FB378) and right after it its other frustums (camera +688, +752)
// are built from the field of view at +176, so a narrower aspect's taller
// one is set around the whole update; the aspect constant is set first.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_822FA8C8);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_822FA8C8) {
  float aspect = ng2::aspect::Aspect();
  if (LoadFloat(kAspectConstant) != aspect && ng2::aspect::g_constantWritable) {
    StoreFloat(kAspectConstant, aspect);
  }
  uint32_t fovAddress = ctx.r3.u32 + kCameraFov;
  if (aspect >= kNative || !ctx.r3.u32) {
    __imp__sub_822FA8C8(ctx, base);
    return;
  }
  float fov = LoadFloat(fovAddress);
  float taller = 2.0f * std::atan(std::tan(fov * 0.5f) * kNative / aspect);
  StoreFloat(fovAddress, taller);
  __imp__sub_822FA8C8(ctx, base);
  // The update may add an effect's change to it (sub_822FDE08): kept.
  StoreFloat(fovAddress, fov + (LoadFloat(fovAddress) - taller));
}

// A sprite's or gauge's quad, in 1280x720 pixels.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368EFF8);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368EFF8) {
  Squeeze s = CurrentSqueeze();
  uint32_t vertices = ctx.r4.u32;
  if (!s.active() || !vertices) {
    if (vertices) {
      NoteQuad(vertices, 24);
    }
    __imp__sub_8368EFF8(ctx, base);
    return;
  }
  constexpr uint32_t kStride = 24, kCount = 4;
  NoteQuad(vertices, kStride);
  uint8_t saved[kStride * kCount];
  std::memcpy(saved, Virtual(vertices), sizeof(saved));
  SqueezeQuad(vertices, kStride, s);
  __imp__sub_8368EFF8(ctx, base);
  std::memcpy(Virtual(vertices), saved, sizeof(saved));
}

// A string's transform.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8370DD70);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8370DD70) {
  Squeeze s = CurrentSqueeze();
  NotePoint(High(ctx.r10.u64), Low(ctx.r10.u64));
  if (s.active()) {
    Anchor a = ItemAnchor(High(ctx.r10.u64), Low(ctx.r10.u64));
    for (PPCRegister* row : {&ctx.r4, &ctx.r6, &ctx.r8}) {
      row->u64 = Pair(High(row->u64) * s.x, Low(row->u64) * s.y);
    }
    // The translation row.
    float offsetX = a.projected ? a.cx * (1.0f - s.x) : MapOffset(s.x, a.x, 1280.0f);
    float offsetY = a.projected ? a.cy * (1.0f - s.y) : MapOffset(s.y, a.y, 720.0f);
    ctx.r10.u64 = Pair(High(ctx.r10.u64) * s.x + offsetX, Low(ctx.r10.u64) * s.y + offsetY);
  }
  __imp__sub_8370DD70(ctx, base);
}

// A movie's quad, in clip space.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_83660FC8);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_83660FC8) {
  uint32_t out = ctx.r3.u32;
  __imp__sub_83660FC8(ctx, base);
  Squeeze s = CurrentSqueeze();
  if (!s.active() || !out) {
    return;
  }
  constexpr uint32_t kStride = 16, kCount = 4;
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kCount; i++) {
    uint32_t at = out + i * kStride;
    StoreFloat(at, LoadFloat(at) * s.x);
    StoreFloat(at + 4, LoadFloat(at + 4) * s.y);
  }
}

// The 2D pass: its items' buckets first.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368E2E8);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368E2E8) {
  ScanBuckets();
  __imp__sub_8368E2E8(ctx, base);
  g_drawBucket = -1;
  LogBoxes();
}

// The items' draw methods: sprite, gauge, text, rectangle, and the other.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368FDB0);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368FDB0) {
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8368FDB0);
}
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368F578);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368F578) {
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8368F578);
}
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8370D5C0);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8370D5C0) {
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8370D5C0);
}
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368E888);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368E888) {
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8368E888);
}
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368EA58);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368EA58) {
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8368EA58);
}

// An untextured rectangle (sub_8368E888 builds it: 4 vertices 16 bytes
// apart, x, y, z, colour), e.g. the health bar's red damage piece.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8368E500);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8368E500) {
  Squeeze s = CurrentSqueeze();
  uint32_t vertices = ctx.r4.u32;
  constexpr uint32_t kStride = 16, kCount = 4;
  if (vertices) {
    NoteQuad(vertices, kStride);
  }
  if (!s.active() || !vertices) {
    __imp__sub_8368E500(ctx, base);
    return;
  }
  uint8_t saved[kStride * kCount];
  std::memcpy(saved, Virtual(vertices), sizeof(saved));
  SqueezeQuad(vertices, kStride, s);
  __imp__sub_8368E500(ctx, base);
  std::memcpy(Virtual(vertices), saved, sizeof(saved));
}

// A clip item (draw method sub_8369FB08: it saves the device's scissor and
// sets one from the item's x, y, width and height at +16..+28; its partner
// sub_8369FBE8 puts the saved one back). The boss's health bar fill is
// drawn whole and clipped to what is left this way. Its draw is tagged as
// the others, and the rect it sets (D3D's SetScissorRect(device, RECT*),
// in the game's 1280x720 pixels) is mapped as the item's pieces are.
REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8369FB08);
bool g_inClipItem = false;
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8369FB08) {
  g_inClipItem = true;
  DrawTagged(ctx, base, __imp__sub_8369FB08);
  g_inClipItem = false;
}

REX_EXTERN(__imp__sub_8375C550);
REX_HOOK_RAW(sub_8375C550) {
  Squeeze s = CurrentSqueeze();
  uint32_t rect = ctx.r4.u32;
  if (!s.active() || !g_inClipItem || !g_drawItem || !rect) {
    __imp__sub_8375C550(ctx, base);
    return;
  }
  int32_t r[4];
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    r[i] = int32_t(Load32(rect + 4 * i));
  }
  if (r[0] <= 0 && r[1] <= 0 && r[2] >= 1280 && r[3] >= 720) {
    __imp__sub_8375C550(ctx, base);  // the whole screen: left as it is
    return;
  }
  Anchor a = ItemAnchor((r[0] + r[2]) * 0.5f, (r[1] + r[3]) * 0.5f);
  auto at = [](float v) { return std::max(0, int32_t(std::lround(v))); };
  auto mapX = [&](float v) { return a.projected ? a.cx + (v - a.cx) * s.x : Map(v, s.x, a.x, 1280.0f); };
  auto mapY = [&](float v) { return a.projected ? a.cy + (v - a.cy) * s.y : Map(v, s.y, a.y, 720.0f); };
  int32_t mapped[4] = {at(mapX(float(r[0]))), at(mapY(float(r[1]))), at(mapX(float(r[2]))),
                       at(mapY(float(r[3])))};
  auto store = [](uint32_t address, int32_t value) {
    uint8_t* p = Virtual(address);
    uint32_t v = uint32_t(value);
    p[0] = uint8_t(v >> 24), p[1] = uint8_t(v >> 16), p[2] = uint8_t(v >> 8), p[3] = uint8_t(v);
  };
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    store(rect + 4 * i, mapped[i]);
  }
  __imp__sub_8375C550(ctx, base);
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    store(rect + 4 * i, r[i]);
  }
}
```
