`src/gpu/guest.h`:

```h
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// Reading guest memory from the renderer: big-endian loads from virtual and
// physical addresses.

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include <rex/runtime.h>
#include <rex/system/xmemory.h>
#include <rex/types.h>

namespace ng2::guest {

// Memory::TranslateVirtual's result without its calls: only the heap at
// 0xE0000000-0xFFCFFFFF has a host offset (a page, where the host's allocation
// granularity is over 4 KB, as on Windows), the same for the whole run.
struct Bases {
  uint8_t* virtualBase;
  uint8_t* physicalBase;
  uint32_t e0Offset;
};
inline const Bases& GetBases() {
  static const Bases bases = [] {
    auto* memory = rex::Runtime::instance()->memory();
    return Bases{memory->virtual_membase(), memory->physical_membase(),
                 uint32_t(memory->TranslateVirtual<uint8_t*>(0xE0000000) -
                          (memory->virtual_membase() + 0xE0000000u))};
  }();
  return bases;
}

inline uint8_t* Virtual(uint32_t address) {
  const Bases& b = GetBases();
  return b.virtualBase + address +
         (address >= 0xE0000000u && address < 0xFFD00000u ? b.e0Offset : 0u);
}

inline uint8_t* Physical(uint32_t address) {
  return GetBases().physicalBase + (address & 0x1FFFFFFF);
}

inline uint32_t Load32(uint32_t address) {
  return rex::byte_swap(*reinterpret_cast<const uint32_t*>(Virtual(address)));
}

inline uint16_t Load16(uint32_t address) {
  return rex::byte_swap(*reinterpret_cast<const uint16_t*>(Virtual(address)));
}

inline int32_t LoadS32(uint32_t address) {
  return int32_t(Load32(address));
}

inline float LoadFloat(uint32_t address) {
  uint32_t bits = Load32(address);
  float value;
  __builtin_memcpy(&value, &bits, sizeof(value));
  return value;
}

// D3D device fields (docs/d3d-map-*.md).
namespace device {
constexpr uint32_t kRenderTargets = 0x3090;  // 4 x D3DSurface*
constexpr uint32_t kDepthStencil = 0x30A0;   // D3DSurface*
}  // namespace device

// A texture's GPUTEXTURE_FETCH_CONSTANT (6 dwords) sits at +28.
constexpr uint32_t kTextureFetchConstant = 28;

}  // namespace ng2::guest

```

`src/gpu/menu_label.cpp`:

```cpp
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// The title menu's "Xbox LIVE Marketplace" picture becomes "RECOMP SETTINGS"
// and the unused "EXIT DEMO" one "EXIT GAME" (src/recomp_settings.cpp), made
// from the game's own letters: the other
// entries' pictures share one 8-bit atlas, one 90-pixel band per entry, in
// the same font. Each word there is split into its letters at the columns
// with the fewest bright pixels, and the new text is laid out from those
// columns (letter, outline and glow), so it takes the menu's palettes like
// the rest. Nothing of the game's art is stored here.

#include "menu_label.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#define XXH_INLINE_ALL
#include <xxhash.h>

namespace ng2::video {
namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kWidth = 520;
constexpr uint32_t kBand = 90;
constexpr uint64_t kAtlasHash = 0x3737e258b350fa36;   // 520x990, the entries' atlas
constexpr uint64_t kLabelHash = 0xf8fb387ec4883ffc;   // 520x90, Xbox LIVE Marketplace
// The other languages' atlases and Marketplace labels (Japanese keeps the
// English label; Portuguese and Simplified Chinese use the English ones).
constexpr uint64_t kOtherAtlases[] = {
    0xd09f6e653f0c44df,  // Japanese
    0x7ba39c742e71ab0f,  // German
    0x0bf716435014362e,  // French
    0xe34071b489a2d830,  // Spanish
    0x4d6f66ffa5fd5392,  // Italian
    0xeb91498647389ab9,  // Korean
    0x298f406c6f391369,  // Traditional Chinese
    0x24ae84c08b328168,  // Polish
    0xccf0c19dcdd7dcb0,  // Russian
};
constexpr uint64_t kOtherLabels[] = {
    0x4774ba1f7e83c512,  // German
    0x9ab60305171f1595,  // French
    0x6f37d128acb6719b,  // Spanish
    0x214c148a5445623e,  // Italian
    0xa75b722fe3c99c52,  // Korean
    0x6a908aa5f96e35ce,  // Traditional Chinese
    0x2bb41db4e7d2702a,  // Polish
    0xef9883b77fd3105f,  // Russian
};
template <size_t N>
bool OneOf(uint64_t hash, const uint64_t (&list)[N]) {
  return std::find(std::begin(list), std::end(list), hash) != std::end(list);
}
constexpr std::string_view kText = "RECOMP SETTINGS";
// The atlas's first entry, EXIT DEMO, isn't used by the retail menu: it
// becomes the exit entry's label (src/recomp_settings.cpp).
constexpr std::string_view kExitText = "EXIT GAME";
// The atlas's entries, top to bottom.
constexpr std::string_view kWords[] = {
    "EXIT DEMO", "NEW GAME", "LOAD GAME", "LEADERBOARDS", "NINJA CINEMA", "OPTIONS", "MISSIONS",
    "PATH OF THE ACOLYTE", "PATH OF THE WARRIOR", "PATH OF THE MENTOR", "PATH OF THE MASTER NINJA"};
constexpr uint8_t kClear = 255;  // outside the picture
constexpr uint8_t kPlate = 0;    // the dark plate behind the words
constexpr uint32_t kSpace = 16;  // columns between words

std::vector<uint8_t> g_atlas;  // the English atlas's pixels, once seen
bool g_atlasMissing = false;   // another language's, and the English one not found

struct Glyph {
  uint32_t band, begin, end;  // columns
};

bool IsLetter(uint8_t v) {
  return v != kClear && v != kPlate && (v <= 70 || v >= 110);
}

// The columns of each of the atlas's words, and of each letter that splits
// cleanly from its word.
std::map<std::string, Glyph, std::less<>> FindGlyphs() {
  std::map<std::string, Glyph, std::less<>> glyphs;
  // EXIT DEMO last: its letters split less cleanly than the others'.
  for (uint32_t i = 1; i <= std::size(kWords); i++) {
    uint32_t band = i % std::size(kWords);
    const uint8_t* pixels = g_atlas.data() + band * kBand * kWidth;
    // Words: runs of columns holding letter pixels.
    std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>> runs;
    bool inside = false;
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x <= kWidth; x++) {
      bool ink = false;
      for (uint32_t y = 0; x < kWidth && y < kBand && !ink; y++) {
        ink = IsLetter(pixels[y * kWidth + x]);
      }
      if (ink && !inside) {
        runs.emplace_back(x, x);
      } else if (!ink && inside) {
        runs.back().second = x;
      }
      inside = ink;
    }
    // Stray columns (EXIT DEMO has one at its left edge) aren't words.
    std::erase_if(runs, [](const auto& run) { return run.second - run.first < 4; });
    std::vector<std::string_view> parts;
    for (std::string_view words = kWords[band]; !words.empty();) {
      size_t space = words.find(' ');
      parts.push_back(words.substr(0, space));
      words = space == std::string_view::npos ? std::string_view() : words.substr(space + 1);
    }
    if (runs.size() != parts.size()) {
      continue;
    }
    for (size_t w = 0; w < parts.size(); w++) {
      auto [begin, end] = runs[w];
      glyphs.try_emplace(std::string(parts[w]), Glyph{band, begin, end});
      size_t letters = parts[w].size();
      // Bright pixels per column, smoothed; the letters' joins are its
      // lowest points.
      std::vector<float> profile(end - begin);
      for (uint32_t x = begin; x < end; x++) {
        uint32_t count = 0;
        for (uint32_t y = 0; y < kBand; y++) {
          uint8_t v = pixels[y * kWidth + x];
          count += v >= 150 && v != kClear;
        }
        profile[x - begin] = float(count);
      }
      std::vector<float> smooth(profile.size());
      for (size_t i = 0; i < profile.size(); i++) {
        float left = i ? profile[i - 1] : 0.0f;
        float right = i + 1 < profile.size() ? profile[i + 1] : 0.0f;
        smooth[i] = left + 2.0f * profile[i] + right;
      }
      std::vector<uint32_t> order(smooth.size());
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < order.size(); i++) {
        order[i] = i;
      }
      std::stable_sort(order.begin(), order.end(),
                       [&](uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return smooth[a] < smooth[b]; });
      std::vector<uint32_t> cuts;
      for (uint32_t c : order) {
        if (cuts.size() + 1 >= letters) {
          break;
        }
        if (c < 6 || c + 6 > smooth.size()) {
          continue;
        }
        if (std::all_of(cuts.begin(), cuts.end(),
                        [&](uint32_t x) { return (c > x ? c - x : x - c) >= 10; })) {
          cuts.push_back(c);
        }
      }
      if (cuts.size() + 1 != letters) {
        continue;
      }
      std::sort(cuts.begin(), cuts.end());
      uint32_t from = begin;
      for (size_t i = 0; i < letters; i++) {
        uint32_t to = i < cuts.size() ? begin + cuts[i] : end;
        glyphs.try_emplace(std::string(1, parts[w][i]), Glyph{band, from, to});
        from = to;
      }
    }
  }
  return glyphs;
}

// A label into pixels (kWidth x kBand), false if a letter is missing: its
// words as the atlas has them where it does, else letter by letter.
bool Compose(std::string_view text, uint8_t* pixels) {
  auto glyphs = FindGlyphs();
  std::vector<const Glyph*> pieces;  // nullptr: a space
  for (std::string_view words = text; !words.empty();) {
    size_t space = words.find(' ');
    std::string_view word = words.substr(0, space);
    words = space == std::string_view::npos ? std::string_view() : words.substr(space + 1);
    if (!pieces.empty()) {
      pieces.push_back(nullptr);
    }
    if (auto it = glyphs.find(word); it != glyphs.end()) {
      pieces.push_back(&it->second);
      continue;
    }
    for (char c : word) {
      auto it = glyphs.find(std::string_view(&c, 1));
      if (it == glyphs.end()) {
        return false;
      }
      pieces.push_back(&it->second);
    }
  }
  uint32_t width = 0;
  for (const Glyph* piece : pieces) {
    width += piece ? piece->end - piece->begin : kSpace;
  }
  if (width > kWidth) {
    return false;
  }
  // The plate's rows, from the NEW GAME entry.
  std::array<bool, kBand> plateRows{};
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < kBand; y++) {
    const uint8_t* row = g_atlas.data() + (kBand + y) * kWidth;
    plateRows[y] = std::find(row, row + kWidth, kPlate) != row + kWidth;
  }
  std::memset(pixels, kClear, kWidth * kBand);
  uint32_t x = (kWidth - width) / 2;
  for (const Glyph* piece : pieces) {
    if (!piece) {
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kSpace; i++, x++) {
        for (uint32_t y = 0; y < kBand; y++) {
          pixels[y * kWidth + x] = plateRows[y] ? kPlate : kClear;
        }
      }
      continue;
    }
    const Glyph& glyph = *piece;
    for (uint32_t gx = glyph.begin; gx < glyph.end; gx++, x++) {
      for (uint32_t y = 0; y < kBand; y++) {
        pixels[y * kWidth + x] = g_atlas[(glyph.band * kBand + y) * kWidth + gx];
      }
    }
  }
  return true;
}

// The header picture: "RECOMP SETTINGS" from the atlas's letters, scaled to
// the header's letter size, with the plate dropped, the letter faces and
// outlines brought to the header's levels and a soft glow around them.
constexpr uint64_t kHeaderHash = 0x3e4f94c916758ea1;  // 172x58, OPTIONS
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderWidth = 172, kHeaderHeight = 58;
// The other languages' Options headers (Japanese and French keep the
// English one; Korean's isn't a picture of these).
struct OtherHeader {
  uint32_t width;
  uint64_t hash;
};
constexpr OtherHeader kOtherHeaders[] = {
    {200, 0x90036f17f3198265},  // German
    {200, 0x26dec7b46f1fc9a3},  // Spanish
    {200, 0x615b10d2d40dfb86},  // Italian
    {94, 0xb90e89d7dc897ad8},   // Traditional Chinese
    {172, 0x880058569d76308a},  // Polish
    {230, 0x6294a9b09f954a41},  // Russian
};
constexpr float kHeaderScale = 0.92f;  // header letters / atlas letters
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderTop = 14, kHeaderMargin = 12;
constexpr int kGlowRadius = 4;
constexpr float kGlowLevel = 70.0f;

// The in-game list's header ("IN-GAME MANUAL AND OPTIONS", 521x58), in the
// same lettering at the same size and place: ours goes in as it is, the rest
// left clear.
constexpr uint64_t kInGameHeaderHash = 0xc16cba91cd852335;
constexpr uint32_t kInGameHeaderWidth = 521;
// The other languages' in-game headers (Portuguese and Simplified Chinese use
// the English one).
constexpr OtherHeader kOtherInGameHeaders[] = {
    {600, 0x739f598f81405715},  // Japanese
    {600, 0xa88403e6cece4b2f},  // German
    {521, 0x106c505107bf91e2},  // French
    {600, 0x05e5802de7f5b991},  // Spanish
    {600, 0x200d43fdfe4ce181},  // Italian
    {600, 0x1f011959bbf09487},  // Korean
    {600, 0xa3210211f7dda0fa},  // Traditional Chinese
    {600, 0x28278a87628524b5},  // Polish
    {600, 0x477b96a506485d61},  // Russian
};

// Set by the menu, read where textures are made.
std::atomic<bool> g_headerWanted = false;
std::atomic<bool> g_inGameHeaderWanted = false;
std::atomic<uint32_t> g_headerGeneration = 0;

// A box blur, each way.
std::vector<float> Blur(const std::vector<float>& image, uint32_t width, uint32_t height) {
  std::vector<float> across(image.size()), out(image.size());
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x < width; x++) {
      float sum = 0.0f;
      for (int d = -kGlowRadius; d <= kGlowRadius; d++) {
        int sx = int(x) + d;
        sum += sx >= 0 && sx < int(width) ? image[y * width + sx] : 0.0f;
      }
      across[y * width + x] = sum / (2 * kGlowRadius + 1);
    }
  }
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x < width; x++) {
      float sum = 0.0f;
      for (int d = -kGlowRadius; d <= kGlowRadius; d++) {
        int sy = int(y) + d;
        sum += sy >= 0 && sy < int(height) ? across[sy * width + x] : 0.0f;
      }
      out[y * width + x] = sum / (2 * kGlowRadius + 1);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

bool MakeHeader(std::vector<uint8_t>& out, uint32_t& outWidth) {
  std::vector<uint8_t> label(kWidth * kBand);
  if (!Compose(kText, label.data())) {
    return false;
  }
  uint32_t x0 = kWidth, x1 = 0, y0 = kBand, y1 = 0;
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < kBand; y++) {
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x < kWidth; x++) {
      if (IsLetter(label[y * kWidth + x])) {
        x0 = std::min(x0, x), x1 = std::max(x1, x + 1);
        y0 = std::min(y0, y), y1 = std::max(y1, y + 1);
      }
    }
  }
  if (x0 >= x1) {
    return false;
  }
  outWidth = uint32_t(std::ceil(float(x1 - x0) * kHeaderScale)) + 2 * kHeaderMargin;
  uint32_t size = outWidth * kHeaderHeight;
  std::vector<float> value(size), mask(size);
  // Bilinear over the letter pixels only.
  for (uint32_t oy = 0; oy < kHeaderHeight; oy++) {
    for (uint32_t ox = 0; ox < outWidth; ox++) {
      float sx = float(x0) + (float(ox) - kHeaderMargin + 0.5f) / kHeaderScale - 0.5f;
      float sy = float(y0) + (float(oy) - kHeaderTop + 0.5f) / kHeaderScale - 0.5f;
      int ix = int(std::floor(sx)), iy = int(std::floor(sy));
      float fx = sx - float(ix), fy = sy - float(iy);
      float sum = 0.0f, weight = 0.0f;
      for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
        int x = ix + (k & 1), y = iy + (k >> 1);
        float w = ((k & 1) ? fx : 1.0f - fx) * ((k >> 1) ? fy : 1.0f - fy);
        if (x >= 0 && x < int(kWidth) && y >= 0 && y < int(kBand) &&
            IsLetter(label[y * kWidth + x])) {
          sum += float(label[y * kWidth + x]) * w;
          weight += w;
        }
      }
      if (weight > 0.5f) {
        value[oy * outWidth + ox] = sum / weight;
        mask[oy * outWidth + ox] = 1.0f;
      }
    }
  }
  std::vector<float> glow = Blur(Blur(mask, outWidth, kHeaderHeight), outWidth, kHeaderHeight);
  out.resize(size);
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    float v;
    if (mask[i] > 0.0f) {
      v = value[i] >= 110.0f ? 150.0f + (value[i] - 110.0f) * (105.0f / 145.0f)  // face
                             : 30.0f + value[i] * 0.7f;                         // outline
    } else {
      v = glow[i] * kGlowLevel;
    }
    out[i] = uint8_t(std::clamp(v, 0.0f, 255.0f));
  }
  return true;
}

}  // namespace

LabelResult RewriteMenuLabel(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint8_t* pixels, uint32_t* rows) {
  *rows = 0;
  if (width != kWidth || (height != kBand && height != kBand * std::size(kWords))) {
    return LabelResult::kUnchanged;
  }
  uint64_t hash = XXH3_64bits(pixels, size_t(width) * height);
  bool english = hash == kAtlasHash;
  if (english || OneOf(hash, kOtherAtlases)) {
    if (english) {
      g_atlas.assign(pixels, pixels + size_t(width) * height);
    }
    // (another language's: its own EXIT DEMO entry, in English letters)
    if (g_atlas.empty() || !Compose(kExitText, pixels)) {
      return LabelResult::kUnchanged;
    }
    *rows = kBand;
    return LabelResult::kRewritten;
  }
  if (hash != kLabelHash && !OneOf(hash, kOtherLabels)) {
    return LabelResult::kUnchanged;
  }
  if (g_atlas.empty()) {
    return g_atlasMissing ? LabelResult::kUnchanged : LabelResult::kRetry;
  }
  if (!Compose(kText, pixels)) {
    return LabelResult::kUnchanged;
  }
  *rows = kBand;
  return LabelResult::kRewritten;
}

bool NeedsEnglishAtlas(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, const uint8_t* pixels) {
  return width == kWidth && height == kBand * std::size(kWords) && g_atlas.empty() &&
         !g_atlasMissing && OneOf(XXH3_64bits(pixels, size_t(width) * height), kOtherAtlases);
}

bool SetEnglishAtlas(const uint8_t* pixels) {
  size_t size = size_t(kWidth) * kBand * std::size(kWords);
  if (XXH3_64bits(pixels, size) != kAtlasHash) {
    return false;
  }
  g_atlas.assign(pixels, pixels + size);
  return true;
}

void EnglishAtlasMissing() {
  g_atlasMissing = true;
}

void SetRecompHeader(bool on) {
  if (on != g_headerWanted) {
    g_headerWanted = on;
    g_headerGeneration++;
  }
}

void SetInGameRecompHeader(bool on) {
  if (on != g_inGameHeaderWanted) {
    g_inGameHeaderWanted = on;
    g_headerGeneration++;
  }
}

uint32_t MenuHeaderGeneration() {
  return g_headerGeneration;
}

bool IsMenuHeaderSize(uint32_t width, uint32_t height) {
  auto widthOf = [&](const OtherHeader& h) { return h.width == width; };
  return height == kHeaderHeight &&
         (width == kHeaderWidth || width == kInGameHeaderWidth ||
          std::any_of(std::begin(kOtherHeaders), std::end(kOtherHeaders), widthOf) ||
          std::any_of(std::begin(kOtherInGameHeaders), std::end(kOtherInGameHeaders), widthOf));
}

bool ReplaceMenuHeader(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, const uint8_t* pixels,
                       std::vector<uint8_t>& out, uint32_t& outWidth, MenuHeaderKind& kind) {
  kind = MenuHeaderKind::kNone;
  if (!IsMenuHeaderSize(width, height)) {
    return false;
  }
  uint64_t hash = XXH3_64bits(pixels, size_t(width) * height);
  bool other = std::any_of(std::begin(kOtherHeaders), std::end(kOtherHeaders),
                           [&](const OtherHeader& h) { return h.width == width && h.hash == hash; });
  if (hash == kHeaderHash || other) {
    kind = MenuHeaderKind::kOptions;
    return g_headerWanted && !g_atlas.empty() && MakeHeader(out, outWidth);
  }
  bool otherInGame =
      std::any_of(std::begin(kOtherInGameHeaders), std::end(kOtherInGameHeaders),
                  [&](const OtherHeader& h) { return h.width == width && h.hash == hash; });
  if (hash != kInGameHeaderHash && !otherInGame) {
    return false;
  }
  kind = MenuHeaderKind::kInGame;
  std::vector<uint8_t> header;
  uint32_t headerWidth = 0;
  if ( !g_inGameHeaderWanted || g_atlas.empty() || !MakeHeader(header, headerWidth) ||
      headerWidth > width) {
    return false;
  }
  out.assign(size_t(width) * height, 0);
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    std::memcpy(&out[size_t(y) * width], &header[size_t(y) * headerWidth], headerWidth);
  }
  outWidth = width;
  return true;
}


}  // namespace ng2::video
```

```h
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// The RECOMP SETTINGS and EXIT GAME title menu labels (menu_label.cpp).

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace ng2::video {

enum class LabelResult { kUnchanged, kRewritten, kRetry };

// Called with each decoded 8-bit texture's base level: keeps the title
// menu's letter atlas and rewrites its EXIT DEMO entry, and rewrites the
// Marketplace label (kRetry: seen before the atlas, upload it again later).
// rows: how many rows from the top were rewritten, for the mips.
LabelResult RewriteMenuLabel(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint8_t* pixels, uint32_t* rows);

// In the other languages the menu's own atlas and labels are the language's,
// but the English atlas is loaded with them (one package for every language),
// and its letters make RECOMP SETTINGS and EXIT GAME there too: true when this
// is another language's atlas and the English one isn't known yet, then
// SetEnglishAtlas with the English atlas's pixels (false: not it).
// EnglishAtlasMissing: it wasn't found, so nothing waits for it.
bool NeedsEnglishAtlas(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, const uint8_t* pixels);
bool SetEnglishAtlas(const uint8_t* pixels);
void EnglishAtlasMissing();

// The Options screen's "OPTIONS" header (a 172x58 8-bit picture) reads
// "RECOMP SETTINGS" while ours is open: a wider picture made from the
// atlas's letters in the header's look. ReplaceMenuHeader gives it for the
// header's base level (false: keep the game's); MenuHeaderGeneration changes
// whenever the wanted picture does, so a cached one is made again. The
// in-game list's header (521x58, same lettering) reads the same while ours is
// shown there, at its own width.
void SetRecompHeader(bool on);
void SetInGameRecompHeader(bool on);
uint32_t MenuHeaderGeneration();
// (kind: which header the picture is, ours or not.)
enum class MenuHeaderKind { kNone, kOptions, kInGame };
// Only a texture of one of these sizes can be a menu header (ReplaceMenuHeader).
bool IsMenuHeaderSize(uint32_t width, uint32_t height);
bool ReplaceMenuHeader(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, const uint8_t* pixels,
                       std::vector<uint8_t>& out, uint32_t& outWidth, MenuHeaderKind& kind);

}  // namespace ng2::video
```

`src/gpu/native_gpu.cpp`:

```cpp
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// The game's GPU without GPU emulation. The native renderer draws from the
// game's Direct3D calls (video.cpp); the rest of what Direct3D asks of a GPU
// is done here, at the Direct3D calls that ask for it, so nothing reads the
// command stream Direct3D writes:
//
// - The command stream: Direct3D still writes and kicks it (CP_RB_WPTR); a
//   kick reports it consumed at once (the read pointer write-back Direct3D
//   checks for room). No packet is looked at.
// - What the hardware would do with the stream that the game can see, as
//   steps in call order on a guest thread of our own (interrupts call into
//   the game), each as soon as its call is made: the renderer draws from
//   copies taken at the calls, so the work before a step is always done.
//     InsertFence (8375F810)          the status word to the fence block's
//                                     +4, then the fence counter to +0
//     the callback handshake          scratch 4 / 5 = callback / argument,
//       (8375FD30)                    scratch 0 = the CPU mask, the
//                                     interrupt (the game's handler runs the
//                                     callback and clears scratch 0); then
//                                     waited back to 0, scratch 4 poisoned
//     the flip (8376A518)             scratch 1 (flip pending) = 1; after its
//                                     handshake (the swap callback 8376A380)
//                                     waited back to 0, which the vblank
//                                     handler does once the flip is due: the
//                                     vsync wait. The steps after it wait too.
//   The scratch registers are mirrored at the block device+10900 points to
//   (scratch n at +4n), the fence block at device+10896.
// - Vblanks: the game's interrupt callback at the video mode's rate.
// - What the stream also holds needs nothing here: waits on GPU registers
//   (cache coherency), cache flush events, the gamma ramp (video.cpp reads
//   the device's copy), XE_SWAP (the Swap hook presents), draws and state.
//   A census of every packet type over boot and Chapter 1's first fight found
//   no other memory write and no occlusion query. Not done: the GPU counter
//   timestamps (EVENT_WRITE_SHD initiator bit 31) Swap writes when
//   device+21608 is set and sub_83771778 in device mode 2; neither happened.
// Each step was checked against the packets TU3's functions write.

#include "native_gpu.h"
#include "video.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>

#include <rex/chrono/clock.h>
#include <rex/cvar.h>
#include <rex/kernel/xboxkrnl/video.h>
#include <rex/logging.h>
#include <rex/memory/utils.h>
#include <rex/system/function_dispatcher.h>
#include <rex/system/interfaces/graphics.h>
#include <rex/system/kernel_state.h>
#include <rex/system/xmemory.h>
#include <rex/system/xthread.h>

REXCVAR_DECLARE(bool, vsync);
REXCVAR_DECLARE(int32_t, present_mode);
// Frame Pacing: Auto puts the guest's vblanks on the display's own refreshes
// (video.cpp's display clock: one every N of them, just after one) when N refreshes come within 2% of the video mode's rate, so no
// frame is shown twice for the drift between the two clocks; else, and with
// Timer, they come from a timer at the video mode's rate.
REXCVAR_DEFINE_INT32(frame_pacing, 1, "Video", "0: auto (on the display's refreshes), 1: timer (the game's)");
// Where in a refresh a locked vblank falls (% of it after the refresh): just
// after it, the frame has nearly the whole refresh to be drawn and shown at
// the next one (at 50, half: a slower frame misses it, waits a refresh).
REXCVAR_DEFINE_INT32(frame_pacing_phase, 5, "Video", "Auto frame pacing: % of a refresh after it");

namespace ng2::gpu {
namespace {

using rex::X_STATUS;

constexpr uint32_t kCpRbWptr = 0x01C5;

// Device fields (big-endian words).
constexpr uint32_t kDevFenceBlock = 10896;    // pointer: +0 fence counter, +4 status word
constexpr uint32_t kDevScratchBlock = 10900;  // pointer: scratch n at +4n
constexpr uint32_t kDevFenceCounter = 10908;  // the fence InsertFence writes
constexpr uint32_t kDevStatusBits = 14904;    // (& 3) | device+48: the status word
constexpr uint32_t kDevStatusBase = 48;

class NativeGraphicsSystem;
std::atomic<NativeGraphicsSystem*> g_system{nullptr};

class NativeGraphicsSystem final : public rex::system::IGraphicsSystem {
 public:
  ~NativeGraphicsSystem() override { Shutdown(); }

  // The renderer owns the window and presents.
  rex::X_STATUS SetupPresentation(rex::ui::WindowedAppContext*) override {
    return X_STATUS_SUCCESS;
  }

  rex::X_STATUS SetupGuestGpu(rex::runtime::FunctionDispatcher* dispatcher,
                              rex::system::KernelState* kernel) override {
    dispatcher_ = dispatcher;
    kernel_ = kernel;
    memory_ = dispatcher->memory();
    // The GPU registers: 0x7FC80000-0x7FCFFFFF.
    memory_->AddVirtualMappedRange(0x7FC80000, 0xFFFF0000, 0x0000FFFF, this, &ReadRegisterThunk,
                                   &WriteRegisterThunk);
    running_ = true;
    g_system = this;
    effect_thread_ = rex::system::object_ref<rex::system::XHostThread>(
        new rex::system::XHostThread(kernel_, 128 * 1024, 0, [this] { return EffectThread(); }));
    effect_thread_->set_name("GPU Steps");
    effect_thread_->Create();
    vsync_thread_ = rex::system::object_ref<rex::system::XHostThread>(
        new rex::system::XHostThread(kernel_, 128 * 1024, 0, [this] { return VsyncThread(); }));
    vsync_thread_->set_name("GPU VSync");
    vsync_thread_->Create();
    REXLOG_INFO("gpu: no GPU emulation (Direct3D's GPU side at its calls)");
    return X_STATUS_SUCCESS;
  }

  bool has_presentation() const override { return false; }

  void SetInterruptCallback(uint32_t callback, uint32_t user_data) override {
    interrupt_callback_ = callback;
    interrupt_data_ = user_data;
  }

  void InitializeRingBuffer(uint32_t, uint32_t) override {}

  void EnableReadPointerWriteBack(uint32_t ptr, uint32_t) override {
    rptr_writeback_.store(ptr, std::memory_order_release);
  }

  // Stops both threads and waits for them (the runtime frees this right after).
  void Shutdown() override {
    {
      std::lock_guard lock(steps_mutex_);
      if (!running_.exchange(false)) {
        return;
      }
    }
    g_system = nullptr;
    steps_cv_.notify_all();
    WakeWaits();
    for (auto* thread : {&effect_thread_, &vsync_thread_}) {
      if (*thread) {
        (*thread)->Wait(0, 0, 0, nullptr);
        thread->reset();
      }
    }
  }

  // --- The Direct3D calls ------------------------------------------------------

  void InsertFence(uint32_t device) {
    uint32_t block = Field(device, kDevFenceBlock);
    uint32_t counter = Field(device, kDevFenceCounter);
    uint32_t word = (Field(device, kDevStatusBits) & 3) | Field(device, kDevStatusBase);
    Step([this, block, word, counter] {
      Write32(block + 4, word);
      Write32(block, counter);
    });
  }

  // flags bit 1: the callback's interrupt; bit 2: wait for its handler, then
  // poison scratch 4; neither: both. CPU mask in flags bits 24-29 (none: CPU 2).
  void CallbackHandshake(uint32_t device, uint32_t flags, uint32_t callback, uint32_t argument) {
    if (!(flags & 6)) {
      flags |= 6;
    }
    uint32_t scratch = Field(device, kDevScratchBlock);
    uint32_t cpus = (flags >> 24) & 0x3F;
    if (!cpus) {
      cpus = 4;
    }
    Step([this, flags, scratch, callback, argument, cpus] {
      if (flags & 2) {
        Write32(scratch + 16, callback);
        Write32(scratch + 20, argument);
        Write32(scratch, cpus);
        for (uint32_t cpu = 0; cpu < 6; cpu++) {
          if (cpus & (1u << cpu)) {
            DispatchInterrupt(1, cpu);
          }
        }
      }
      if (flags & 4) {
        WaitWord(scratch, 0);
        Write32(scratch + 16, 0x0BADF00Du);
      }
    });
  }

  void FlipBegin(uint32_t device, uint32_t noWait) {
    if (noWait) {
      return;
    }
    uint32_t scratch = Field(device, kDevScratchBlock);
    Step([this, scratch] { Write32(scratch + 4, 1); });
  }

  void FlipWait(uint32_t device, uint32_t noWait) {
    if (noWait) {
      return;
    }
    uint32_t scratch = Field(device, kDevScratchBlock);
    Step([this, scratch] { WaitWord(scratch + 4, 0); });
  }

 private:
  // --- Registers ---------------------------------------------------------------

  static uint32_t ReadRegisterThunk(void*, void* context, uint32_t addr) {
    return static_cast<NativeGraphicsSystem*>(context)->ReadRegister(addr);
  }
  static void WriteRegisterThunk(void*, void* context, uint32_t addr, uint32_t value) {
    static_cast<NativeGraphicsSystem*>(context)->WriteRegister(addr, value);
  }

  // The answers the SDK's GraphicsSystem gives; the game reads the interrupt status.
  uint32_t ReadRegister(uint32_t addr) {
    uint32_t r = (addr & 0xFFFF) / 4;
    rex::system::X_VIDEO_MODE mode;
    switch (r) {
      case 0x0F00:  // RB_EDRAM_TIMING
        return 0x08100748;
      case 0x0F01:  // RB_BC_CONTROL
        return 0x0000200E;
      case 0x194C:  // R500_D1MODE_V_COUNTER
        rex::kernel::xboxkrnl::VdQueryVideoMode(&mode);
        return std::min(uint32_t(mode.display_height), 0x0FFFu);
      case 0x1951:  // interrupt status: vblank
        return 1;
      case 0x1961:  // AVIVO_D1MODE_VIEWPORT_SIZE
        rex::kernel::xboxkrnl::VdQueryVideoMode(&mode);
        return std::min(uint32_t(mode.display_width), 0x0FFFu) << 16 |
               std::min(uint32_t(mode.display_height), 0x0FFFu);
      default:
        return 0;
    }
  }

  // The kick: consumed as soon as written.
  void WriteRegister(uint32_t addr, uint32_t value) {
    if ((addr & 0xFFFF) / 4 != kCpRbWptr) {
      return;
    }
    if (uint32_t writeback = rptr_writeback_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
      rex::memory::store_and_swap<uint32_t>(memory_->TranslatePhysical(writeback), value);
    }
  }

  // --- Steps ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  uint32_t Field(uint32_t device, uint32_t offset) const {
    return rex::memory::load_and_swap<uint32_t>(memory_->TranslateVirtual(device + offset));
  }

  void Write32(uint32_t address, uint32_t value) {
    if (auto* p = memory_->TranslateVirtual<uint8_t*>(address)) {
      rex::memory::store_and_swap<uint32_t>(p, value);
    }
  }

  // A step runs once the draw worker (if on) has drawn the calls before it.
  void Step(std::function<void()> step) {
    uint64_t after = ng2::video::RecordedCalls();
    {
      std::lock_guard lock(steps_mutex_);
      steps_.push_back({after, std::move(step)});
    }
    steps_cv_.notify_one();
  }

  int EffectThread() {
    while (running_) {
      PendingStep step;
      {
        std::unique_lock lock(steps_mutex_);
        steps_cv_.wait(lock, [&] { return !steps_.empty() || !running_; });
        if (!running_) {
          break;
        }
        step = std::move(steps_.front());
        steps_.pop_front();
      }
      ng2::video::WaitForRecordedCalls(step.after);
      step.run();
    }
    return 0;
  }

  // Until a guest word reads `value`; the steps after it wait too. Looked at
  // again at each vblank (its handler is what clears the words waited on) and
  // every 100 us. At most 250 ms: a word nothing sets must not hold the game
  // for ever (logged).
  void WaitWord(uint32_t address, uint32_t value) {
    auto read = [&] {
      return rex::memory::load_and_swap<uint32_t>(memory_->TranslateVirtual(address));
    };
    if (read() == value) {
      return;
    }
    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    std::unique_lock lock(waits_mutex_);
    while (running_ && read() != value) {
      uint64_t seen = wakes_;
      waits_cv_.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::microseconds(100),
                         [&] { return wakes_ != seen || !running_; });
      if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start > std::chrono::milliseconds(250)) {
        if (read() != value) {
          REXLOG_WARN("gpu: a wait gave up after 250 ms: {:08X} reads {:08X}, not {:08X}", address,
                      read(), value);
        }
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  void WakeWaits() {
    {
      std::lock_guard lock(waits_mutex_);
      wakes_++;
    }
    waits_cv_.notify_all();
  }

  // The game's graphics interrupt callback on the calling guest thread. One at
  // a time, as on the console (both kinds go to CPU 2): the swap callback fills
  // the flip queue the vblank handler drains.
  void DispatchInterrupt(uint32_t source, uint32_t cpu) {
    if (!interrupt_callback_) {
      return;
    }
    std::lock_guard lock(interrupt_mutex_);
    auto* thread = rex::system::XThread::GetCurrentThread();
    if (!thread) {
      return;
    }
    thread->SetActiveCpu(cpu);
    uint64_t args[] = {source, interrupt_data_};
    dispatcher_->ExecuteInterrupt(thread->thread_state(), interrupt_callback_, args, 2);
  }

  // --- Vblanks -------------------------------------------------------------------

  // A sleep to a point, its last part spun (yielding): what a sleep may
  // overshoot by (Windows' sleeps are whole milliseconds).
  static void SleepNs(int64_t ns) {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    constexpr int64_t kSpin = 1'500'000;
#else
    constexpr int64_t kSpin = 300'000;
#endif
    int64_t end = ng2::video::DisplayClockNow() + ns;
    if (ns > kSpin) {
      std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::nanoseconds(ns - kSpin));
    }
    while (ng2::video::DisplayClockNow() < end) {
      std::this_thread::yield();
    }
  }

  // The video mode's rate (1 kHz with vsync off, as the SDK's worker did).
  int VsyncThread() {
    rex::system::X_VIDEO_MODE mode;
    rex::kernel::xboxkrnl::VdQueryVideoMode(&mode);
    double hz = std::max(1.0, double(float(mode.refresh_rate)));
    uint64_t frequency = rex::chrono::Clock::guest_tick_frequency();
    uint64_t vsyncInterval = std::max<uint64_t>(1, uint64_t(double(frequency) / hz));
    uint64_t freeInterval = std::max<uint64_t>(1, frequency / 1000);
    uint64_t last = rex::chrono::Clock::QueryGuestTickCount();
    const int64_t guestPeriodNs = int64_t(1e9 / hz);
    int64_t lastVblankNs = 0;
    bool lockedLogged = false;
    int64_t lastDrainNs = 0, drainPausedUntil = 0, drainPauseNs = 30'000'000'000;
    int drainsLogged = 0, drainsQuick = 0;
    bool skipNext = false;
    while (running_) {
      int64_t refreshNs = 0, periodNs = 0;
      // (FIFO and Mailbox only: there the presents reach the screen on its
      // refreshes; with V-Sync Off or Adaptive a late one shows at once)
      // NG2_TEST_GAMESCOPE_AUTO=1 (#46): Auto under gamescope too, where it
      // otherwise acts as Timer.
      static const bool gamescopeAuto = [] {
        const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_TEST_GAMESCOPE_AUTO");
        bool on = v && v[0] == '1';
        if (on) {
          REXLOG_INFO("video: test switch NG2_TEST_GAMESCOPE_AUTO=1");
        }
        return on;
      }();
      int32_t presentMode = REXCVAR_GET(present_mode);
      if (REXCVAR_GET(vsync) && REXCVAR_GET(frame_pacing) == 0 &&
          (!ng2::video::UnderGamescope() || gamescopeAuto) &&
          (presentMode == 1 || presentMode == 2) &&
          ng2::video::DisplayRefresh(&refreshNs, &periodNs)) {
        int64_t every = std::clamp<int64_t>((guestPeriodNs + periodNs / 2) / periodNs, 1, 4);
        int64_t step = periodNs * every;
        if (std::abs(step - guestPeriodNs) * 50 < guestPeriodNs) {
          if (!lockedLogged) {
            lockedLogged = true;
            REXLOG_INFO("gpu: vblanks on the display's refreshes ({:.3f} Hz, every {})",
                        1e9 / double(periodNs), every);
          }
          // frame_pacing_phase after one, the first at least half a step
          // after the last vblank (no two close together when the lock starts).
          int64_t phase = std::clamp<int32_t>(REXCVAR_GET(frame_pacing_phase), 0, 50);
          int64_t target = refreshNs + periodNs * phase / 100;
          while (target < lastVblankNs + step / 2) {
            target += step;
          }
          int64_t wait = target - ng2::video::DisplayClockNow();
          if (wait > 0) {
            SleepNs(wait);
          }
          lastVblankNs = ng2::video::DisplayClockNow();
          last = rex::chrono::Clock::QueryGuestTickCount();
          // A drain request (gamescope's, below) isn't acted on while locked:
          // taken here so it doesn't skip a vblank when the lock lets go.
          ng2::video::DrainRequested();
          DispatchInterrupt(0, 2);
          WakeWaits();
          continue;
        }
      }
      uint64_t interval = REXCVAR_GET(vsync) ? vsyncInterval : freeInterval;
      uint64_t now = rex::chrono::Clock::QueryGuestTickCount();
      // A frame ahead of the display under gamescope (video.cpp's
      // DrainRequested): the next step gives no vblank, once. Up to 3 come
      // within 3 s of each other (a queue two frames ahead takes two); a
      // fourth means skips don't help (a GPU too slow, Steam's frame
      // limiter): none for 30 s, doubling each time that happens again, up
      // to 10 min. A skip with no request for 3 s after it starts that over.
      bool drain = ng2::video::DrainRequested();  // (always taken: none left over)
      if (drain && REXCVAR_GET(vsync) && (presentMode == 1 || presentMode == 2)) {
        int64_t t = ng2::video::DisplayClockNow();
        bool quick = lastDrainNs && t - lastDrainNs < 3'000'000'000;
        if (lastDrainNs && !quick) {
          drainPauseNs = 30'000'000'000;  // (the last skips helped)
        }
        drainsQuick = quick ? drainsQuick + 1 : 0;
        if (drainsQuick >= 3) {
          drainPausedUntil = t + drainPauseNs;
          drainPauseNs = std::min<int64_t>(drainPauseNs * 2, 600'000'000'000);
          drainsQuick = 0;
          lastDrainNs = 0;
        } else if (t >= drainPausedUntil) {
          lastDrainNs = t;
          skipNext = true;
          if (drainsLogged < 20) {
            drainsLogged++;
            REXLOG_INFO("gpu: a vblank late, the game a frame ahead of the display");
          }
        }
      }
      if (now - last > std::max(interval * 4, frequency / 20)) {
        last = now - interval;  // far behind (a stall over 50 ms): no burst
      }
      if (now - last >= interval) {
        last += interval;
        if (skipNext) {  // (the drain: this step gives no vblank)
          skipNext = false;
          continue;
        }
        lastVblankNs = ng2::video::DisplayClockNow();
        DispatchInterrupt(0, 2);
        WakeWaits();
        continue;
      }
      auto left = std::chrono::nanoseconds(
          int64_t(double(last + interval - now) * 1e9 / double(frequency)));
#if defined(_WIN32)
      // Sleeps are whole milliseconds there (a vblank up to 1 ms late, as the SDK's worker).
      if (left >= std::chrono::milliseconds(1)) {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
      } else {
        std::this_thread::yield();
      }
#else
      std::this_thread::sleep_for(left);
#endif
    }
    return 0;
  }

  rex::runtime::FunctionDispatcher* dispatcher_ = nullptr;
  rex::system::KernelState* kernel_ = nullptr;
  rex::memory::Memory* memory_ = nullptr;
  std::atomic<bool> running_{false};
  std::atomic<uint32_t> rptr_writeback_{0};
  uint32_t interrupt_callback_ = 0, interrupt_data_ = 0;
  std::recursive_mutex interrupt_mutex_;
  std::mutex steps_mutex_;
  std::condition_variable steps_cv_;
  struct PendingStep {
    uint64_t after = 0;  // the draw worker's calls recorded before it
    std::function<void()> run;
  };
  std::deque<PendingStep> steps_;
  std::mutex waits_mutex_;
  std::condition_variable waits_cv_;
  uint64_t wakes_ = 0;
  rex::system::object_ref<rex::system::XHostThread> effect_thread_, vsync_thread_;
};

NativeGraphicsSystem* System() {
  return g_system.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
}

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<rex::system::IGraphicsSystem> CreateNativeGraphicsSystem() {
  return std::make_unique<NativeGraphicsSystem>();
}

void OnInsertFence(uint32_t device) {
  if (auto* s = System()) {
    s->InsertFence(device);
  }
}

void OnCallbackHandshake(uint32_t device, uint32_t flags, uint32_t callback, uint32_t argument) {
  if (auto* s = System()) {
    s->CallbackHandshake(device, flags, callback, argument);
  }
}

void OnFlipBegin(uint32_t device, uint32_t noWait) {
  if (auto* s = System()) {
    s->FlipBegin(device, noWait);
  }
}

void OnFlipWait(uint32_t device, uint32_t noWait) {
  if (auto* s = System()) {
    s->FlipWait(device, noWait);
  }
}

}  // namespace ng2::gpu
```

`src/gpu/prompts.cpp`:

```cpp
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// Button prompts (prompts.h). Every button the game shows, in the HUD and in
// its menus' texts (the @[pad:...] tags), is drawn from one 512x256 8-bit
// atlas (X, Y, B, A, the triggers and shoulders, the sticks, the d-pad, BACK
// and START) looked up in a 256x1 palette. Both are told apart by their
// content as the renderer loads them (CreateTexture); for the PlayStation,
// Nintendo or keyboard prompts the button cells are painted over with that
// set's pictures (prompt_sets.inc, from Xelu's CC0 prompts; the keyboard's are
// the keys bound to each button) and the set's colours written into the
// palette entries no other part of the atlas uses. The sticks' and the
// d-pad's pictures stay the game's. Nothing of the game's is shipped: only
// which cells and palette entries these are. The renderer checks both every
// frame with Generation() in their hash, so a change shows at once.

#include "prompts.h"

#include <atomic>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>

#include <rex/cvar.h>
#include <rex/logging.h>

#include "../controls.h"
#define XXH_INLINE_ALL
#include <xxhash.h>

REXCVAR_DEFINE_INT32(button_prompts, 0, "Display",
                     "0: Auto (the device in use), 1: Xbox, 2: PlayStation, 3: Nintendo, 4: Keyboard");

namespace ng2::prompts {

namespace {

struct PromptCell {
  uint16_t x, y, w, h;
};
#include "prompt_sets.inc"

constexpr uint64_t kAtlasHash = 0xEAF07C3B5DAB0BA1ull, kPaletteHash = 0xD1C855C91D4CEB65ull;
constexpr uint32_t kAtlasWidth = 512, kAtlasHeight = 256;
// The cells' surroundings cleared too (the game's shadows).
constexpr int kMargin = 8;
// The palette entries only the cleared cells use (from the game's atlas).
constexpr uint8_t kFree[] = {24,  35,  41,  60,  64,  67,  75,  76,  81,  84,  86,  91,  95,
                             97,  98,  99,  103, 110, 112, 113, 116, 121, 126, 127, 130, 131,
                             135, 136, 141, 144, 146, 149, 151, 158, 160, 162, 164, 167, 170,
                             172, 173, 177, 179, 180, 186, 188, 193, 198, 199, 203, 210, 212,
                             215, 218, 222, 231, 239, 244, 246, 247, 248, 251};
constexpr size_t kCellCount = sizeof(kPromptCells) / sizeof(kPromptCells[0]);

struct SetData {
  const uint8_t (*colors)[4];
  size_t colorCount;
  const uint8_t* const* cells;
};

SetData Data(Set set) {
  switch (set) {
    case Set::kPlayStation:
      return {kPlayStationColors, sizeof(kPlayStationColors) / 4, kPlayStationCells};
    case Set::kNintendo:
      return {kNintendoColors, sizeof(kNintendoColors) / 4, kNintendoCells};
    default:
      return {nullptr, 0, nullptr};
  }
}

static_assert(sizeof(kPlayStationColors) / 4 <= sizeof(kFree));
static_assert(sizeof(kNintendoColors) / 4 <= sizeof(kFree));
static_assert(sizeof(kKeyboardColors) / 4 <= sizeof(kFree));

// The atlas's cells, in kPromptCells' order: the button whose keys a keyboard
// cell shows, and the shape of its key picture.
enum class Shape { kSquare, kTall, kWide };
struct CellButton {
  const char* bind;
  Shape shape;
};
constexpr CellButton kCellButtons[] = {
    {"keybind_x", Shape::kSquare},           {"keybind_y", Shape::kSquare},
    {"keybind_b", Shape::kSquare},           {"keybind_a", Shape::kSquare},
    {"keybind_left_trigger", Shape::kTall},  {"keybind_right_trigger", Shape::kTall},
    {"keybind_left_shoulder", Shape::kWide}, {"keybind_right_shoulder", Shape::kWide},
    {"keybind_lstick_press", Shape::kSquare}, {"keybind_rstick_press", Shape::kSquare},
    {"keybind_back", Shape::kSquare},        {"keybind_start", Shape::kSquare},
};
static_assert(sizeof(kCellButtons) / sizeof(kCellButtons[0]) == kCellCount);

// The first key bound to a button, its modifiers left out ("Shift+Up": Up).
std::string FirstKey(const char* bind) {
  std::string keys = rex::cvar::GetFlagByName(bind);
  std::string first = keys.substr(0, keys.find(','));
  size_t plus = first.rfind('+');
  if (plus != std::string::npos && plus + 1 < first.size()) {
    first = first.substr(plus + 1);
  }
  while (!first.empty() && first.front() == ' ') {
    first.erase(first.begin());
  }
  while (!first.empty() && first.back() == ' ') {
    first.pop_back();
  }
  return first;
}

const KeyPictures& Key(const std::string& name) {
  for (const KeyPictures& key : kKeys) {
    if (name == key.name) {
      return key;
    }
  }
  return kKeys[sizeof(kKeys) / sizeof(kKeys[0]) - 1];  // the blank key
}

Set Chosen() {
  // NG2_PROMPTS=ps / nintendo / keys / xbox overrides the setting (tests).
  if (const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_PROMPTS"); v && *v) {
    switch (v[0]) {
      case 'p': case 'P': return Set::kPlayStation;
      case 'n': case 'N': return Set::kNintendo;
      case 'k': case 'K': return Set::kKeyboard;
      default: return Set::kXbox;
    }
  }
  switch (REXCVAR_GET(button_prompts)) {
    case 1: return Set::kXbox;
    case 2: return Set::kPlayStation;
    case 3: return Set::kNintendo;
    case 4: return Set::kKeyboard;
    default:
      switch (controls::ActiveDevice()) {
        case controls::Device::kPlayStation: return Set::kPlayStation;
        case controls::Device::kNintendo: return Set::kNintendo;
        case controls::Device::kKeyboard: return Set::kKeyboard;
        default: return Set::kXbox;
      }
  }
}

std::atomic<uint32_t> g_generation{0};
std::mutex g_mutex;
Set g_shown = Set::kXbox;          // (g_mutex)
std::string g_shownKeys;           // (g_mutex) the keyboard set's keys
std::string BoundKeys() {
  std::string keys;
  for (const CellButton& cell : kCellButtons) {
    keys += FirstKey(cell.bind) + ',';
  }
  return keys;
}

}  // namespace

Set CurrentSet() {
  std::lock_guard lock(g_mutex);
  return g_shown;
}

uint32_t Generation() {
  Set set = Chosen();
  std::string keys = set == Set::kKeyboard ? BoundKeys() : std::string();
  std::lock_guard lock(g_mutex);
  if (set != g_shown || keys != g_shownKeys) {
    g_shown = set;
    g_shownKeys = std::move(keys);
    g_generation++;
  }
  return g_generation.load();
}

bool Apply(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, Kind kind, uint8_t* data, uint64_t bytes) {
  bool atlas = kind == Kind::kIndex8 && width == kAtlasWidth && height == kAtlasHeight &&
               bytes >= uint64_t(width) * height &&
               XXH3_64bits(data, size_t(width) * height) == kAtlasHash;
  bool palette = !atlas && kind == Kind::kRGBA8 && width == 256 && height == 1 && bytes >= 1024 &&
                 XXH3_64bits(data, 1024) == kPaletteHash;
  if (!atlas && !palette) {
    return false;
  }
  Set set = CurrentSet();
  if (set == Set::kXbox) {
    return true;  // the game's own
  }
  if (set == Set::kKeyboard && atlas) {
    for (size_t c = 0; c < kCellCount; c++) {
      const PromptCell& cell = kPromptCells[c];
      for (int y = int(cell.y) - kMargin; y < int(cell.y + cell.h) + kMargin; y++) {
        for (int x = int(cell.x) - kMargin; x < int(cell.x + cell.w) + kMargin; x++) {
          if (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < int(width) && y < int(height)) {
            data[size_t(y) * width + x] = 0;
          }
        }
      }
      const KeyPictures& key = Key(FirstKey(kCellButtons[c].bind));
      Shape shape = kCellButtons[c].shape;
      const uint8_t* pixels = shape == Shape::kTall ? key.tall : shape == Shape::kWide ? key.wide : key.square;
      uint32_t w = shape == Shape::kTall ? kTallW : shape == Shape::kWide ? kWideW : kSquareW;
      uint32_t h = shape == Shape::kTall ? kTallH : shape == Shape::kWide ? kWideH : kSquareH;
      // Centred on the cell, within its cleared surroundings.
      int x0 = int(cell.x) + (int(cell.w) - int(w)) / 2, y0 = int(cell.y) + (int(cell.h) - int(h)) / 2;
      for (uint32_t y = 0; y < h; y++) {
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < w; x++) {
          int ax = x0 + int(x), ay = y0 + int(y);
          uint8_t v = pixels[y * w + x];
          if (v && ax >= 0 && ay >= 0 && ax < int(width) && ay < int(height)) {
            data[size_t(ay) * width + ax] = kFree[v - 1];
          }
        }
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
  if (atlas) {
    SetData d = Data(set);
    for (size_t c = 0; c < kCellCount; c++) {
      const PromptCell& cell = kPromptCells[c];
      for (int y = int(cell.y) - kMargin; y < int(cell.y + cell.h) + kMargin; y++) {
        for (int x = int(cell.x) - kMargin; x < int(cell.x + cell.w) + kMargin; x++) {
          if (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < int(width) && y < int(height)) {
            data[size_t(y) * width + x] = 0;
          }
        }
      }
      const uint8_t* pixels = d.cells[c];
      for (uint32_t y = 0; y < cell.h; y++) {
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < cell.w; x++) {
          uint8_t v = pixels[y * cell.w + x];
          data[size_t(cell.y + y) * width + cell.x + x] = v ? kFree[v - 1] : 0;
        }
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
  {
    // The game samples the palette swizzled (03012): stored B, G, R, A.
    SetData d = set == Set::kKeyboard ? SetData{kKeyboardColors, sizeof(kKeyboardColors) / 4, nullptr}
                                      : Data(set);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < d.colorCount; i++) {
      uint8_t* entry = data + kFree[i] * 4;
      entry[0] = d.colors[i][2];
      entry[1] = d.colors[i][1];
      entry[2] = d.colors[i][0];
      entry[3] = d.colors[i][3];
    }
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

}  // namespace ng2::prompts
```

```h
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// Button prompts: the PlayStation, Nintendo or keyboard buttons drawn instead
// of the Xbox 360's (prompts.cpp; the Button Prompts setting).

#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

namespace ng2::prompts {

enum class Set { kXbox, kPlayStation, kNintendo, kKeyboard };
enum class Kind { kIndex8, kRGBA8, kOther };

// The set the atlas is made with now.
Set CurrentSet();

// Changes whenever the set shown changes (the setting, the device in use, the
// keys bound): the renderer adds it to the atlas's and palette's hashes, which
// it checks every frame (renderer thread).
uint32_t Generation();

// From the texture loader, with a texture's untiled base level (the host
// format's bytes) before it is uploaded: the button atlas or its palette,
// rewritten for the set shown. True if it is one of them (the renderer
// checks those every frame).
bool Apply(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, Kind kind, uint8_t* data, uint64_t bytes);

}  // namespace ng2::prompts
```

`src/gpu/shader_cache.h`:

```h
// ng2 - Ninja Gaiden II static recompilation
//
// Shaders translated ahead of time by XenosRecomp (build step, see
// CMakeLists.txt). Entries are sorted by the XXH3 hash of the guest shader
// container; offsets point into the decompressed SPIR-V cache (smol-v
// encoded, zstd compressed as a whole). There is no DXIL: Vulkan only.

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

struct ShaderCacheEntry {
  const uint64_t hash;
  const uint32_t dxilOffset;
  const uint32_t dxilSize;
  const uint32_t spirvOffset;
  const uint32_t spirvSize;
  const uint32_t specConstantsMask;
  // Vertex fetch constants 0-95 the shader reads directly (vfetchRaw);
  // declared elements' streams come from the vertex declaration per draw.
  const uint32_t vertexFetchMask[3];
  // Float constant registers (0-255) and texture fetch slots (0-31) the shader
  // reads: the others aren't uploaded or looked up for its draws.
  const uint64_t floatConstantMask[4];
  const uint32_t textureSlotMask;
  // A variant that interpolates the part id itself with the GPU's
  // barycentrics (the shaders that hide cut-off parts), in the same cache; 0
  // bytes for the others.
  const uint32_t barycentricSpirvOffset;
  const uint32_t barycentricSpirvSize;
  struct GuestShader* guestShader;
};

extern ShaderCacheEntry g_shaderCacheEntries[];
// Defined by caches that carry floatConstantMask and textureSlotMask (an older
// one fails to link instead of drawing with no constants or textures).
extern const int g_shaderCacheHasMasks;
extern const size_t g_shaderCacheEntryCount;

extern const uint8_t g_compressedSpirvCache[];
extern const size_t g_spirvCacheCompressedSize;
extern const size_t g_spirvCacheDecompressedSize;
```

`src/gpu/shaders/copy_7e3_ms_ps.hlsl`:

```hlsl
// copy_7e3_ps from a multisampled target: each sample is 7e3 in EDRAM before
// the resolve averages them, so round every sample, then average.
#include "float7e3.hlsli"

struct PushConstants
{
    uint TextureIndex;
    int OffsetX;
    int OffsetY;
};

[[vk::push_constant]] ConstantBuffer<PushConstants> g_PushConstants;

Texture2DMS<float4> g_Texture2DMSDescriptorHeap[] : register(t0, space0);

float4 main(in float4 position : SV_Position) : SV_Target
{
    int2 texel = int2(position.xy) + int2(g_PushConstants.OffsetX, g_PushConstants.OffsetY);
    Texture2DMS<float4> source = g_Texture2DMSDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.TextureIndex];
    uint width, height, samples;
    source.GetDimensions(width, height, samples);
    float4 sum = 0.0;
    for (uint i = 0; i < samples; i++)
    {
        sum += Round7e3(source.Load(texel, i));
    }
    return sum / float(samples);
}

```

`src/gpu/shaders/copy_7e3_ps.hlsl`:

```hlsl
// Resolve of a 2_10_10_10_FLOAT (7e3) render target: the EDRAM holds 10-bit
// 7e3 color and 2-bit alpha, which the host's float16 target doesn't. Rounds
// the source texel the way packing it into EDRAM would, so passes reading the
// resolve (bloom, tone mapping) see what they would on the console.
#include "float7e3.hlsli"

struct PushConstants
{
    uint TextureIndex;
    int OffsetX;
    int OffsetY;
};

[[vk::push_constant]] ConstantBuffer<PushConstants> g_PushConstants;

Texture2D<float4> g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[] : register(t0, space0);

float4 main(in float4 position : SV_Position) : SV_Target
{
    int2 texel = int2(position.xy) + int2(g_PushConstants.OffsetX, g_PushConstants.OffsetY);
    return Round7e3(g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.TextureIndex].Load(int3(texel, 0)));
}
```

`src/gpu/shaders/float7e3.hlsli`:

```hlsli
// 2_10_10_10_FLOAT (7e3) color as the EDRAM stores it: clamped to
// [0, 31.875] (NaN and -0 to 0, as Xenia's NClamp) and rounded to 7e3, from
// Xenia's PreClampedFloat32To7e3 / Float7e3To32.
float Round7e3(float value)
{
    uint f = (value > 0.0) ? asuint(min(value, 31.875)) : 0u;
    uint denormal = ((f & 0x7FFFFFu) | 0x800000u) >> min(125u - (f >> 23), 24u);
    uint biased = f < 0x3E800000u ? denormal : f - (124u << 23);
    uint f10 = ((biased + 0x7FFFu + ((biased >> 16) & 1u)) >> 16) & 0x3FFu;
    uint exponent = f10 >> 7, mantissa = f10 & 0x7Fu;
    return exponent == 0 ? float(mantissa) / 512.0
                         : (1.0 + float(mantissa) / 128.0) * exp2(float(exponent) - 3.0);
}

// Color and 2-bit alpha of one 7e3 sample.
float4 Round7e3(float4 color)
{
    return float4(Round7e3(color.r), Round7e3(color.g), Round7e3(color.b),
                  round(saturate(color.a) * 3.0) / 3.0);
}

```

`src/gpu/shaders/fullscreen_vs.hlsl`:

```hlsl
// Fullscreen triangle: three vertices, no vertex buffer. Vulkan clip space
// (y = -1 at the top; internal shaders are compiled without -fvk-invert-y),
// texture coordinates (0, 0) at the top left.
void main(in uint vertexId : SV_VertexID, out float4 position : SV_Position, out float2 texCoord : TEXCOORD0)
{
    texCoord = float2((vertexId << 1) & 2, vertexId & 2);
    position = float4(texCoord * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
```

`src/gpu/shaders/present_ps.hlsl`:

```hlsl
// Scales the guest front buffer to the window (linear filtering), then
// applies the display's gamma table (UpdateGammaTable) as scan-out would.
// Push constants share the 24-byte range the game's shaders use for buffer
// addresses; internal shaders only use the first bytes.
struct PushConstants
{
    uint TextureIndex;
    uint SamplerIndex;
    uint GammaTableIndex;  // 256x1, 0 = none
};

[[vk::push_constant]] ConstantBuffer<PushConstants> g_PushConstants;

Texture2D<float4> g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[] : register(t0, space0);
SamplerState g_SamplerDescriptorHeap[] : register(s0, space3);

// The table maps 8-bit front buffer values; between entries (after the
// scaling filter), interpolate.
float ApplyGamma(Texture2D<float4> table, float value, uint channel)
{
    float position = value > 0.0 ? min(value, 1.0) * 255.0 : 0.0;  // NaN to 0
    int index = min(int(position), 254);
    float low = table.Load(int3(index, 0, 0))[channel];
    float high = table.Load(int3(index + 1, 0, 0))[channel];
    return lerp(low, high, position - float(index));
}

float4 main(in float4 position : SV_Position, in float2 texCoord : TEXCOORD0) : SV_Target
{
    Texture2D<float4> source = g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.TextureIndex];
    SamplerState samplerState = g_SamplerDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.SamplerIndex];
    // Larger than the window (a render scale above 1): average a grid of
    // bilinear taps over the pixel's footprint, up to 4x4, rather than one tap
    // that would skip texels.
    float2 size;
    source.GetDimensions(size.x, size.y);
    float2 footprint = float2(abs(ddx(texCoord.x)), abs(ddy(texCoord.y))) * size;
    uint2 taps = uint2(clamp(ceil(footprint / 2.0), 1.0, 4.0));
    float2 step = footprint / float2(taps) / size;
    float2 start = texCoord - step * (float2(taps) - 1.0) * 0.5;
    float4 color = 0.0;
    for (uint y = 0; y < taps.y; y++)
    {
        for (uint x = 0; x < taps.x; x++)
        {
            color += source.SampleLevel(samplerState, start + step * float2(x, y), 0);
        }
    }
    color /= float(taps.x * taps.y);
    if (g_PushConstants.GammaTableIndex != 0)
    {
        Texture2D<float4> table = g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.GammaTableIndex];
        color.r = ApplyGamma(table, color.r, 0);
        color.g = ApplyGamma(table, color.g, 1);
        color.b = ApplyGamma(table, color.b, 2);
    }
    return float4(color.rgb, 1.0);
}

```

`src/gpu/shaders/rect_list_gs.hlsl`:

```hlsl
// Xenos rectangle lists: each three vertices are three corners of a
// rectangle; the fourth is v1 + v2 - v0 for every output (as Xenia does).
//
// Translated vertex shaders write TEXCOORD0-7 (locations 0-7), COLOR0-1
// (8-9) and TEXCOORD8-15 (10-17); NG2's pixel shaders only read TEXCOORD0-7
// and COLOR0-1, and passing all 18 would exceed the 64 geometry input
// components some GPUs allow, so only those pass through.
struct Vertex
{
    float4 position : SV_Position;
    [[vk::location(0)]] float4 texCoord[8] : TEXCOORD0;
    [[vk::location(8)]] float4 color0 : COLOR0;
    [[vk::location(9)]] float4 color1 : COLOR1;
};

Vertex Fourth(Vertex corner, Vertex a, Vertex b)
{
    Vertex v;
    v.position = a.position + b.position - corner.position;
    [unroll] for (uint i = 0; i < 8; i++)
        v.texCoord[i] = a.texCoord[i] + b.texCoord[i] - corner.texCoord[i];
    v.color0 = a.color0 + b.color0 - corner.color0;
    v.color1 = a.color1 + b.color1 - corner.color1;
    return v;
}

[maxvertexcount(4)]
void main(triangle Vertex input[3], inout TriangleStream<Vertex> output)
{
    // The corner between the rectangle's two sides is the one opposite the
    // longest edge (the diagonal).
    float d01 = distance(input[0].position.xy / input[0].position.w, input[1].position.xy / input[1].position.w);
    float d02 = distance(input[0].position.xy / input[0].position.w, input[2].position.xy / input[2].position.w);
    float d12 = distance(input[1].position.xy / input[1].position.w, input[2].position.xy / input[2].position.w);
    uint corner = 0;
    if (d01 >= d02 && d01 >= d12)
        corner = 2;
    else if (d02 >= d01 && d02 >= d12)
        corner = 1;
    uint a = (corner + 1) % 3;
    uint b = (corner + 2) % 3;

    output.Append(input[a]);
    output.Append(input[corner]);
    output.Append(Fourth(input[corner], input[a], input[b]));
    output.Append(input[b]);
}

```

```hlsl
// A texture's color times a factor, texel for texel (the reduced bloom setting).
struct PushConstants
{

    float Factor;

[[vk::push_constant]] ConstantBuffer<PushConstants> g_PushConstants;

{
    float4 color = g_Texture2DDescriptorHeap[g_PushConstants.TextureIndex].Load(int3(position.xy, 0));
    return float4(color.rgb * g_PushConstants.Factor, color.a);
```

```cpp
// Descriptor slots 0-2 hold the blank 2D, 3D and cube textures.

  DESCRIPTOR_NULL_2D,
  DESCRIPTOR_NULL_3D,
  DESCRIPTOR_NULL_CUBE,
  DESCRIPTOR_FIRST_FREE,

// A host texture with the layout it was last transitioned to.
struct HostTexture {
  std::unique_ptr<RenderTexture> texture;
  RenderTextureLayout layout = RenderTextureLayout::UNKNOWN;
  RenderFormat format = RenderFormat::UNKNOWN;
  uint32_t width = 0;
  uint32_t height = 0;

  bool float7e3 = false;  // a color target last bound as 2_10_10_10_FLOAT

  bool prompts = false;   // the button atlas or its palette (prompts.cpp)
};

struct DescriptorAllocator {
  uint32_t next = DESCRIPTOR_FIRST_FREE;
  std::vector<uint32_t> freed;
  uint32_t Allocate() {
    if (!freed.empty()) {
      uint32_t index = freed.back();
      freed.pop_back();
      return index;
    }
    return next < TEXTURE_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT ? next++ : 0;
  }
  void Free(uint32_t index) {
    if (index >= DESCRIPTOR_FIRST_FREE) {
      freed.push_back(index);
    }
  }
};

// NG2_PROFILE=1: time spent per renderer stage, logged once a second.
// NG2_PROFILE=2 also times each draw on the GPU, logged by shader pair.
// wait: for the GPU (a frame's fence, the swapchain image), mostly inside the other stages.
enum class Stage { kDraw, kSync, kTexture, kPipeline, kResolve, kPresent, kWait, kCount };
constexpr const char* kStageNames[] = {"draw", "sync", "texture", "pipeline", "resolve",
                                       "present", "wait"};
struct Profile {
  bool enabled = [] {
    const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_PROFILE");
    return v && (v[0] == '1' || v[0] == '2');
  }();
  bool perDraw = [] {
    const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_PROFILE");
    return v && v[0] == '2';
  }();
  uint64_t nanoseconds[size_t(Stage::kCount)] = {};
  uint64_t comparedBytes = 0, uploadedBytes = 0, frames = 0;
  uint64_t textureLookups = 0, hashedBytes = 0, texturesMade = 0, textureMadeBytes = 0;
  // GPU time (timestamps): whole frames, their resolves and their present pass.
  uint64_t gpuNs = 0, gpuResolveNs = 0, gpuPresentNs = 0, gpuFrames = 0;
  uint64_t barriers = 0, passes = 0;  // recorded (the CPU's count), and passes started
  uint64_t prologueCopies = 0, inOrderCopies = 0;  // guest memory copies, by where they go
  // GPU time by render pass target ("1120x584 fmt 3 x2, 2 colors, depth"): from a
  // pass's start mark to the next mark.
  std::map<std::string, uint64_t> gpuPassNs;
  // With NG2_PROFILE=2, GPU time by shader pair (vertex, pixel): from a draw's
  // mark to the next mark, and the number of draws.
  std::map<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>, std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> gpuDrawNs;
  std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point last = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
} g_profile;

// With NG2_PROFILE=1: GPU timestamps in each frame's command list, read once
// its slot comes round again (its fence passed). Marks: the frame's start,
// each resolve's start and end, the present pass's start, the frame's end.
enum class GpuMark : uint8_t {
  kFrameStart, kResolveStart, kResolveEnd, kPresentStart, kFrameEnd, kPass, kDraw, kDrawEnd
};
uint32_t GpuMarkCapacity() {
  return g_profile.perDraw ? 8192 : 512;
}
struct GpuTiming {
  std::unique_ptr<RenderQueryPool> pool;
  uint32_t count = 0;  // marks written this frame
  std::vector<GpuMark> kinds;
  std::vector<std::string> passLabels;  // per kPass mark, in order
  std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> drawShaders;  // per kDraw mark, in order
};
GpuTiming g_gpuTiming[NUM_FRAMES];

// log_hitches (or NG2_HITCHES=1): a frame that took over 25 ms, and well
// over the one before, is logged with what the renderer spent its time on
// and what it had to make.
struct FrameStats {
  bool enabled = false;
  uint64_t nanoseconds[size_t(Stage::kCount)] = {};
  uint32_t pipelines = 0, shaders = 0, textures = 0;
  uint64_t pipelineNs = 0, shaderNs = 0, textureNs = 0, textureBytes = 0;
  std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point lastSwap;
  double lastMs = 0.0;
} g_frameStats;

bool Timing() {
  return g_profile.enabled || g_frameStats.enabled;
}

// The timers' clock: the CPU's time stamp counter where there is one (a
// clock_gettime is tens of ns, and the stages are timed thousands of times a
// frame), converted at a rate measured once against steady_clock.
uint64_t TimerTicks() {
#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
  return __rdtsc();
#else
  return uint64_t(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
                      std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
                      .count());
#endif
}
uint64_t TicksToNs(uint64_t ticks) {
#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
  static const double nsPerTick = [] {
    auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    uint64_t c0 = __rdtsc();
    while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0 < std::chrono::milliseconds(2)) {
    }
    auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    uint64_t c1 = __rdtsc();
    return double(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(t1 - t0).count()) /
           double(c1 - c0);
  }();
  return uint64_t(double(ticks) * nsPerTick);
#else
  return ticks;
#endif
}

// Times one thing made during the frame (a pipeline, shader or texture).
class MakeTimer {
 public:
  MakeTimer(uint32_t& count, uint64_t& ns) : count_(count), ns_(ns) {
    if (g_frameStats.enabled) {
      start_ = TimerTicks();
    }
  }
  ~MakeTimer() {
    if (g_frameStats.enabled) {
      count_++;
      ns_ += TicksToNs(TimerTicks() - start_);
    }
  }

 private:
  uint32_t& count_;
  uint64_t& ns_;
  uint64_t start_ = 0;
};

class StageTimer {
 public:
  explicit StageTimer(Stage stage) : stage_(stage) {
    if (Timing()) {
      start_ = TimerTicks();
    }
  }
  ~StageTimer() {
    if (Timing()) {
      uint64_t ns = TicksToNs(TimerTicks() - start_);
      if (g_profile.enabled) {
        g_profile.nanoseconds[size_t(stage_)] += ns;
      }
      g_frameStats.nanoseconds[size_t(stage_)] += ns;
    }
  }

 private:
  Stage stage_;
  uint64_t start_ = 0;
};

// NG2_PRESENT_GAPS=1: the time between presents, each second: the median,
// the shortest and longest, and how many were over 20 ms or under 13 ms (at
// 60 fps an even game presents every 16.7 ms; frame pacing shows up here).
void ReportPresentGaps(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point now) {
  static const bool enabled = [] {
    const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_PRESENT_GAPS");
    return v && v[0] == '1';
  }();
  if (!enabled) {
    return;
  }
  static std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point last, start;
  static std::vector<double> gaps;
  if (last != std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point()) {
    gaps.push_back(std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - last).count());
  } else {
    start = now;
  }
  last = now;
  if (now - start < std::chrono::seconds(1) || gaps.empty()) {
    return;
  }
  std::sort(gaps.begin(), gaps.end());
  size_t over = std::count_if(gaps.begin(), gaps.end(), [](double g) { return g > 20.0; });
  size_t under = std::count_if(gaps.begin(), gaps.end(), [](double g) { return g < 13.0; });
  REXLOG_INFO("video: present gaps ms: {} median {:.2f} min {:.2f} max {:.2f}, {} over 20, {} under 13",
              gaps.size(), gaps[gaps.size() / 2], gaps.front(), gaps.back(), over, under);
  gaps.clear();
  start = now;
}

void ReportHitch() {
  g_frameStats.enabled = REXCVAR_GET(log_hitches) || [] {
    const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_HITCHES");
    return v && v[0] == '1';
  }();
  auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto& f = g_frameStats;
  if (f.enabled && f.lastSwap != std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point()) {
    double ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - f.lastSwap).count();
    // Over 25 ms and well over the frame before (cutscenes run at 30 fps).
    if (ms > 25.0 && ms > 1.6 * f.lastMs) {
      // Sync, texture and pipeline time is spent inside draws.
      double renderer = (f.nanoseconds[size_t(Stage::kDraw)] +
                         f.nanoseconds[size_t(Stage::kResolve)] +
                         f.nanoseconds[size_t(Stage::kPresent)]) / 1e6;
      std::string stages;
      for (size_t i = 0; i < size_t(Stage::kCount); i++) {
        stages += fmt::format(" {} {:.1f}", kStageNames[i], f.nanoseconds[i] / 1e6);
      }
      REXLOG_INFO("video: hitch {:.1f} ms (renderer {:.1f}:{}); made {} pipelines {:.1f} ms, "
                  "{} shaders {:.1f} ms, {} textures {:.1f} ms {:.1f} MB",
                  ms, renderer, stages, f.pipelines, f.pipelineNs / 1e6, f.shaders,
                  f.shaderNs / 1e6, f.textures, f.textureNs / 1e6, f.textureBytes / 1048576.0);
    }
  }
  bool enabled = f.enabled;
  double lastMs = f.lastSwap != std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point()
                      ? std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - f.lastSwap).count()
                      : 0.0;
  f = FrameStats{};
  f.enabled = enabled;
  f.lastSwap = now;
  f.lastMs = lastMs;
}

// NG2_LATENCY_LOG=1: from the game starting a frame (it reads the pad then)
// to that frame's present call, averaged and worst over each second.
std::atomic<int64_t> g_frameStartNs{0};
void ReportLatency() {
  static const bool enabled = [] {
    const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_LATENCY_LOG");
    return v && v[0] == '1';
  }();
  int64_t start = g_frameStartNs.exchange(0);
  if (!enabled || !start) {
    return;
  }
  static double sum = 0.0, worst = 0.0;
  static uint32_t count = 0;
  static auto last = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  double ms = (now.time_since_epoch().count() - start) / 1e6;
  sum += ms, worst = std::max(worst, ms), count++;
  if (now - last >= std::chrono::seconds(1)) {
    REXLOG_INFO("latency frame start to present: avg {:.2f} ms, worst {:.2f} ms ({} frames)",
                sum / count, worst, count);
    sum = worst = 0.0, count = 0, last = now;
  }
}

// With NG2_PROFILE, every 5 s: the busiest threads' CPU time (ms of each
// second, from /proc; Linux only), so a slow machine's log tells which thread
// limits the frame rate. "(renderer)" is the game's render thread, which runs
// the renderer's hooks (the Vulkan side is on "Render Commands").
void ReportThreads() {
#if defined(__linux__)
  static std::unordered_map<int, uint64_t> last;
  static auto lastTime = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  static const int self = int(gettid());
  auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  double seconds = std::chrono::duration<double>(now - lastTime).count();
  if (seconds < 5.0) {
    return;
  }
  lastTime = now;
  static const double msPerTick = 1000.0 / double(sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK));
  std::vector<std::pair<double, std::string>> busy;
  std::unordered_map<int, uint64_t> current;
  std::error_code error;
  for (const auto& entry : std::filesystem::directory_iterator("/proc/self/task", error)) {
    int tid = std::atoi(entry.path().filename().c_str());
    FILE* f = std::fopen((entry.path() / "stat").c_str(), "r");
    if (!f) {
      continue;
    }
    char text[512] = {};
    size_t n = std::fread(text, 1, sizeof(text) - 1, f);
    std::fclose(f);
    text[n] = 0;
    const char* open = std::strchr(text, '(');
    const char* close = std::strrchr(text, ')');
    if (!open || !close) {
      continue;
    }
    // After the name: state (field 3) ... utime (14), stime (15).
    unsigned long long utime = 0, stime = 0;
    if (std::sscanf(close + 2, "%*c %*d %*d %*d %*d %*d %*u %*u %*u %*u %*u %llu %llu", &utime,
                    &stime) != 2) {
      continue;
    }
    uint64_t ticks = utime + stime;
    current[tid] = ticks;
    auto it = last.find(tid);
    if (it == last.end() || ticks < it->second) {  // new, or a reused thread id
      continue;
    }
    double ms = double(ticks - it->second) * msPerTick / seconds;
    if (ms >= 10.0) {
      std::string name(open + 1, close);
      busy.emplace_back(ms, tid == self ? name + " (renderer)" : name);
    }
  }
  last = std::move(current);
  std::sort(busy.begin(), busy.end(), std::greater<>());
  std::string line;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < busy.size() && i < 8; i++) {
    line += fmt::format("{}{} {:.0f}", i ? ", " : " ", busy[i].second, busy[i].first);
  }
  if (!line.empty()) {
    REXLOG_INFO("threads, ms of CPU each second:{}", line);
  }
#endif
}

void ReportProfile() {
  ReportHitch();
  if (g_profile.enabled) {
    ReportThreads();
  }
  g_profile.frames++;
  auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  if (!g_profile.enabled || now - g_profile.last < std::chrono::seconds(1)) {
    return;
  }
  std::string line;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < size_t(Stage::kCount); i++) {
    line += fmt::format(" {} {:.1f}", kStageNames[i], g_profile.nanoseconds[i] / 1e6);
  }
  REXLOG_INFO("video: {} frames, ms:{}; compared {:.1f} MB, uploaded {:.1f} MB; textures {} "
              "looked up, {:.1f} MB hashed, {} made {:.1f} MB",
              g_profile.frames, line, g_profile.comparedBytes / 1048576.0,
              g_profile.uploadedBytes / 1048576.0, g_profile.textureLookups,
              g_profile.hashedBytes / 1048576.0, g_profile.texturesMade,
              g_profile.textureMadeBytes / 1048576.0);
  if (g_profile.gpuFrames) {
    double frames = double(g_profile.gpuFrames);
    REXLOG_INFO("video: GPU {:.2f} ms a frame: resolves {:.2f}, present {:.2f} ({} frames timed); "
                "{:.0f} passes, {:.0f} barriers a frame",
                g_profile.gpuNs / 1e6 / frames, g_profile.gpuResolveNs / 1e6 / frames,
                g_profile.gpuPresentNs / 1e6 / frames, g_profile.gpuFrames,
                g_profile.passes / double(std::max<uint64_t>(g_profile.frames, 1)),
                g_profile.barriers / double(std::max<uint64_t>(g_profile.frames, 1)));
    REXLOG_INFO("video: guest memory copies a frame: {:.1f} in the prologue, {:.1f} in order",
                g_profile.prologueCopies / double(std::max<uint64_t>(g_profile.frames, 1)),
                g_profile.inOrderCopies / double(std::max<uint64_t>(g_profile.frames, 1)));
    std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, std::string>> passes;
    for (auto& [label, ns] : g_profile.gpuPassNs) {
      passes.emplace_back(ns, label);
    }
    std::sort(passes.rbegin(), passes.rend());
    std::string top;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < passes.size() && i < 6; i++) {
      top += fmt::format("{}{} {:.2f}", i ? "; " : "", passes[i].second, passes[i].first / 1e6 / frames);
    }
    REXLOG_INFO("video: GPU ms a frame by pass target: {}", top);
    if (!g_profile.gpuDrawNs.empty()) {
      std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>>> pairs;
      for (auto& [shaders, timed] : g_profile.gpuDrawNs) {
        pairs.emplace_back(timed.first, shaders);
      }
      std::sort(pairs.rbegin(), pairs.rend());
      std::string draws;
      // (NG2_PROFILE_TOP=<n>: that many pairs instead of 8)
      static const size_t top = [] {
        const char* v = std::getenv("NG2_PROFILE_TOP");
        return v ? size_t(std::max(1, std::atoi(v))) : size_t(8);
      }();
      for (size_t i = 0; i < pairs.size() && i < top; i++) {
        auto [vs, ps] = pairs[i].second;
        draws += fmt::format("{}vs {:016X} ps {:016X} {:.2f} ({:.0f} draws)", i ? "; " : "", vs, ps,
                             pairs[i].first / 1e6 / frames,
                             g_profile.gpuDrawNs[pairs[i].second].second / frames);
      }
      REXLOG_INFO("video: GPU ms a frame by shaders: {}", draws);
    }
  }
  g_profile = Profile{};
  g_profile.last = now;
}

// Guest physical memory as the GPU sees it (512 MB): vertex data read by the
// shaders and memory export targets, addressed like the console.
constexpr uint64_t GUEST_MEMORY_SIZE = 512ull << 20;
std::unique_ptr<RenderBuffer> g_guestMemory;
uint64_t g_guestMemoryAddress = 0;
// What g_guestMemory holds, byte for byte, as of the uploads recorded so far
// (calloc: untouched pages cost nothing). Ranges compare the guest's memory
// with it rather than with their own last contents: draws with different
// ranges over the same memory (a ring buffer reused with other sizes)
// overwrite each other's uploads.
uint8_t* g_guestMemoryShadow = nullptr;

// Ranges synced: the frame they were last checked in and the frame they last
// changed in. A range that hasn't changed for a frame is checked once a
// frame; one that has (a dynamic buffer the game fills in batches, which no
// GPU ever stalls here) is checked on every draw, and so is one caught
// written between its draws (dynamic) until it stays unchanged for 8 frames.
//
// Some buffers are written after the draw that reads them: the game's jobs
// fill bone matrices while the render thread goes on, since the console's
// GPU reads them only after the frame is kicked off. A range found changed
// at the end of a frame it was drawn in becomes late: its copy is still
// recorded at its first draw in a frame, but filled from guest memory just
// before the frame is submitted.
//
// Bone palettes (fetch slot 94) are late from their first draw: they rotate
// through three buffers, and a buffer the jobs fill only after the frame's
```
